records.title: Director of Integrated Fab Manufacturing
records.description:
**Bold Thinking. World Changing.**
At SkyWater, our ingenuity helps improve lives around the world by manufacturing U.S. made semiconductors that are essential ingredients of modern life. Automotive safety enhancements, life-saving medical devices, consumer electronics and American security require semiconductors. Working in our Minnesota headquarters, Florida, or Texas location — employees join together to improve the world.
 
 
**Explore what’s possible.**
Joining our U.S. - based team means contributing to and learning about the commercialization of some of the most exciting technologies the world has ever seen. We are turning “science fiction” into everyday reality through technologies such as superconducting, 3D integrated circuits or computer chips, carbon nanotubes, photonic logic devices, micro electro-mechanical systems and other emerging device topologies. We manufacture products for aerospace and defense, medical, automotive, consumer and industrial markets, to name a few. Our customers include emerging leaders who rely on our intellectual property security and quality manufacturing services.
 
 
**Step into the future.**
SkyWater’s values of Integrity, Excellence, Collaboration, Empowerment and Growth Mindset guide us to cultivate an empowered, learning environment. We also invest in developing highly skilled, dedicated employees — and employees who are entering the workforce for the first time, from the military, and a variety of educational backgrounds.
 
 
**Are you bold thinking?**
Find your place on our team and help us change the world!
 
 
**Primary Objective**
Join an innovative semiconductor manufacturing organization at the forefront of advanced technology and manufacturing excellence. The Director of Integrated Fab Manufacturing owns the operational, financial, and strategic leadership of the Bloomington fabrication facility, including the Advanced Technology Services (ATS) Process Engineering Technician team. This role ensures the factory achieves world-class safety, quality, output, cycle time, and cost performance while directing a 24/7 organization and partnering across engineering, planning, and quality teams to meet all customer and business commitments.
 
 
In this role, you will be responsible for the end-to-end operational execution, strategic planning, budgetary ownership, and leadership to ensure safe, reliable, and efficient semiconductor manufacturing. You will be responsible for driving absolute excellence across safety, quality, output, cost optimization, and ensuring smooth production flow to consistently meet internal and external customer quality and on-time delivery (OTD) commitments, and fab velocity metrics / key performance indicators (KPIs).
 
 
The successful candidate will own the organizational design and talent strategy for their organization, serving as a role model and lead a highly matrixed organization consisting of the Manufacturing team, Process Engineering Technicians group, and Flow Engineers. This role is expected to partner closely with Program Managers, Technical Leads, Wafer Planning, Manufacturing, Equipment Engineering, Quality, and Technology Development teams to improve operational performance, resolve manufacturing constraints, and deliver business objectives. This leader will play a critical role in transforming factory capabilities to meet strict customer commitments and flexible demand by influencing long-range capacity and setting standards for the MN fab operations organization.
 
 
**Major Areas Of Accountability**

* Operations Leadership: Lead the daily and long-term operational execution in the fab, as well as the ATS technician and flow engineer teams to meet all production starts, output targets, yield expectations, cycle time goals, and quality standards, including setting clear priorities for the organization. Direct, develop, and coach the 24/7 operations teams—including Production, ATS Process Engineering Technicians, and Flow Engineers—to ensure capability, accountability, and organizational readiness.
* Team Leadership: Lead, develop, and empower the Production team, Process Engineering Technicians and Flow Engineers to provide effective manufacturing support, maintain production continuity, and resolve process and workflow issues
* Budgetary Responsibility: Own the fab operating budget, including labor, materials, maintenance, and operational spending; drive cost-reduction initiatives and evaluate capital investments using ROI-based decision-making.
* Wafer Planning and Customer Delivery: Partner with Wafer Planning and Program Management to align schedules, capacity, and customer priorities; identify delivery risks and oversee recovery plans to maintain on time delivery (OTD) performance.
* Manufacturing Performance: Partner with Industrial Engineers, and drive continuous improvement in throughput, cycle time, WIP management, yield, quality, equipment availability, and manufacturing cost using data-driven decision-making and structured problem-solving.
* Cross-Functional Collaboration: Coordinate with Manufacturing, Process Engineering, Equipment Engineering, Quality, and Technology Development to resolve production constraints, improve equipment readiness, and maintain stable manufacturing operations.
* Operational Excellence: Establish and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs), including customer OTD, cycle time, throughput, equipment availability, and quality. Promote standardization, disciplined execution, effective escalation, and continuous improvement.
* Talent Development: Build a high-performing organization through coaching, accountability, collaboration, and development of technical and operational talent. Responsible for the organizational design and talent strategy of these teams, with a focus on cultivating and retaining key talent, developing future leaders and preparing current leaders for the next level role.

**Required Qualifications**- Education: Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Materials Science, Physics, or related technical discipline.
- Experience: Minimum 12 years in semiconductor manufacturing or operations; minimum 5+ years leading fab operations in a senior manager or director capacity within a 24/7 manufacturing environment.
- Skills:

* Demonstrated ability to improve manufacturing performance (throughput, cycle time, yield, cost, and customer delivery).
* Expertise in wafer planning, WIP management, or production scheduling.
* Strong capability in statistical process control (SPC), structured problem-solving, and data-driven decision-making.
* Demonstrated leadership with large technical teams, with an ability to communicate and collaborate cross-functionally, delivering results in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.
* Proven track record of managing a 24/7 manufacturing organization and guiding cross-functional teams through technical tool or yield crises.
* Citizenship: US Citizen required.

**Physical Requirements**

* Ability to enter the cleanroom in full PPE to provide technical and operational support.
* Ability to navigate multi-level fab environments, including prolonged walking and standing when needed.

*The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job.*
**Preferred Qualifications**

* Education: Master’s or PhD in a relevant technical discipline.
* Experience: Deep knowledge of advanced Complimentary Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor (CMOS) nodes, fab toolsets (Lithography, Etch, Diffusion, Thin Films, Chemical Mechanical Polish, Metrology, Metals), and factory automation systems.
* Skills: Experience driving major manufacturing transformations, automation or digitization initiatives, or large-scale capacity improvements.

records.title: Director of Manufacturing
records.description:
**About Us:**
Alliance Machine Systems International, LLC is a privately held company with over 35 years of history dedicated to providing corrugated box manufacturing machines and services to the changing industry. As the paperboard packaging industry's premier global supplier of productivity-enhancing process machinery and systems, we supply innovative designs, intelligent automation, and optimized workflow, coupled with highly responsive parts and service support. Our United States and Europe based engineering, manufacturing, sales and service operations provide a global support system covering the full product portfolio of Alliance, Serco, TEI, ASC, Pallmac, J&L and Tanabe machines.
 
 
Barry-Wehmiller is a diversified global supplier of engineering consulting and manufacturing technology for the packaging, corrugating, sheeting and paper-converting industries. By blending people-centric leadership with disciplined operational strategies and purpose-driven growth, Barry-Wehmiller has become a $3 billion organization with nearly 12,000 team members united by a common belief: to use the power of business to build a better world.
 
 
**Job Description:**
***THIS IS AN ONSITE ROLE LOCATED IN SPOKANE, WASHINGTON.***
**Job Overview:**
Alliance Machine Systems Int is seeking a Director of Manufacturing to lead manufacturing performance and operational scale across its North American production sites.
 
 
This is a considerable leadership role for an experienced manufacturing leader who understands the complexity of producing industrial automation equipment and engineered systems.
 
 
The Director of Manufacturing will be responsible for improving the connection between engineering, production, quality, supply chain, and customer delivery.
 
 
The successful candidate will lead a manufacturing environment where products may include complex electrical, mechanical, robotic and controls. The role will involve managing high-mix production, engineered-to-order or configure-to-order manufacturing, and the delivery of technically sophisticated equipment to major industrial customers.
 
 
**Key Responsibilities:**

* Lead manufacturing operations across the company’s production facilities.
* Set standards for safety, quality, on-time delivery, productivity, and cost.
* Improve the transfer of products and projects from engineering into manufacturing.
* Increase capacity while maintaining quality, delivery, and customer performance.
* Improve on-time delivery, lead times, throughput, and gross margin.
* Strengthen production planning, scheduling, capacity planning, and work-in-progress control.
* Manage critical components, suppliers, and long-lead materials with procurement and supply chain teams.
* Establish scalable processes for complex, high-mix, engineered-to-order automation products and systems.
* Support new product introduction and design-for-manufacture initiatives.
* Improve collaboration across sales, engineering, project management, procurement, and manufacturing.
* Lead recovery plans for delayed or strategically important projects.
* Establish clear manufacturing and performance-management KPIs.
* Develop plant managers, production managers, and operational teams.
* Support facility expansion, automation investment, capital planning, and potential upcoming new-site development.
* Partner with the executive team on manufacturing strategy, capacity, organizational design, and long-term growth.

**Requirements:**

* 12+ years’ experience in manufacturing, operations, or plant leadership within an industrial manufacturing environment.
* At least 7 years in manufacturing leadership, with direct responsibility for manufacturing performance.
* Experience within industrial automation, robotics, machinery, electrical equipment, motion control, or engineered capital equipment manufacturing.
* Direct leadership of manufacturing operations, rather than engineering or project delivery alone.
* Experience with complex, high-mix, engineered-to-order, configure-to-order, or project-based production.
* A proven record of improving delivery, quality, productivity, capacity, cost, and gross margin.
* Experience leading cross-functional teams across production, quality, planning, and supply chain.
* Strong understanding of the transition from engineering and product design into manufacturing.
* Experience leading managers and developing scalable operational structures.
* Working knowledge of ERP, MRP, production planning, scheduling, and manufacturing-performance systems.
* Strong communication and stakeholder-management skills across engineering, sales, project management, supply chain, service, and executive leadership.
* Willingness to travel to US manufacturing sites, suppliers, and customers as required.

Compensation: $150,000-180,000 base salary
 
 
Benefits: Alliance offers a competitive benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, life insurance, disability insurance, 401K with employer match, PTO, paid holidays and a bonus program.
 
 
*At Barry-Wehmiller we recognize that people come with a wealth of experience and talent beyond just the technical requirements of a job. If your experience is close to what you see listed here, please still consider applying. We know that our differences often can bring about innovation, excellence and meaningful work—therefore, people from all backgrounds are encouraged to apply to our positions. Please let us know if you require reasonable accommodations during the interview process.*
Barry-Wehmiller is an equal opportunity employer. M/F/D/V This organization uses E-Verify.
 
 
Applicants may be subject to pre-employment screening which may include drug screening, reference checks, employment verifications, background screening and/or skills assessments.
 
 
**Company:**
Alliance

**Director of Manufacturing (Rubber)**

The Director of Manufacturing will oversee rubber production operations across 2 manufacturing plants with 200 total employees, 100 employees per plant, 1 union plant & 1 non-union, 5-8 Direct Reports (Department Managers) with responsibility for safety, quality, delivery, and cost, acting as leader with accountability for both operations.

**Location**
: Columbia, Missouri (Relocation Assistance Offered)

**Compensation**
: $175,000 - $215,000 base salary + 15% bonus.

**Benefits**
: Medical, Dental, Vision, STD, LTD, 401k Match 6%, 3 weeks PTO, Tuition Assistance, etc.

**Job Description:**

*Operational Leadership & Plant Management*

* Hold full P&L, safety, quality, delivery, and cost accountability for both rubber manufacturing plants across textile & milling operations including mixing and cord production, acting as a multi-site operations leader.
* Lead, develop, and hold accountable a team of 6-8 managers who in turn lead roughly 200 salaried and hourly employees across multiple shifts.
* Develop and execute annual operating plans, capital plans, and budgets; manage conversion cost, yield, scrap, rework, material variance, and overhead against targets.
* Balance production schedules and capacity across both sites to meet downstream Belt and Hose demand, optimizing changeovers, inventory, and material availability.
* Partner with the VP of Manufacturing, plant managers of downstream operations, supply chain, and commercial teams on demand planning, capacity strategy, and make-versus-buy decisions.
* Spend meaningful time on the floor at each site (approximately 30% travel), maintaining a visible presence on all shifts and engaging directly with operators and supervisors.

*Compound Quality, Technology & Process Control*

* Own end-to-end compound consistency, using rheology (Mooney, MDR/RPA), physical properties, and downstream processing and molding results as the measures of success.
* Reduce process variation through structured methods such as design of experiments (DOE), statistical process control, capability studies, and root cause analysis.
* Develop, standardize, and improve mixing programs (load order, ram pressure, rotor speed, mix time, dump temperature, energy-based and multi-stage mixing) for new and existing compounds, including EPDM, CR, HNBR, NBR, SBR, and NR systems.
* Oversee textile operations (cord unwinding, coating, and rewinding) and raw material handling, heating, and cooling to ensure consistent adhesion and reinforcement performance in finished belts and hoses.
* Lead cross-functional troubleshooting with chemists, the materials lab, process and manufacturing engineers, and downstream operations, leading investigations through disciplined experimentation.
* Establish a single, controlled system of work instructions, batch cards, and process parameters across both sites so that the same compound is produced the same way regardless of site, shift, or operator.
* Evaluate and recommend mixing equipment, automation, weighing/batching, and tooling options for current and new processes and products.

Mill: raw materials are received and handled, then weighed, mixed, heated, and cooled to produce uniform rubber compound for downstream product production.

Textiles: cord is carefully unwound, coated, and rewound to specification, giving finished products consistent strength and adhesion.

*Safety, Compliance & Culture*

* Champion a zero-harm safety culture, including lockout/tagout, machine guarding, mill nip and pinch-point hazards, hot surfaces, combustible dust, and chemical handling.
* Ensure compliance with OSHA, EPA, environmental permitting, SDS requirements, and applicable customer, ISO/IATF, and corporate standards.
* Drive 5S, standardized work, and lean manufacturing practices; treat housekeeping as both a safety and a quality requirement.
* Build a culture of accountability in which following the documented process is the standard and deviations are surfaced openly.

*Talent Development & Organizational Capability*

* Build a bench of operators, leads, supervisors, and managers through structured training, skills matrices, cross-training, and succession planning.
* Set clear expectations, conduct performance reviews, and partner with HR on coaching, corrective action, recognition, and labor relations.
* Capture experienced operators' tribal knowledge and convert it to documented, teachable standards.
* Attract, hire, and retain top technical and operational talent in a competitive labor market.

*Strategy & Continuous Improvement*

* Work with the plant leadership and engineering leadership to define annual improvement initiatives, then align cross-functional teams to targets and track results.
* Lead capital projects, technology transfers, and new-process launches from concept through ramp-up.
* Use KPIs, trend charts, and daily management routines to drive visibility, problem solving, and sustained results.
* Contribute to the North American and global compounding strategy, sharing best practices with sister sites and corporate technology teams.

*Key Performance Indicators*

* Safety: recordable incident rate, near-miss reporting, and audit results
* Compound first-pass quality and out-of-spec rate; rheology capability and variation reduction
* Downstream molding and processing results attributable to compound and cord
* Schedule attainment and on-time delivery to downstream operations
* Scrap, rework, yield, and material and conversion cost versus budget
* Equipment uptime and overall equipment effectiveness (OEE)
* Operator qualification coverage and cross-training depth
* Employee engagement, turnover, and leadership bench strength

**Qualifications Seeking:**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering (Chemical, Polymer, Mechanical, Materials, or Industrial), Chemistry, or a related technical field preferred. Experience in lieu of Bachelors will be considered.
* 8+ years of manufacturing experience, including 5–10 years of hands-on polymer or rubber compounding and mixing experience.
* 5+ years of progressive leadership experience managing managers and multi-shift operations, including responsibility for safety, quality, cost, and delivery.
* Strong working knowledge of internal mixers (tangential and intermeshing), two-roll mills, TSE, weigh-up/batching, and compound testing (Mooney, MDR/RPA, specific gravity, dispersion).
* Demonstrated experience reducing process variation using DOE, SPC, and structured problem-solving methods.
* Proven ability to lead cross-functional troubleshooting with chemists, lab, engineering, and production teams.
* Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills, direct without being abrasive.
* Willingness and ability to travel approximately 30% between sites and to work on the floor in a manufacturing environment.

**Preferred Qualifications (Not Required):**

* Master's degree in Polymer Science, Chemistry, or Engineering, or an MBA.
* Experience in belt, hose, or other engineered rubber product manufacturing, with understanding of rheology and downstream extrusion, calendering, and molding.
* Experience with cord treatment, textile reinforcement, or adhesive systems.
* Experience managing multi-site operations and leading change across sites.
* Lean Six Sigma Black Belt or Green Belt certification, or equivalent.
* Familiarity with ERP/MES systems, mixing control software, and automation for production and material traceability.
* Experience leading capital projects, new-equipment commissioning, or greenfield/expansion launches.

**Core Competencies Seeking:**

* Technical depth: credible expert in rubber chemistry, rheology, and mixing who can coach engineers and operators alike.
* Leadership: develops managers, builds accountability, and engages a unionized or non-union frontline workforce.
* Systems thinking: standardizes work and builds sustainable processes rather than relying on individual heroics.
* Analytical rigor: makes decisions with data, experimentation, and clear trend visibility.
* Business acumen: manages cost, capital, and capacity with a P&L mindset.
* Learning agility: quickly learns new technologies and applies them to business needs.

records.title: Director of Operations
records.description:
**Position Summary**
The Director of Operations is responsible for leading Hughes-Treitler operations to achieve business objectives related to safety, quality, delivery, cost, productivity, and customer satisfaction. This hands-on leadership role provides strategic and day-to-day direction for manufacturing, materials, and operational excellence while ensuring the organization has the talent, capacity, processes, and resources required to support current demand and business growth. The Director establishes operating plans, drives accountability, builds organizational capability, and leads continuous improvement initiatives that improve performance, expand capacity, control costs, and strengthen customer responsiveness.
 
 
**Supervisory Responsibilties**

* The position has direct reports but must be able to work in partnership with Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain and Production in support of the departmental objectives.

**Duties And Responsibilities**

* Lead and develop Operations teams to effectively support day-to-day execution, strategic business objectives, customer requirements, and growth plans.
* Establish operating strategies, objectives, budgets, capital requirements, material plans, labor requirements, and organizational priorities aligned with customer and business needs.
* Ensure the organization is structured and staffed with the talent, resources, and capabilities needed to meet customer quality, technical, delivery, and turnaround-time expectations.
* Partner with business leadership to achieve key performance indicators, including safety, quality, on-time delivery, throughput, backlog reduction, customer lead time, productivity, labor utilization, cost, and profitability.
* Lead the development and execution of the site Lean and Operational Excellence roadmap, using Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, 5S, TPM, SIOP and daily management practices to improve flow, yield, cycle time, productivity, and cost performance.
* Establish and monitor operating standards, performance metrics, and management routines that drive accountability, timely problem-solving, and sustained results.
* Drive capacity planning and expansion initiatives, including capital equipment, automation, facility, tooling, staffing, and process investments required to support business growth.
* Manage operating expenses and capital investments in accordance with approved budgets; identify and execute cost-reduction and productivity opportunities.
* Ensure effective planning and control of materials, inventory, suppliers, production schedules, and labor resources to support quality, cost, and delivery commitments.
* Collaborate with Quality, Engineering, Sales, Finance, and other cross-functional partners to resolve operational issues, support new product introductions, strengthen manufacturability, and meet customer requirements.
* Provide leadership for robust root cause analysis, corrective actions, and continuous improvement activities related to safety, quality, delivery, cost, and customer performance.
* Participate in the development and execution of the business strategy and translate strategic priorities into actionable operating plans and measurable objectives.
* Support commercial and customer-facing activities, including operational reviews, pricing and capacity analyses, customer visits, and performance presentations.
* Recruit, develop, coach, and retain operations talent through performance management, career development, succession planning, cross-training, and ongoing capability building.
* Foster a culture of accountability, employee engagement, collaboration, innovation, safety, and continuous improvement across the organization.
* Author annual performance reviews and develop continuing education and advancement paths for entire department.
* Demonstrate the ability and willingness to use AI tools appropriately to improve productivity, decision-making, work quality, and cost performance, including identifying suitable use cases and critically evaluating AI-generated outputs.

**Required Skills And Abilities**

* Strong leadership, project management, analytical, problem-solving, and cross-functional collaboration skills.
* Demonstrated success leading manufacturing operations and continuous improvement initiatives in a complex manufacturing environment.
* Proficiency with Lean, Six Sigma, 5S, Kaizen, TPM, and other continuous improvement methodologies.
* Ability to establish performance metrics, analyze operating data, prioritize competing demands, and drive accountability for results.
* Proven ability to lead change, manage multiple complex initiatives, and meet critical deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
* Exceptional interpersonal, written, verbal, and presentation skills, with the ability to build effective work relationships.
* Strong customer orientation and demonstrated ability to balance customer requirements with operational, financial, and organizational priorities.
* Ability to work effectively under pressure, exercise sound judgment, and maintain a hands-on leadership presence across the operation.
* Proficiency with enterprise resource planning and manufacturing systems; experience with SIOP or related planning processes preferred.
* Demonstrated history of successful change management and implementation of operational excellence improvements.
* Strong interpersonal, leadership and organizational skills and the ability to communicate with all levels of the organization from the production floor to the executive office.
* Willingness to work a flexible schedule and travel as needed to support business requirements.

**Education And Experience**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Supply Chain, Business, or another related technical discipline required; MBA or other relevant advanced degree preferred.
* Minimum of 10 years of progressive manufacturing operations leadership experience in a low-volume/high-mix, build-to-order, or engineered-products environment; experience in aerospace, defense, metal-forming, precision machining, brazing, welding, or another highly regulated industry preferred.
* Demonstrated experience leading salaried and hourly employees.
* Demonstrated experience leading Lean Manufacturing, Operational Excellence, and continuous improvement programs with measurable results.
* Demonstrated experience driving operational planning, capital and capacity expansion, production and materials management, cost optimization, organizational improvements, and customer-facing operational reviews.

**Other**

* Due to the nature of Hughes-Treitler's programs and products, applicants must have the legal right to work in the US and additionally must be legally authorized to access export-controlled information and source code.

**Compensation**
Employee Type: Salaried
 
 
Currency: USD
 
 
Salary Minimum: 200,000
 
 
Salary Maximum: 225,000
 
 
Incentive: No

records.description:
**Job Description**
**Director Operations for Drug Product**
Do you aspire to secure a critical role in the production of biologics-based medicines? Are you excited to lead dynamic teams in a state-of-the-art facility that brings transformative biotech treatments to patients globally? We invite you to become a part of our journey as the Director Operations for Drug Product. This role offers you the chance to contribute to the site's development and wield technical leadership to ensure successful GMP manufacturing.
 
 
**Principle Roles & Responsibilities / Accountabilities**

* The Director, Operations – Drug Product plays a critical part in strategic project realization of the Wilmington Biotech facility, a new hi-potent facility in our company's Biologic manufacturing network, ensuring that site’s mission and objectives are effectively achieved, consistent with our company's requirements to ensure compliance, safety and reliable supply to our customers.
* As a key member of the Site Leadership Team, you'll have the opportunity to shape site and organizational strategies, overseeing drug product manufacturing for commercial and new product introductions.
* Be part of facility start-up to manufacture high-potent products, eg antibody drug conjugates (ADCs)
* You will work collaboratively with cross-functional teams to streamline technology transfers and commercial approvals, meanwhile nurturing and empowering your operations team.
* You'll get to foster a culture of continuous learning and improvement, leading or supporting various site functional and cross-functional structures for departmental alignment.
* Tackling resource constraints and needs, you will champion operational and technical excellence for efficient production and implement Lean principles for process optimization.
* Upholding our Manufacturing Division Quality Management System (QMS) requirements, you will manage relevant quality topics, and ensure permanent inspection readiness.
* You will oversee financial forecasts and workload for departmental cost improvements, aligning with capital and expense targets while contributing to sustainability and cost reduction initiatives.
* You will have the chance to leverage digital tools for operational efficiency and informed decision-making, keeping pace with emerging digital technologies relevant to manufacturing processes.
* You will be accountable for achieving onsite Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), monitoring and striving to improve performance metrics related to hiring, uptime, training, change controls, investigations, CAPAs, yield, volume, production cadence, operational availability, and more.

**Qualification And Experience**
**Required Experience and Skills:**

* A degree or equivalent in Engineering, Science, Technical, or other relevant fields: Bachelor’s degree + 12 years industry experience Or Masters + 10 years Or PhD + 8 years
* 6 or more years demonstrated leadership ability and experience managing, coaching, and mentoring high-performing cross function teams.
* Demonstrated experience in a biotech/vaccines/pharma manufacturing site, project, or other relevant roles, specifically drug product sterile manufacturing.
* Demonstrated experience in manufacturing clinical and commercial products.
* Understanding of cGMP requirements for commercial high-potent ADC manufacturing of drug product

**Preferred Experience And Skills**

* Sterile manufacturing leadership & operations, with preferred multi-product experience.
* A leader who inspires, coaches, and fosters a high-performance organizational culture.
* A continuous learner who cultivates a culture of ongoing development within your team.
* An innovative thinker with excellent decision-making and problem-solving skills.
* Experienced in leading highly effective cross-functional teams with a passion for shaping the future of our organization.
* Capable of influencing and building relationships across organizational layers, as well as externally with partners.

#ADC #ADC2026
 
 
**Required Skills**
Adaptability, Adaptability, Business Agility, Continuous Development, Cross-Functional Project Management, Customer Delivery, Data Analysis, Decision Making, Lean Manufacturing, Manufacturing, Manufacturing Quality Control, Manufacturing Technologies, Operations Management, Organizational Leadership, People Leadership, Performance Metrics, Process Improvements, Process Optimization, Product Compliance, Production Scheduling, Quality Compliance, Quality Control Management, Quality Control Systems, Quality Management, Regulatory Compliance {+ 7 more}

records.title: Plant Director
records.description:
**At The Cheesecake Factory Bakery, We Don't Do Ordinary!**
Nothing is scaled down. Not the pride, not the fun, and definitely not the teamwork. Here, you'll lead great people, drive meaningful impact, and help shape the future of our business while supporting the bakery and restaurant teams behind the iconic cheesecakes our guests enjoy every day. That's the kind of culture that has earned us a place on Fortune's 100 Best Companies to Work For® list every year since 2014.

**The Plant Director**
provides strategic and operational leadership for a three-shift, seven-day manufacturing facility encompassing approximately 160 full-time, non-union employees. Leading all aspects of production and packaging operations, you will drive performance, efficiency, quality, and continuous improvement across scheduling, logistics, pre-scaling, mixing, depositing, baking, decorating, and packaging to support the Bakery's operational and business objectives.

They utilize excellent leadership, analytical, management, and technical skills, abilities, and behaviors to drive performance in key areas such as people, safety, quality, service, and cost, aligned with measurable objectives and the Company’s Mission, Vision, and Values. The Director also assists with business continuity in the absence of the VP of Operations.

**You’ll thrive in this position if you are:**

* **Service oriented:**
 you are a people person who is systematic and trustworthy and interacts constructively with peers or teams of various levels demonstrating strong, positive communication skills.
* **Driven by results:**
 you are conscientious and persistent about delivering timely, high-quality deliverables, and performing all job functions safely while following instructions.
* **Improvement focused:**
 you never turn off the thought “how can I do this better/faster”.
* **Pressure resistant:**
 you have ice in your veins while under pressure. Maintaining a positive outlook at work while the heat is on is never an issue for you.

**Here’s more of what you’ll get to do:**

* Maintain positive employee relations through respectful, open, and effective two-way communication at the individual and team levels.
* Partner with human resources and training departments to develop, implement, and maintain effective training and development programs that support performance goals and provide a satisfying work environment.
* Maintain a fair and professional work environment that balances business objectives with quality-of-work-life factors for employees.
* Work with Human Resources to ensure compliance with all applicable laws, regulations, and company policies, while driving improvements in employee performance as measured by turnover rate, attendance, and feedback mechanisms.
* Oversee production planning and scheduling to optimize service and efficiency, balancing resources such as crewing, materials, and equipment with other department managers.
* Supervise the development of synchronized crewing, equipment setup, and materials preparation plans to ensure schedule attainment and optimize capacity utilization.
* Manage timekeeping, labor efficiency, and plant productivity in compliance with legal and company policies, aiming to minimize overtime and control non-productive line time.
* Collaborate with the Plant Engineer to ensure preventive and emergency maintenance efforts are effective, minimizing downtime and optimizing machine performance.
* Manage material usage to ensure minimal waste and maximum yield, while maintaining strict adherence to product quality standards and inventory management.
* Monitor spending and manage operations within approved budget levels, while driving improvements in cost performance through labor productivity, waste reduction, and yield maximization.
* Ensure disciplined compliance with product and process quality standards, food safety, and regulatory requirements, striving for “EXCELLENT” or “SUPERIOR” scores in third-party audits.
* Lead plant safety efforts, including co-chairing the Safety Steering Committee, safety inspections, and training, while driving improvements in safety performance as measured by injury frequency and workers' compensation data.
* Participate in business plan development, budgeting processes, and plant-level meetings to ensure effective communication and alignment with operational goals.
* Ability to transform the facility into a CI culture driven by people, process and equipment/technology.
* Ensure the utilization of 4-step process to drive result in sustainability which are Huddles, Daily meeting, utilization of Red Zone and Sic meetings.

**What we require:**

* Minimum of 15 years of experience in food manufacturing management, preferably in the bakery/dessert industry, with demonstrated success at the Plant Manager or Director of Manufacturing/Operations level.
* Bachelor’s degree (MBA a Plus)
* Strong experience with food safety, food process equipment, and regulations.
* Strong experience with emergency preparedness and emergency response plans and procedures.
* Familiar with regulatory and safety codes, including USDA, FDA, and OSHA regulations.
* Knowledge and demonstrated skill in lean manufacturing, Kaizen, kitting, and Six Sigma techniques.
* Prior experience with direct responsibility for a large-scale P&L.
* Strong and effective strategic management skills, including long-range planning, organizing, communicating, influencing, gathering and using information, and motivating a team to achieve results. Ability to use, and teach others to use, various analytical tools and techniques.
* Demonstrated mentoring skills.

**What we offer:**

* Eligible for annual bonus
* Eligible for annual equity grants
* Medical, Dental & Vision
* Eligible for benefits first day of the month following date of hire
* 401K with company match
* 3 weeks of vacation which increases to 4 weeks starting in your 5th year
* 5 days of sick time per year (first year prorated)
* Tuition Reimbursement of $2,500 for qualified programs
* Adoption Assistance Benefit of $2,500
* 25%-35% discount when dining as a guest
* Reusable gift card loaded annually for your dining enjoyment

**About the Company:**

The Cheesecake Factory Bakery creates over 35,000 delicious cheesecakes per day across our two facilities in Calabasas, CA and Rocky Mount, NC plus other baked products for our restaurants, international licensees, and third-party bakery customers.

The Cheesecake Factory Bakery is a subsidiary of The Cheesecake Factory Incorporated. Recognized as a Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For® since 2014, The Cheesecake Factory Incorporated is a global $3.8 billion public company with more than 370 casual dining restaurants and over 48,000 staff members.

We are an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive and welcoming workplace for all. We welcome applicants from a wide variety of identities, ideas, perspectives, backgrounds and experiences to apply. The Cheesecake Factory offers reasonable accommodation to job applicants with disabilities.

#SoCheesecake #LifeAtCheesecake

To notify of a non-compliant job posting, please send a notice to ats@thecheesecakefactory.com.

records.title: Southwest Regional Director of Production and Logistics
records.description:
About PopUp Bagels

 

PopUp Bagels is not just a bagel company—we’re a cultural movement. Our stores are small, our vibes are loud, and our energy is contagious. From signature neon and iconic bullhorns to our “Not Famous but Known” mirror, we’ve reimagined not just how a bagel is created, but how it’s enjoyed: Grip, Rip and Dip! With a cult-like following, massive social presence, and unparalleled collaborations with top companies, partners and Brand Ambassadors PopUp Bagels is defining a new food lifestyle brand.

 

We keep things simple, but we do them really, really well. And our customers agree.

 

The Role

 

We're looking for a Regional Director to lead operations at our Nevada cream cheese production facility. This facility will play an important role in supporting PopUp's continued growth and our ability to deliver the products our customers love.

 

This is a senior operational leadership role responsible for overseeing the day-to-day performance of the facility, from the moment raw materials come through the door to the second finished goods ship out to shops around the country.

 

Here's what makes this role different from other operations roles: we're building something big, and we're building quickly. With established production facilities and operating procedures already in place, the right person for this role will know how to take proven processes, put them into practice, and continue improving them as we grow.

 

We're looking for a problem-solver who isn't afraid to roll up their sleeves and find solutions, a leader who earns trust on the floor just as easily as they collaborate with senior leadership, and someone who can translate operational expectations into consistent, measurable results.

 

This role serves as a key connection between the Nevada production facility and our broader operations leadership team. You'll have the opportunity to influence how we operate, develop our people, and contribute to the continued evolution of our production processes as PopUp expands.

 

If you're a driven leader who thrives in fast-moving environments, values collaboration, and takes pride in building strong teams and efficient operations, this could be the role for you.

 

What You'll Do:

 

Run the Facility. You'll provide day-to-day operational leadership and oversight across Cream Cheese and Schmear production, Warehouse, Quality Assurance, Sanitation, and Equipment Maintenance Working closely with the President of Operations and other facility leaders, you'll implement and maintain established SOPs, manage production schedules, drive throughput targets, and identify opportunities to continuously improve how we operate. You'll be responsible for addressing operational challenges, escalating significant issues when appropriate, and ensuring the facility consistently meets established performance, quality, and safety expectations.

 

Lead People Who Make an Impact. Building a strong team culture is at the core of this role. You'll recruit, develop, and retain a workforce that makes a genuine impact at PopUp Bagels. You'll coach and support your management team, reinforce established training programs, and identify opportunities to strengthen employee development as the operation grows. You'll create an environment where accountability and recognition go hand in hand. Our hourly workforce is the backbone of this operation, and how you show up for them defines everything.

 

Manage the Numbers. You'll be accountable for facility-level operational performance, including production costs, labor efficiency, waste reduction, and budget adherence. You'll partner closely with the President of Operations, Finance, and Accounting on budgeting, forecasting, and period-end reporting, and regularly communicate facility performance, challenges, and opportunities to senior leadership. You'll identify ways to improve efficiency and control costs without compromising quality, safety, or people, while supporting broader capital planning and investment decisions.

 

Drive Supply Chain Alignment. Work directly with our VP of Supply Chain to align production schedules with material availability. You'll oversee raw material procurement planning, inventory controls, and warehouse operations, ensuring established FIFO and food safety standards are consistently followed. You'll collaborate with Supply Chain and other production facilities to support inventory accuracy, product availability, and efficient distribution.

 

Lead Food Safety & Regulatory Compliance. Champion a food-safety-first culture across every part of the facility. You'll ensure consistent execution of established food safety programs and compliance with applicable FDA regulations, FSMA requirements, HACCP plans, and third-party audit standards (SQF, BRC), as applicable. You'll partner with Quality Assurance and the President of Operations to maintain rigorous in-process and finished product quality standards, address compliance concerns, and implement corrective actions when something doesn't meet the bar.

 

Collaborate Across the Company. You'll represent Nevada facility operations in company-wide leadership meetings and collaborate with Distribution & Logistics, Supply Chain, Quality Assurance, and corporate leadership. You'll translate what's happening on the floor into meaningful operational insights, communicate opportunities for improvement, and ensure company priorities and decisions are effectively implemented at the facility level.

 

Who You Are and What You Bring

 

     We're looking for a leader who is genuinely:

 

A scrappy problem-solver. When something breaks at 7am or a key ingredient is backordered, you find a way. You're resourceful, calm under pressure, and put in the time to figure it out. You know when to make decisions, when to collaborate, and when to escalate an issue.

 

A trust-builder. Your team respects you because you've worked to build trust, not because of your title. You're on the floor, you know people's names, and you follow through on what you say.

 

A galvanizing leader. You provide clear direction, get buy-in, and bring your team along with energy and conviction. People want to work hard for you because they know you'll do the same for them.

 

Equally at home in a leadership meeting and a production room. You can review financial and operational performance in the morning and troubleshoot a production issue in the afternoon. You don't ask your team to do what you're not willing to do yourself.

 

Built for growth and continuous improvement. PopUp is growing fast, and our processes will continue to evolve. You appreciate the value of established systems and standards, but you're also comfortable identifying opportunities to make them better. You know how to balance consistency with adaptability as the business scales.

 

       You bring:

 

 
* Bachelor's degree in Food Science, Engineering, Operations Management, Business Administration, or a related field, or equivalent relevant professional experience. Master's degree (MBA or MS) preferred.
 
* 8–10+ years of progressive plant or manufacturing operations leadership experience, including demonstrated responsibility for facility performance, team leadership, and operational budgets.
 
* Experience leading operations in fast-paced manufacturing environments, preferably within growing or multi-site organizations.
 
* Proven track record of leading high-performing, cross-functional manufacturing teams.
 
* Prior food and beverage industry experience strongly preferred; dairy, cream cheese, spreads, or related refrigerated food production experience is a significant plus.
 
* Familiarity with food safety regulatory frameworks, including FSMA, HACCP, GMP, and third-party audit standards (SQF, BRC, AIB).
 
* Strong financial acumen, including budget management, cost analysis, labor efficiency, and operational performance reporting.
 
* Working knowledge of production cost drivers, manufacturing KPIs, and continuous improvement methodologies (Lean, Production Excellence, or equivalent).
 
* Demonstrated experience implementing and maintaining standardized operating procedures, production processes, and operational controls.
 
* Experience partnering with corporate Finance, Supply Chain, Quality Assurance, and Distribution teams.
 
* Availability and willingness to be on-call on weekends and off-hours to respond to facility disruptions or emergencies.
 
* Experience supporting capital improvement projects and operational efficiency initiatives.
 
* A history of building positive, rewarding workplace cultures for hourly workforces.
 

 

Physical Requirements

 

The following physical requirements are representative of those needed to perform the essential functions of this role. Reasonable accommodations may be made for individuals with qualifying disabilities.

 

 
* Ability to walk, stand, and move throughout a production facility for extended periods during daily floor presence and inspections.
 
* Must be able to work in a manufacturing environment with varying temperatures, including refrigerated dairy production and storage areas, moderate to loud noise levels, and exposure to dairy ingredients and food-grade cleaning agents.
 
* Occasional lifting of up to 50 pounds may be required.

records.title: Plant Manager
records.description:
Job ID: 530934
 
 
Ash Grove is a CRH company with a legacy dating back to 1882. We combine technical expertise, safety and customer-focused solutions to deliver reliable performance for our customers. We manufacture and supply high-performance, advanced cementitious materials for the most demanding construction and infrastructure needs. With more than 2,000 people across 60 locations in the United States and Canada, we support a wide range of applications, from major infrastructure projects to the development and refurbishment of residential and non-residential buildings that support everyday life, from highways and bridges to schools and commercial buildings.
 
 
To learn more about us go to www.ashgrove.com
 
 
**Job Summary**
The Plant Manager plans, coordinates, and supervises the production operations, hazardous waste fuel program, maintenance activities, quality and safety programs, and other related functions involved in plant operations. This position incorporates directives provided by corporate management into policies and procedures to maintain standards and schedules. The position exercises direct or indirect supervision over a large number of employees.
 
 
**Job Location**

* This role will work out of our plant in Midlothian, TX.

**Job Responsibilities**

* Promote and follow all plant safety guidelines.
* Conducts meetings with plant staff personnel to communicate, coordinate and discuss plant operations.
* Monitors, inspects, and reviews all plant activities.
* Ensures production schedule corresponds with sales forecasts.
* Assists in investigating customer and quality problems and concerns.
* Meets with government agencies and community groups concerning plant activities to ensure compliance with environmental regulations, policies, and standards.
* Prepares regular reports regarding plant production operations.
* Attends Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA) training for waste-derived fuel activities.
* Promotes effective job performance through motivation, goals, and providing feedback.
* Promotes the safety program, compliance with safety standards, and participates in safety meetings.
* Establishes plant standards, short-term goals, and long-term strategic plans for production, maintenance, and improvements.
* Discusses new products, equipment, and ideas with staff and vendors.
* Analyzes plant costs and explore methods to improve productivity cost-effectively.
* Uses technology to develop a continuous improvement plan for the plant.
* Troubleshoots various problems and performance barriers.

**Job Requirements**

* Ability to read, write, and understand warning labels, instructions, signs, etc.
* Minimum 4 Year - Bachelors Degree in engineering, chemistry, natural sciences, business administration, or closely related field.
* Professional Engineer (PE) preferred
* Ability to develop and deliver effective presentations
* Ability to make decisions and solve problems with high attention to detail and accuracy
* Ability to make sound independent judgments regularly
* Ability to effectively coach and deliver constructive feedback
* Ability to inspire and develop staff
* Proficient in effective negotiation skills in business and construction contracts
* Proficient in Microsoft Office365
* Ability to effectively use computers for general word processing, spreadsheets, presentations, e-mail, internet, and customized company programs.
* Ability to communicate the company's vision into actionable goals and contributions for plant personnel.
* Ability to network with industry professionals, consultants, vendors, suppliers, regulators, and the community.
* Knowledge of safety and environmental health regulations.
* Knowledge of cement chemistry, physical testing, and concrete performance.
* Knowledge of various systems for cement manufacturing (crushing, grinding, pyro processing, chemistry).
* Ability to work from general policies and procedures.
* Ability to refer to supervisor when clarification or interpretation of the organizational policy

**What CRH Offers You**

* Highly competitive base pay
* Comprehensive medical, dental and disability benefits programs
* Group retirement savings program
* Health and wellness programs
* An inclusive culture that values opportunity for growth, development, and internal promotion

**About CRH**
CRH has a long and proud heritage. We are a collection of hundreds of family businesses, regional companies and large enterprises that together form the CRH family. CRH operates in a decentralized, diversified structure that allows you to work in a small company environment while having the career opportunities of a large international organization.
 
 
If you’re up for a rewarding challenge, we invite you to take the first step and apply today! Once you click apply now, you will be brought to our official employment application. Please complete your online profile and it will be sent to the hiring manager. Our system allows you to view and track your status 24 hours a day. Thank you for your interest!
 
 
Ash Grove Cement, a CRH Company, is an Affirmative Action and Equal Opportunity Employer.
 
 
EOE/Vet/Disability
 
 
CRH is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, status as a protected veteran or any other characteristic protected under applicable federal, state, or local law.
 
 
AI tools may be used in certain stages of the employment lifecycle, such as candidate review; however, all final employment decisions will be made by a person.

records.title: Director, Advanced Manufacturing Engineering
records.description:
**Job Description**
**At a Glance**
**Legrand**
has an exciting opportunity for a
**Director of Advanced Manufacturing Engineering**
to join the
**Electrical Infrastructure division.**
This leader identifies, develops, industrializes, and scales manufacturing processes, automation, autonomation, equipment, and digital capabilities that improve safety, quality, service, productivity, capacity, and flexibility across the manufacturing network.
 
 
The Director of Advanced Manufacturing Engineering advises, develops, and executes operational business strategies with the VP of Operations and EI division Leadership Team in support of EI growth and financial goals. Those strategies include footprint and capacity expansion, factory roles, insourcing/outsourcing, operating constraints, and growth enablement into a multiyear manufacturing technology roadmap. The role provides technical leadership for significant manufacturing investments, establishes common engineering and equipment standards, and ensures solutions are economically justified, successfully industrialized, and deliver sustained operating and financial results.
 
 
The Director of Advanced Manufacturing Engineering is expected to determine when advanced technology creates differentiated value and when a simpler process, equipment, maintenance, sourcing, or product solution is more appropriate.
 
 
This position leads a focused technical organization that works through plant resources, internal partners, equipment suppliers, and qualified integrators.
 
 
**Responsibilities**
**What Will You Do?**
**Manufacturing Technology Strategy**

* Develop and maintain a multiyear advanced manufacturing roadmap aligned with business strategy, factory roles, product requirements, capacity needs, and footprint plans.
* Evaluate and deploy appropriate manufacturing technologies, including automation, autonomation, robotics, machine vision, controls, advanced tooling, and digital manufacturing systems.
* Identify manufacturing capabilities the division should protect, build, standardize, modernize, source externally, or retire.
* Adapt technology strategies to differences in product complexity, volume, mix, demand stability, and operating model.

**Opportunity Portfolio and Investment Leadership**

* Build and prioritize a network-wide portfolio of advanced manufacturing, automation, and equipment-modernization opportunities.
* Define the operating loss or constraint being addressed, credible alternatives, expected business impact, investment requirement, lifecycle cost, risk, payback, and sustainment requirements.
* Determine when technology creates differentiated value and when process redesign, tooling, equipment refurbishment, maintenance improvement, outsourcing, product redesign, or another solution is more appropriate.
* Serve as the division’s technical authority for significant manufacturing technology and equipment investments.
* Support footprint, make-versus-buy, capacity, and capital-allocation decisions with clear technical facts and alternatives.
* Lead the division governance process for manufacturing capital planning and deployment, providing consolidated visibility to investment requirements, approvals, timing, expenditure, implementation risk, and expected benefits.
* Partner with Operations, business General Managers, and Finance to develop and maintain a prioritized multi-year manufacturing plan.
* Monitor the deployment of approved manufacturing investments and escalate material risks involving scope, cost, schedule, technical performance, plant readiness, or benefit realization.

**Technical Industrialization and Standards**

* Establish standards for manufacturing equipment, automation, controls, tooling, data connectivity, safety, maintainability, and industrialization.
* Lead technical reviews of equipment specifications, process concepts, integrator selection, designs, risk assessments, acceptance testing, process capability, documentation, training, and critical spares.
* Ensure new processes incorporate quality at source, error-proofing, equipment reliability, operator safety, cybersecurity, and appropriate performance visibility.
* Establish preferred technology platforms, reusable equipment concepts, and qualified supplier and integrator networks where standardization creates value.

**Deployment and Sustainable Results**

* Lead the technical delivery of selected high-value, high-risk, or highly replicable manufacturing initiatives.
* Define when central AME involvement is required and when plant teams can execute within established standards.
* Establish clear ownership for technical development, plant readiness, commissioning, production ramp, and ongoing sustainment.

* Conduct post-implementation reviews to verify that operating and financial benefits are achieved and sustained.
* Capture lessons learned and creates replication methods for proven solutions.

**Organization and Capability Development**

* Build and develop a high-performance advanced manufacturing engineering team with the technical depth required to support the division’s strategy.
* Define which capabilities should be retained internally and which should be accessed through plants, internal partners, equipment suppliers, engineering firms, or system integrators.
* Establish expectations for supplier and integrator performance, documentation, intellectual property, lifecycle support, and reuse of developed solutions.
* Develop plant technical capability to minimize long-term dependence on central resources or external partners.

**Qualifications**
**Education:**

* Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Automation Engineering, or a related technical field.

**Experience**

* At least 10 years of progressive experience in advanced manufacturing engineering, automation, process engineering, or industrialization, including five years leading technical teams or multisite programs.
* Demonstrated experience in automation, robotics, autonomation, controls, machine vision, advanced tooling, or manufacturing data systems.
* Experience with equipment specifications, integrator management, design reviews, acceptance testing, commissioning, capability validation, and production handoff.
* Broad manufacturing-process knowledge and experience in both high-mix and higher-volume environments.
* Proven record of turning manufacturing technology investments into sustained operating and financial results.

**Skills/Knowledge/Abilities**

* Strong understanding of capital economics, lifecycle cost, capacity analysis, labor impact, and benefit realization.
* Ability to translate operating losses and business requirements into prioritized technical opportunities.
* Ability to determine when advanced technology is appropriate and when a simpler operational solution will create greater value.
* Ability to translate technical complexity into clear business decisions and influence across a matrixed organization.
* Strong cross-functional collaboration with Operations, Finance, Product Engineering, Quality, EHS, HR, IT, Supply Chain, Lean, and PMO teams.
* Strong supplier, equipment manufacturer, and system-integrator management capabilities.
* Ability to balance enterprise standardization with legitimate differences across products, processes, plants, and operating models.
* Demonstrated ability to lead technical professionals, develop organizational capability, and operate effectively across multiple businesses and manufacturing locations.

**About Us**
Legrand is the global specialist in electrical and digital building infrastructures. Its comprehensive offering of solutions for residential, commercial, and datacenter markets makes it a benchmark for customers worldwide.
 
 
Bridging power from sources to pathways to touchpoints, Legrand’s Electrical Infrastructure division combines innovation and quality to provide leading solutions for an evolving energy landscape. Our expertly designed products enable customers to confidently address the complex needs and challenges of electrification, while enhancing everyday experiences like plugging in, switching on, and staying connected. Committed to best-in-class service at every stage, we act as a trusted partner for our customers to ensure each project’s success and their continued satisfaction. Legrand's Electrical Infrastructure division includes the following brands and product lines: Girtz, Avtron, Power Bus Way, Cablofil, Connectrac, Wiremold and Pass & Seymour.
 
 
Legrand, North & Central America offers comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, as well as distinctive benefits like a high employer 401K match, paid time off (PTO) and holiday pay, short-term and long-term disability benefit plans, above-benchmark paid maternity and parental leave, bonus opportunities in accordance with the Company’s incentive plans, paid time off to volunteer, and an active/growing Employee Resource Group network. For more information, visit legrand.us.

records.title: Director, NPI Operations Engineering
records.description:
Skydio is the leading US drone company and the world leader in autonomous flight, the key technology for the future of drones and aerial mobility. The Skydio team combines deep expertise in artificial intelligence, best-in-class hardware and software product development, operational excellence, and customer obsession to empower a broader, more diverse audience of drone users, from utility inspectors to first responders, soldiers in battlefield scenarios, and beyond.
 
 
**About The Role**
The NPI Operations Engineering leader builds and leads the team responsible for making Skydio's next generation of autonomous robotics, including drones, docks and accessories, at our internal manufacturing facility in Hayward. You’ll deliver the process, manufacturing know-how and technology needed to build the most capable flying robots on the planet. The team combines Manufacturing Design Engineering and Supply Base Engineering into one organization that is 100% focused on new product development.
 
 
You will own the manufacturability of every new product: assembly time, assembly yield and the processes, fixtures, equipment and supplier readiness needed to hit them. You and your team will engage with Product Engineering from early architecture, carry products through EVT, DVT and PVT, and hand them to Process Engineering for sustaining once they meet clear production-readiness criteria.
 
 
This is a leadership role with significant scope to shape how Skydio develops hardware. You'll set the team's direction, hire and grow engineers, and be the single operations voice in product development. Sustaining engineering for products already in production sits with Process Engineering, so this team stays focused on getting new products right before they reach the line.
 
 
**How You’ll Make An Impact**
**Own manufacturability of new products**

* Own the operations engineering development for NPI programs across supply chain and in-house manufacturing
* Drive design-for-manufacturing, assembly and serviceability (DFx) input from early architecture onward
* Set and commit to assembly time and assembly yield targets for each new product, and track them at every build
* Own operations sign-off at product development gates, and escalate manufacturability risks with clear trade-offs
* Use PFMEA, DFM reviews and prototype yield, quality and process data to align product design with manufacturing strategy
* Identify manufacturing risks early and drive mitigation plans to closure before production ramp

**Lead NPI execution through production readiness**

* Own the manufacturing plan for new products and major design changes, from prototype through PVT
* Define assembly flow, line layout, fixtures and equipment for new products, with labor, cost and capacity estimates that sharpen at each build
* Coordinate engineering, design and production validation builds with Product Engineering, Manufacturing, Test and Quality
* Define production-readiness and handoff criteria, and lead manufacturing readiness reviews
* Develop and continuously improve Skydio's NPI process
* Transfer products to Process Engineering with complete documentation, released tooling, and yield and cycle time at target

**Develop processes, fixtures and assembly equipment**

* Own development and validation of assembly processes, including mechanical assembly, electronics integration, adhesive bonding, fastening, soldering and calibration
* Own design and qualification of assembly fixtures, error-proofing, and assembly equipment such as dispense systems and torque-controlled drivers
* Own the capital budget for new-product assembly fixtures and equipment. Capital for the running production line stays with Manufacturing
* Develop process specifications, control plans, component and assembly CTQs, inspections, inline tests, work instructions and manufacturing BOMs, all complete before handoff
* Use statistical process control (SPC), capability studies and structured experiments to establish robust process windows

**Develop core manufacturing technologies**

* Build a roadmap of core process technologies that future products depend on, such as waterproofing and ingress protection, conformal coatings, sealing and advanced bonding
* Partner with material suppliers, equipment vendors and technology partners to develop, qualify and industrialize these processes ahead of product need
* Serve as the technical owner for these technologies after production launch

**Lead supply base engineering for new products**

* Drive supplier selection, part qualification and supplier process readiness for new products
* Own NPI automation at the process level during development, and partner with the Factory Automation team for production handoff
* Work with suppliers on component DFM, process capability, capacity and quality before production launch
* Partner with Supply Chain and Quality on make-versus-buy decisions, supplier development and capital business cases

**Lead and build the team**

* Set the vision, strategy and execution plan for NPI Operations Engineering
* Lead, hire and develop a team of manufacturing design engineers and supply base engineers, acting as the team's lead technical expert and mentor
* Integrate MDE and SBE into one team with shared programs, goals and ways of working
* Set priorities and staffing across multiple concurrent programs and SKUs at different stages, working with leaders across the company to understand build targets and focus the team on hitting them
* Protect the team's focus on new products, with a clean handoff to Process Engineering for sustaining
* Build an inclusive, diverse, engaged and high-performing team through a mix of external hiring and developing internal talent, with regular coaching and growth opportunities
* Build a culture of technical rigor, ownership and close partnership with design engineering

**Collaboration**

* Work closely with Product Engineering leaders on airframes, propulsion, cameras, sensors, batteries, gimbals and payloads
* Align with Manufacturing, Process Engineering, Test Engineering and Automation Engineering on capacity, equipment and handoff plans
* Communicate program status, risks and manufacturability trade-offs clearly to executive leadership

**What Makes You a Good Fit**

* Bachelor's degree in Manufacturing, Mechanical, Industrial or Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, or a related technical field, or equivalent experience.
* 10+ years of hands-on experience in manufacturing engineering, NPI or production engineering for complex electromechanical products, ideally including high-volume production.
* [4+] years leading engineering teams, including hiring and developing engineers [and managers].
* A track record of taking multiple complex hardware products from early development into high-quality production.
* Deep expertise in DFM/DFA and a history of influencing product design early, not only fixing problems at the build.
* Hands-on fixture design experience, and a strong understanding of factory lines, assembly flow and how to optimize them.
* SPC, Lean and Six Sigma experience.
* Experience working with suppliers on part qualification, process capability and production readiness.
* Strong data skills: you set yield, cycle-time and cost targets, measure them and use the data to drive decisions.
* Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, working collaboratively with people at every level, from technicians to executive leadership.
* Strong project management, analytical skills and attention to detail, with sound independent judgment on complex, broad-scope problems.
* Comfort working in a fast-paced environment with evolving products, and willingness to be on the floor during critical builds.
* Obtaining FAA Part 107 certification within the first 60 days of employment is strongly encouraged for all Skydio employees and required for certain positions.

**Nice to have**

* Experience with drones, aerospace, robotics, autonomous systems or consumer electronics.
* Experience developing waterproofing and ingress-protection solutions (IP-rated products), conformal coating, sealing or adhesive processes.
* Experience with PCBAs, cameras and optics, gimbals, inertial sensors, motors, batteries or composite structures.
* Experience working with contract manufacturers or managing NPI across in-house and outsourced production.

**Compensation:**
At Skydio, our compensation packages for regular, full-time employees include competitive base salaries, equity in the form of stock options, and comprehensive benefits packages. Compensation will vary based on factors, including skill level, proficiencies, transferable knowledge, and experience. Relocation assistance may also be provided for eligible roles. The annual base salary range for this position is $229,500 - $302,500\*. Fundamentally, we believe that equity is the key to long-term financial growth, and we ensure all regular, full-time employees have the opportunity to significantly benefit from the company's success. Regular, full-time employees are eligible to enroll in the Company’s group health insurance plans. Regular, full-time employees are eligible to receive the following benefits: Paid vacation time, sick leave, holiday pay and 401K savings plan. This position and all associated benefits are subject to applicable federal, state, and local laws, as well as the Company’s policies and eligibility criteria.
 
 

* Compensation for certain positions may vary based on the position’s location.

At Skydio we believe that diversity drives innovation. We have created a multidisciplinary environment that embraces the power of diverse perspectives to create elegant solutions for complex problems. We are committed to growing our network of people, programs, and resources to nurture an inclusive culture.
 
 
Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, or other characteristics protected by federal, state or local anti-discrimination laws.
 
 
For positions located in the United States of America, Skydio, Inc. uses E-Verify to confirm employment eligibility. To learn more about E-Verify, including your rights and responsibilities, please visit https://www.e-verify.gov/
