### **POSITION****SUMMARY:**

Working closely with the Division Head and CYP Leadership Team, the Director of Program Quality and Training of Youth Programs documents best practices, designs tools to measure staff and youth outcomes, and supports collaboration among youth-serving organizations. This role provides strategic leadership for quality improvement, staff development, and outcomes assessment across Cambridge Youth Programs’ five youth centers serving more than 1,200 youth ages 9–19, partnering with the Division Head and CYP Leadership Team to codify best practices, build measurement tools, and strengthen collaboration among youth-serving organizations. The Director directly supervises an Administrative Assistant and a Youth Connector, and manages organization-wide partnerships, grant implementation and reporting, and recruitment and outreach efforts.

### **ESSENTIAL****JOB****FUNCTIONS****and****DUTIES:**

*The**essential**functions**or**duties**listed**below**are**intended**only**as**illustrations**of**the**various**type**of**work**that may be performed. The omission of specific statements of duties does not exclude them from the position if the work is similar, related, or a logical assignment to the position.*

* Support expanded learning and out-of-school-time programs serving youth ages 9–19 across the City’s youth centers, including afterschool programs, evening programs, school vacation programming, and specialized youth activities.
* Assist the Division Head for Youth Programs in establishing program goals, objectives, and operational priorities.
* Assist with oversight of programs and activities across the City’s youth centers and collaborate with

 Youth Program staff as part of the Cambridge Youth Programs Leadership Team.
* Provide strategic oversight and support for program quality improvement initiatives and develop systems to assess, track, and manage program performance using positive youth development principles.
* Develop and implement systems to identify staff training and professional development needs and design and deliver training programs that support best practices in youth development, out-of-school-time programming, and effective supervision.
* Provide guidance and support to program staff in program planning, implementation, and continuous improvement efforts.
* Develop and manage organization-wide partnerships, initiatives, and grant partnerships, including implementation oversight and grant reporting; support recruitment materials development and outreach to prospective participants and partner organizations.
* Supervise a Youth Connector who develops and supports sites around middle school and teen transition programs, pre-teen, middle school, and teen recruitment and enrollment, and the organization’s social media plan.
* Provide direct coaching support to assigned youth center sites, working with Program Directors on a weekly basis to develop, implement, and assess both site-based plans and collective projects across the organization.
* Collaborate with the Director of Youth Program Operations to design and implement tools that measure staff and youth outcomes, support organizational accountability, and evaluate program effectiveness.
* Collaborate with the Director of Youth Program Operations, develop, coordinate, and manage staff trainings and professional development for full-time and part-time staff.
* Conduct program evaluations, analyze data, and prepare quarterly reports that support performance measurement and continuous improvement efforts.
* Develop relationships with internal and external stakeholders and support collaboration and resource sharing among youth centers, schools, community organizations, families, and public safety partners.
* Perform related duties as required.

**QUALIFICATIONS:**

***Education/Experience***

* A bachelor’s degree required, preferably in a related field; master’s degree preferred.
* Three (3) years of out-of-school time (OST) program management experience required.
* Five (5) years of experience supervising staff and working with diverse populations required.
* Demonstrated knowledge of positive youth development principles and experience in program development required.
* Experience developing and implementing systems for program delivery, staff training, program quality improvement, evaluation, and assessment processes.
* Demonstrated ability to influence without direct line authority and provide leadership in developing and sustaining collaborative internal and external partnerships.
* Experience working with community agencies, youth, and schools required.
* Strong interpersonal, communication, presentation, writing, organizational, and facilitation skills required.
* An equivalent combination of education, training, and relevant lived or professional experience may be considered.

***Knowledge,******Skills,******and*** ***Abilities:***
-------------------------------------------------------

* Deep knowledge of positive youth development, out-of-school time program models, and trauma-informed, culturally responsive, and linguistically responsive practices.
* Skill in designing, facilitating, and evaluating staff training using adult learning principles, coaching strategies, and reflective supervision techniques.
* Ability to develop and implement program quality frameworks and assessment tools and use qualitative and quantitative data to support continuous improvement efforts.
* Strong facilitation, presentation, and written communication skills, including the ability to convene diverse stakeholders and lead collaborative problem-solving initiatives across multiple sites.
* Proficiency with data management, project management, and budgeting tools and systems.
* Ability to manage complex projects, timelines, and competing priorities while ensuring compliance with applicable policies and regulations.
* Strong interpersonal, organizational, and leadership skills with the ability to build and sustain collaborative partnerships.
* Commitment to anti-racism, diversity, equity, and inclusion.
* Ability to work and interact effectively with individuals and groups across diverse identities, cultures, backgrounds, and ideologies.

### **SUPERVISION****RECEIVED:**

### **Works****under****the****general****direction****of****the****Division****Head****of****Cambridge****Youth****Programs;****exercises****considerable independent judgment; and has work reviewed through conferences, reports, and achievement of program** **objectives.**

### 

### **SUPERVISION****EXERCISED:**

### **May****directly****supervise****two full-time staff members:****an****Administrative Assistant and a Youth Connector.****Also provides functional supervision and coaching support to Program Directors and staff across assigned youth center sites; may oversee consultants or interns engaged in training, program quality, and evaluation** **initiatives.**

### 

### **WORK** **ENVIRONMENT:**

### **Work is performed in a standard office setting with fluorescent lighting, carpeted floors, air conditioning, and moderate noise levels. Evening and weekend hours may be required to support operational needs.**

### 

### **PHYSICAL** **DEMANDS:**

### **Ability****to****use****a****computer****to****access,****input,****and****retrieve****information;****answer****telephones;****maintain****multiple****files; and lift items weighing up to 25 pounds. Ability to travel throughout the City of Cambridge to multiple Youth Center locations as required.**

*The City of Cambridge's workforce, like the community it serves, is diverse. Applicants must have the ability to**work and interact**effectively**with**individuals**and**groups**with**a variety of**identities, cultures, backgrounds, and ideologies.*

**COMPENSATION PHILOSOPHY**

The City of Cambridge is committed to providing fair, transparent, and competitive compensation to all employees. The salary range listed in this job posting reflects the full range for this position's pay grade (Steps 1–10). New employees joining the organization are hired within the hiring range, Steps 1 through 5, with placement at the midpoint reserved for the most qualified candidates. Starting placement is based on directly related education and experience relative to the minimum qualifications of the position, required licenses or certifications, internal equity with current employees, and relevant labor market factors. Employees progress through the 10 steps over time through the City's established step and pay progression policies.

This compensation philosophy applies to non‑union positions. For union positions, please refer to the applicable collective bargaining agreement.

Current City employees applying to another position should refer to the Compensation & Classification Manual for the policies governing promotions, lateral transfers, and other internal salary changes.

**ABOUT THE CITY OF CAMBRIDGE**

The City of Cambridge is a diverse and vibrant community that 120,000 residents of different ethnic, racial, religious, U.S. nationals and other backgrounds call home. We take pride in our City’s diversity and strive to create a workplace that is reflective of the community we serve - one in which all employees can thrive. The City is also deeply committed to creating an environment in which all our employees are treated equitably and feel included. In joining our team, you would work in a workplace environment that advances and values antiracism, diversity, equity, and inclusion (ADEI), and that is committed to embedding ADEI best practices and tenets in all aspects of our work. City of Cambridge residents are especially encouraged to apply to job openings.

**EQUAL OPPORTUNITY / AFFIRMATIVE ACTION**

The City of Cambridge is an Affirmative Action/Equal Opportunity Employer and does not discriminate based on race, color, sex, religion, age, national origin, disability, or any other protected category. Women, minorities, veterans, members of the LGBTQ+ Community, and persons with disabilities are encouraged to apply. The City is committed to advancing a workforce culture of antiracism, diversity, equity, and inclusion. Auxiliary aids and services, written materials in alternative formats, and reasonable modifications in policies and procedures will be provided to qualified individuals with disabilities free of charge, upon request by contacting Human Resources at humanresources@cambridgema.gov.

**Location** Gaithersburg, Maryland, United States **Job ID** R-264366 **Date posted** 19/11/2026

 

**WHY JOIN US?**

At AstraZeneca, we are dedicated to being a Great Place to Work, where you are empowered to push the boundaries of science and unleash your entrepreneurial spirit. With an ambitious goal of delivering 20 new medicines by 2030, there is no better place to make a difference in medicine, for patients, and in society.

Join us on this exciting journey to pioneer the future of healthcare. Our inclusive culture champions diversity and collaboration, and we are always committed to lifelong learning, growth, and development. As part of our team, you'll contribute to groundbreaking advancements that will shape a healthier future for people everywhere. Be a catalyst for change at AstraZeneca, where your work will have a real impact on improving people's lives.

Recognizing the importance of individualized flexibility, our ways of working allow employees to balance personal and work commitments while ensuring we continue to create a strong culture of collaboration and teamwork by **engaging face-to-face in our offices 3 days a week**. Our head office is purposely designed with collaboration in mind, providing space where teams can come together to strategize, brainstorm and connect on key projects.**This is a hybrid role located in Gaithersburg, Maryland. Candidates must reside within commuting distance of Gaithersburg or be willing to relocate for this opportunity.****About the Role**

The Director, Quality Systems is a senior leader within Development Quality Biologics (DQB), accountable for strategy, governance, performance, and continuous improvement of the Quality Management System (QMS) supporting Biologics Development.

The role provides leadership and oversight for critical Quality Systems processes, including Deviation and CAPA Management, Change Control, Quality Risk Management, Inspection Management, Documentation Management, Quality Management Review, and GxP Training and Learning. The Director also leads Business Process Management (BPM) within DQB, ensuring business and quality processes are effectively owned, defined, governed, measured, and continuously improved.

The Director leads a team of up to 12 employees and partners broadly across DQB, Biopharmaceutical Development (BPD), Development Quality, Global Quality, and other functions to deliver a compliant, efficient, risk-based, and future-ready QMS.

**Key Accountabilities**

* Lead the DQB Quality Management System, providing strategy, governance, and oversight to ensure Quality Systems are compliant, effective, risk-based, phase-appropriate, and fit for purpose.

* Provide leadership for core Quality Systems processes, including deviations and CAPAs, change control, quality risk management, inspection management and readiness, documentation management, Quality Management Review, GxP training, and associated metrics and trending. Champion excellence in fundamental Quality processes like root cause analysis and effective CAPA development, risk mitigation, inspection readiness, and continuous improvement.

* Lead Business Process Management within DQB, establishing clear process ownership, governance, performance measures, and improvement mechanisms. Drive simplification, standardization, and elimination of non-value-added activities while maintaining appropriate compliance and control.

* Drive QMS performance and continuous improvement through meaningful metrics, trending, management review, risk identification, and data-driven insights. Translate QMS performance into clear priorities and actions for DQB and BPD leadership.

* Ensure sustainable inspection readiness, including effective preparation, execution, response, and follow-up for regulatory inspections and audits, ensuring learnings are incorporated into Quality System improvements.

* Lead and develop a team of up to 12 employees, building capability in Quality Systems, process ownership, risk-based decision-making, data and digital fluency, continuous improvement, and critical thinking.

**Shaping the QMS of the Future**

The Director will play a key role in evolving the DQB QMS to support the future needs of the Biologics’ development portfolio and AZ's 2030 Vision. The role will champion a phase-appropriate, risk-based and digitally enabled QMS that is fit for purpose, reduces unnecessary complexity, enables innovation, and maintains strong regulatory compliance and patient-focused quality.

The Director role will lead the responsible adoption of AI, advanced analytics, automation, digital workflows, and other emerging technologies to simplify processes, reduce manual work, improve knowledge access, identify quality signals earlier, and strengthen data-driven decision-making. The role will help advance the QMS from primarily retrospective management of quality events toward a more proactive and predictive model, while ensuring appropriate human accountability, transparency, data integrity, traceability, and GxP controls.

**Measures of Success**

**Success in the role will be demonstrated through:**

* A compliant, effective, phase-appropriate, and fit-for-purpose QMS that enables delivery of the AZ portfolio.

* Strong QMS health, including effective management of deviations, CAPAs, changes, risks, training, documentation, and inspection readiness.

* Mature Business Process Management with clear accountability and measurable improvements in process effectiveness, efficiency, and simplicity.

* A Quality Management Review with processes and metrics that provide actionable insights, identify emerging risks, and enable timely leadership decisions.

* Increased and appropriately governed use of data, digital solutions, automation, and AI to improve QMS performance and reduce administrative burden.

* A capable, engaged team prepared to lead and support the QMS of the future.

**Essential Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in a scientific or technical discipline such as Pharmacy, Biology, Chemistry, Biotechnology, or a related field.
* 10+ years of progressive experience within Quality in the pharmaceutical or biopharmaceutical industry, including significant people leadership experience.
* Demonstrated experience leading a sizeable (10+) Quality team/function and delivering measurable improvements.
* Strong knowledge of Quality Management Systems (QMS), including deviations/CAPA, change control, Quality Risk Management, documentation, training, and inspection readiness.
* Strong understanding of GxP requirements, regulatory expectations, and SOP-driven environments, with experience driving compliance and sustainable Quality practices.
* Experience using Quality metrics, trending, risk indicators, and management review to identify priorities and drive continuous improvement.
* Demonstrated experience leading complex, cross-functional initiatives and significant process or organizational change, including management of resources, stakeholders, vendors, and budgets.
* Strong leadership, communication, and influencing skills with the ability to partner across Quality, Development, and senior leadership.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience within biologics, Development Quality, or pharmaceutical development.
* Experience managing managers or leading leaders within a Quality organization.
* Experience with Business Process Management, Operational Excellence, Lean, or continuous improvement.
* Experience leading QMS transformation, harmonization, or process simplification.
* Experience with digital Quality systems, automation, advanced analytics, or AI-enabled Quality solutions in a regulated environment.
* Experience with non-GMP biopharmaceutical work and its phase-appropriate requirements for compliance.

**SO, WHAT’S NEXT?**

To be considered for this exciting opportunity, please complete the full application on our website at your earliest convenience – it is the only way that our Recruiter and Hiring Manager can know that you feel well qualified for this opportunity. If you know someone who would be a great fit, please share this posting with them.

**Are you interested in working at AZ, apply today!**

AstraZeneca is committed to accommodating persons with disabilities. Such accommodation is available on request in respect of all aspects of the recruitment, assessment and selection process and may be requested by emailing AZCHumanResources@astrazeneca.com.

records.description:
**About Us:**

BW Design Group is a fully integrated architecture, engineering, construction, system integration, and consulting firm committed to helping our clients realize their most critical goals from Strategy to Commercialization. As the only firm born from a manufacturing technology company to become an independent and fully integrated firm, we combine deep domain expertise in the manufacturing environment with an approach that is built to serve the dynamic needs of our clients. Rooted in our distinct culture of Truly Human Leadership, we cultivate the leaders who will define tomorrow and partner with our clients in the food & beverage, life sciences, industrial, and advanced technology industries to build the future of manufacturing and technology. 
 
Barry-Wehmiller is a diversified global supplier of engineering consulting and manufacturing technology for the packaging, corrugating, sheeting and paper-converting industries. By blending people-centric leadership with disciplined operational strategies and purpose-driven growth, Barry-Wehmiller has become a $3 billion organization with nearly 12,000 team members united by a common belief: to use the power of business to build a better world. 
 

**Job Description:**

**Who You’ll Work With**

At BW Design Group, you'll collaborate with experienced leaders, technical specialists, and subject matter experts to solve complex challenges for some of the world's leading companies. You'll join a growing team of more than 2000 professionals across nearly 50 U.S. offices where you'll be empowered to make an impact, develop your expertise, and grow your career.

As Director, Quality for our Boston office, you will join our Regulatory Compliance Practice, leading the local quality team while serving as a trusted quality subject matter expert, industry thought leader, and client lead for life science clients across New England.

**What You’ll Do**

This role balances hands-on, billable project/service delivery with growing our Boston team, client relationships, and reputation in the industry.

* Lead a team of quality professionals and interface with clients
* Train, mentor, and recruit talent, championing the career growth of early-career professionals through Individual Development Plans and on-the-job coaching.
* Serve as the firm’s local quality SME across QMS maturity, supplier quality, CAPA and deviations, audit and inspection readiness, remediation, and product development, and advise clients on evolving regulatory guidance.
* Lead delivery of multiple concurrent projects, owning scope, budget, schedule, quality, risk, and client satisfaction.
* Drive thought leadership through publications, white papers, and industry conference presentations, and contribute to firmwide quality standards and best practices.
* Maintain a personal billable utilization target of approximately 60–70% while managing team staffing and utilization to meet billable hours goals.
Develop scopes, estimates, and proposals, and expand engagements with new and existing clients through your industry network. 

**What You’ll Bring**

* A minimum of fifteen years of increasing responsibility in quality services and project management for life sciences, biotech, medical device, or other FDA regulated projects.
* A minimum of five years of people leadership experience, including hiring, coaching, and developing quality professionals.
* Proven success in a consulting or professional services environment, including meeting billable utilization goals and leading client relationships
* Experience leading quality teams across capital project handover, QMS establishment, quality audits, root cause and deviation resolution, and remediation planning.
* Working knowledge of quality regulations for medical device, pharmaceuticals, biologics, C&GT, and aseptic/sterile manufacturing (21 CFR Parts 11, 210/211, and 820; ISO 13485; EU GMP), along with cGMP, good documentation practices, and risk management tools (ICH Q9, FMEA, PFMEA/DFMEA).
* Recognized industry expertise and thought leadership through publications, presentations, or professional associations such as ISPE, PDA, or ASQ; a Boston/New England life science network is preferred.
* Strong communication and technical writing skills, with experience developing proposals and estimates is preferred.
* A willingness to travel regionally to client sites throughout the Boston/New England area, as well as for company sponsored meetings, training, and industry events.
A Bachelor of Science in engineering or a related technical degree; an advanced degree or ASQ certification is preferred. 

 

Our culture and commitment to our people is what sets us apart. We foster an environment of mutual respect, integrity, and unconditional interest in the individual and collective success of our professionals. Our model and entrepreneurial mindset offer a rewarding, challenging, and highly flexible path.

 

As Director of Quality, you will build a meaningful and fulfilling career with the support of professional development resources and mentorships including our First Year Experience program, Individual Development Plans, and Career Path resources and tools. You will be surrounded by exceptional talent who will support your development as both a world-class professional and a highly effective leader.

 

*At Barry-Wehmiller we recognize that people come with a wealth of experience and talent beyond just the technical requirements of a job. If your experience is close to what you see listed here, please still consider applying. We know that our differences often can bring about innovation, excellence and meaningful work—therefore, people from all backgrounds are encouraged to apply to our positions. Please let us know if you require reasonable accommodations during the interview process.*

Barry-Wehmiller is an equal opportunity employer. M/F/D/V This organization uses E-Verify. 
 
Applicants may be subject to pre-employment screening which may include drug screening, reference checks, employment verifications, background screening and/or skills assessments. 
 

**Company:**

Design Group

records.title: VP, Operations
records.description:
**Building the people that build the world.**

With platforms in HVAC and Detection and Measurement, SPX Technologies builds innovative solutions that enable a safer, more efficient, sustainable world. Through our RiSE talent development framework, we Reach, Identify, Strengthen, and Engage our employees to support them in their continued development. We’re a global company of problem solvers, collaborators, and innovators, and our businesses build solutions that impact the world.

As part of HVAC Cooling, SPX Cooling Technologies is a leader in high quality industrial HVAC equipment used to cool large facilities like hospitals, data centers, and power plants. With cooling towers, fans, and refrigeration units, companies rely on brands like Marley, Recold, and SGS to provide comfort and mission critical and industrial cooling solutions.

 

**How You Will Make an Impact**

The Vice President, Operations is a key member of the business unit leadership team and is responsible for the global operations strategy and execution for a rapidly growing business scaling beyond $1.5 billion in annual revenue. This leader will have responsibility for a global manufacturing network of 8+ facilities and will ensure the operations organization has the capacity, capabilities, systems, talent, and processes required to support significant organic and inorganic growth.

The VP, Operations will establish and execute a scalable global operating model that delivers world-class performance across safety, quality, delivery, productivity, cost, working capital, and customer service. This leader will drive greater consistency and integration across manufacturing locations while ensuring the operating footprint, capital investments, supply chain capabilities, and organizational structure are positioned to support long-term growth.

A critical priority will be building an operations organization capable of operating at significantly greater scale. The VP will develop strong plant and functional leaders, create clear accountability across the operations network, institutionalize continuous improvement, and partner closely with Commercial, Engineering, Product Management, Finance, Human Resources, and Supply Chain to translate business strategy into operational execution.

**What You Can Expect in This Role**

* **Develop and execute the global operations strategy** to support the business unit's growth, financial objectives, customer commitments, and long-term strategic plan.
* **Lead the global manufacturing network of 8+ facilities**, establishing common operating expectations, performance metrics, management systems, and accountability across locations.
* **Build the operational capacity and capabilities required to support a $2B+ business**, anticipating future requirements for facilities, equipment, automation, technology, supply chain, and talent.
* **Own manufacturing footprint and capacity strategy**, including plant utilization, expansions, greenfield/start-up operations, consolidations, transfers of production, and other network optimization opportunities.
* **Drive world-class performance across Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost and Working Capital**, establishing clear performance expectations and corrective actions across the global operating organization.
* **Champion a culture of safety**, ensuring consistent leadership practices, risk identification, corrective actions, compliance, and continuous improvement across all manufacturing locations.
* **Establish a disciplined Lean operating system** utilizing standard work, daily management, Kaizen, problem solving, value-stream optimization, and other continuous improvement methodologies to drive sustained performance improvement.
* **Improve operational scalability and productivity** through automation, manufacturing technology, process redesign, labor productivity, plant layout optimization, and improved utilization of assets.
* **Lead operations planning and execution**, ensuring alignment between customer demand, production capacity, labor, materials, inventory, and capital requirements through disciplined SIOP/S&OP and scheduling processes.
* **Optimize material flow and working capital**, improving inventory turns, supplier performance, schedule adherence, throughput, and overall cash conversion.
* **Develop and execute the global capital strategy for Operations**, prioritizing investments based on growth requirements, productivity, safety, quality, capacity, automation, and return on invested capital.
* **Partner with Engineering and Commercial leadership** to improve manufacturability, new product introduction, quote-to-delivery execution, capacity planning, and responsiveness to changing customer requirements.
* **Support acquisition integration and business expansion**, establishing operating standards, identifying synergies, integrating newly acquired manufacturing operations, and accelerating performance improvement.
* **Build a high-performing global Operations leadership team**, strengthening succession depth and developing Plant Managers and functional leaders capable of leading increasingly large and complex operations.
* **Create a culture of accountability and operational excellence**, ensuring leaders use data, metrics, structured problem solving, and operating rhythms to identify issues early and deliver commitments.
* **Serve as a strategic advisor to the President and business leadership team**, bringing an operations perspective to growth strategy, investment decisions, customer commitments, acquisitions, organizational design, and long-range planning.

**Key Measures of Success**

Success in this role will be demonstrated through:

* Sustained improvement in employee safety and environmental performance
* World-class product quality and reduction in customer quality issues
* 95%+ on-time delivery performance and improved schedule adherence
* Year-over-year productivity and manufacturing cost improvement
* Improved inventory turns and working capital performance
* Effective deployment and return on capital investments
* Capacity and manufacturing footprint aligned with business growth
* Successful operational integration of acquisitions and new facilities
* Strong succession depth and leadership capability across Operations
* Consistent implementation of operating systems and best practices across the global manufacturing network

**What We Are Looking For**

**Required Experience**

* 15+ years of progressive operations and manufacturing leadership experience, including significant leadership of complex, multi-site operations.
* Demonstrated experience leading a large-scale global or geographically dispersed manufacturing organization.
* Experience operating within a business of significant scale and complexity, ideally $1B+ in revenue with demonstrated experience supporting substantial growth.
* Proven ability to scale manufacturing capacity, systems, processes, and organizations during periods of rapid growth.
* Demonstrated success improving safety, quality, delivery, productivity, cost, and working capital performance across multiple manufacturing locations.
* Strong experience in Lean manufacturing and building sustainable continuous improvement cultures.
* Experience developing manufacturing footprint strategies including plant expansions, start-ups, consolidations, transfers, and capacity investments.
* Demonstrated success developing senior operations leaders and building strong succession pipelines.
* Experience working effectively within a matrixed, global organization and influencing across functions.
* Experience operating in both union and non-union manufacturing environments preferred.
* Experience integrating acquired businesses or manufacturing operations strongly preferred.

**Knowledge, Skills and Abilities**

* Enterprise-level strategic thinking combined with a strong bias for execution.
* Ability to translate aggressive business growth plans into executable operations, capacity, talent, and capital strategies.
* Strong financial and business acumen with an understanding of operating margin, manufacturing economics, capital allocation, working capital, and return on investment.
* Demonstrated ability to establish operating systems, metrics, governance, and accountability across a diverse manufacturing network.
* Strong change leadership capability and demonstrated success leading organizations through significant growth and transformation.
* Exceptional leadership, communication, and influencing skills with the ability to operate effectively from the plant floor through the executive leadership team.
* Ability to identify emerging operational risks, resolve near-term issues, and simultaneously build the capabilities required for long-term growth.
* Strong knowledge of ERP, planning, manufacturing technology, automation, and data-driven operating environments.

**Education & Certifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Operations, Business, Supply Chain, or related field required.
* MBA or advanced degree strongly preferred.
* Lean/Six Sigma or comparable continuous improvement certification preferred.

**Travel & Working Environment**

* Significant domestic and international travel required to maintain strong leadership presence across the global manufacturing network.
* Regular interaction within manufacturing environments with varying levels of noise, temperature, and other plant conditions.

**How we live our culture**

Our culture is at the center of what we do and, more importantly, who we are. Our core values set a standard for how we manage ourselves, and our Leadership Model sets the standard for how we engage with each other. Whether you are an individual contributor or you lead a large team, each of us leads at SPX.

**What benefits do we offer?**

We know that the well-being of our employees is integral. Our benefits include:

* Generous and flexible paid time off including paid personal time off, caregiver, parental, and volunteer leave
* Competitive health insurance plans and 401(k) match, with benefits starting day one
* Competitive and performance-based compensation packages and bonus plans
* Educational assistance, leadership development programs, and recognition programs

**Our commitment to embrace diversity to build a culture of inclusion at SPX**

We value different backgrounds, experiences, and voices at SPX, and we are committed to challenging ourselves, openly communicating, and striving to improve every day. We believe in creating an inclusive work environment where everyone has a voice and is encouraged to realize their fullest potential.

SPX is an affirmative action and equal opportunity employer committed to making selection decisions without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation or identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other legally protected basis.

records.title: Vice President of Operations
records.description:
**About the Role:**

The Vice President of Operations in a manufacturing environment is responsible for overseeing and optimizing all operational aspects to ensure efficiency, quality, and profitability. This role requires strategic leadership to align operational goals with the company’s overall vision and market demands. The VP of Operations will drive continuous improvement initiatives, manage cross-functional teams, and implement best practices to enhance production processes and supply chain management. They will also play a critical role in financial planning, resource allocation, and risk management to support sustainable growth. Ultimately, this position ensures that manufacturing operations meet customer expectations while maintaining compliance with industry standards and regulatory requirements.

**Minimum Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Engineering, Operations Management, or a related field.
* Minimum of 10 years of progressive leadership experience in manufacturing operations.
* Proven track record of strategic planning and successful execution in a complex manufacturing environment.
* Strong financial acumen with experience in budgeting, forecasting, and financial analysis.
* Demonstrated ability to lead large teams and manage cross-functional projects.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Master’s degree in Business Administration (MBA) or relevant advanced degree.
* Experience with Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, or other continuous improvement methodologies.
* Familiarity with advanced data analytics tools and enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems.
* Previous experience in a senior executive role within the manufacturing industry.
* Certifications related to operations management or leadership development.

**Responsibilities:**

* Develop and execute comprehensive operational strategies that support the company’s business objectives and growth plans.
* Lead and mentor senior management and operational teams to foster a culture of high performance, accountability, and continuous improvement.
* Oversee production planning, quality control, supply chain logistics, and maintenance to maximize operational efficiency and product quality.
* Collaborate with finance to manage budgets, forecast operational costs, and analyze financial performance to inform decision-making.
* Utilize data analytics to monitor key performance indicators, identify operational risks, and implement corrective actions promptly.
* Drive talent development initiatives to build a skilled and motivated workforce aligned with organizational goals.
* Communicate operational plans, progress, and challenges effectively to the executive leadership team and stakeholders.
* Ensure compliance with health, safety, environmental regulations, and industry standards across all manufacturing sites.

**Skills:**

The required skills such as Executive Presence and Leadership are essential for inspiring and guiding diverse teams while representing the operations function at the executive level. Strategic Planning and Execution skills enable the VP to develop actionable roadmaps that align operational activities with long-term business goals. Operational Strategy expertise is applied daily to optimize manufacturing processes, improve supply chain efficiency, and ensure product quality. Communication and Presentation skills are critical for articulating complex operational plans and performance metrics to stakeholders clearly and persuasively. Delegation, Financial Planning and Analysis, Data Analysis, and Talent Development skills are utilized to empower teams, manage resources effectively, make data-driven decisions, and cultivate a high-performing workforce that drives continuous operational excellence.

postedPay.title: VP of Ops for a fast growing Food Production Facility

records.description:
Taher is seeking a **Vice President of Operations** to lead its Production Kitchen in Plymouth, Minnesota. This senior leadership role is responsible for the day-to-day and long-term operational performance of a high-volume food production environment, including production, packaging, food safety, quality assurance, sanitation, maintenance, production planning, staffing, and continuous improvement.

The ideal candidate is a hands-on, people-centered operations leader who can strengthen systems, support employee development, improve production efficiency, and protect Taher's commitment to safe, high-quality, chef-driven food. This individual will bring operational discipline, food production expertise, financial acumen, and the ability to lead teams through growth while maintaining a strong culture of safety, quality, teamwork, and accountability.

**Key Responsibilities**
========================

**Strategic** **and Operational** **Leadership**
------------------------------------------------

* Develop and execute the operations strategy for the Plymouth Production Kitchen in alignment with Taher's business goals, customer commitments, and growth opportunities.
* Partner with senior leadership, culinary, purchasing, finance, human resources, quality assurance, and customer-facing teams to support production growth and operational excellence.
* Lead planning for new products, increased production volumes, new lines, equipment needs, and staffing models.
* Establish clear operational goals, performance standards, and daily accountability routines for safety, quality, service, cost, and people.

**Production Kitchen** **Operations**
-------------------------------------

* Provide leadership and oversight for daily production, packaging, storage, sanitation, and outbound readiness at the Plymouth Production Kitchen.
* Drive improvements in employee safety, food safety, quality, throughput, labor utilization, line balance, yield, waste, and on-time completion.
* Ensure production schedules are met while maintaining product specifications, ingredient standards, labeling accuracy, and customer requirements.
* Optimize staffing models across shifts, production lines, machine operations, hand-wrapping, packing, rework, and support functions.
* Support supervisors, leads, maintenance, quality, and production teams in identifying and resolving issues quickly and professionally.

**Food Safety****,** **Quality****, and Compliance**
----------------------------------------------------

* Ensure a strong culture of food safety, sanitation, quality, regulatory compliance, and continuous improvement across all production activities.
* Oversee compliance with applicable FDA, USDA, OSHA, HACCP, GMP, allergen control, labeling, sanitation, and customer requirements.
* Partner with Food Safety and Quality Assurance leadership to maintain strong systems for product checks, inspections, corrective actions, documentation, and audit readiness.
* Ensure timely investigation and resolution of product quality, food safety, foreign material, temperature, sanitation, and customer concerns.

**Supply Chain****,** **Planning****, and Material Readiness**
--------------------------------------------------------------

* Partner with purchasing, inventory, warehouse, culinary, and production planning teams to ensure ingredients, packaging, labels, equipment, and labor are ready before production begins.
* Improve production scheduling, inventory accuracy, freezer/cooler organization, material flow, and customer service performance.
* Identify opportunities to reduce complexity, prevent shortages, improve changeovers, and strengthen end-to-end execution from receiving through shipping.

**Financial and Operational Performance**
-----------------------------------------

* Own operational budgets for the Plymouth Production Kitchen and contribute to annual operating, staffing, equipment, and capital plans.
* Drive cost control and margin improvement without compromising food safety, product quality, employee safety, or customer expectations.
* Monitor key performance indicators including labor efficiency, yield, waste, downtime, rework, production output, inventory accuracy, and service levels.
* Identify and execute opportunities to improve profitability, line productivity, equipment utilization, and return on invested capital.

**Continuous Improvement****, Equipment,** **and** **Facility Support**
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

* Champion practical continuous improvement methods that help teams work safer, faster, cleaner, and more consistently.
* Develop and execute programs to reduce downtime, improve line flow, minimize waste, strengthen changeovers, and increase production capacity.
* Oversee equipment investments, automation opportunities, maintenance priorities, facility improvements, and capital projects.
* Promote the use of data, visual controls, staffing boards, production records, and shift communication to improve daily decision-making.

**People** **Leadership** **and Culture**
-----------------------------------------

* Build, develop, and retain a strong Plymouth operations leadership team, including supervisors, leads, technical roles, production support, and front-line employees.
* Establish a culture of accountability, teamwork, respect, safety, sanitation, continuous improvement, and pride in Taher's standards.
* Develop succession plans, training routines, onboarding support, and leadership development for critical production kitchen roles.
* Promote effective communication across shifts, departments, and support teams so employees understand the plan, the priorities, and the standard.

**Benefits**
------------

Medical & Dental

Doctegrity Telemedical

401k

Sick Time

Vacation Time

Lifemart Corporate Discount program

Bonus structure

Free turkey for Thanksgiving

**Who We Are:**
---------------

Taher, Inc. is a family-owned and operated, chef-driven, food service management company. We specialize in providing K-12 school lunch management, campus dining, senior dining, catering, vending, and office beverage services to clients in our growing nationwide footprint.

Customers choose Taher for its chef-developed recipes created from natural and sustainable local sources, and for delivering the latest in culinary trends and operational resources to provide outstanding food options for our guests. Taher maintains a consistent presence in Food Service Management's Top 25 companies.

Requirements:

**Qualifications**
==================

* Bachelor's degree in Operations Management, Engineering, Food Science, Business, Culinary Operations, or a related field preferred; equivalent experience may be considered.
* 10+ years of progressive leadership experience in food production, commissary, production kitchen, packaged food, convenience retail food, or related high-volume food manufacturing environment.
* Experience leading multi-shift production teams, production supervisors, line leads, technical staff, sanitation, and quality support functions.
* Demonstrated success improving production output, labor efficiency, staffing stability, quality performance, sanitation execution, and operational discipline.
* Strong working knowledge of food safety, HACCP, GMPs, sanitation, allergen controls, labeling, traceability, regulatory requirements, and production documentation.
* Experience with Lean, continuous improvement, visual management, production metrics, root cause problem solving, and equipment reliability practices.
* Proven ability to manage operating budgets, staffing plans, production schedules, capital projects, and cross-functional priorities.
* Strong financial, analytical, communication, coaching, and team-building skills.

**Required Skills and Experience**
==================================

* Proven leadership in high-volume food production, commissary, production kitchen, packaged food, convenience retail food, or related manufacturing environments.
* Strong knowledge of food safety, sanitation, HACCP, GMPs, allergen control, labeling, traceability, audits, inspections, and regulatory compliance.
* Demonstrated ability to lead multi-shift teams, production supervisors, line leads, technical employees, sanitation teams, quality support, and front-line employees.
* Experience managing operating budgets, labor models, production schedules, capital projects, equipment priorities, and cross-functional initiatives.
* Strong analytical, communication, coaching, problem-solving, and team-building skills.
* Ability to balance strategic planning with hands-on daily execution in a fast-paced production environment.

records.description:
The **Director of Operations** - Production Kitchen provides strategic and hands-on leadership for Taher's Plymouth, MN manufacturing operation. This role is responsible for leading safe, efficient, high-quality, and cost-effective production across food manufacturing, meal assembly, packaging, warehousing, logistics coordination, maintenance partnership, food safety, and continuous improvement.

This leader will help position the Production Kitchen for growth by strengthening operating discipline, improving production flow, developing leaders, supporting audit readiness, and ensuring Taher delivers consistent, chef-driven products that meet customer, regulatory, and company expectations.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Operational Leadership**

* Lead daily operations for Taher's Plymouth Production Kitchen, including production, packaging, warehousing, and cross-functional manufacturing support.
* Ensure safety, food quality, service, production attainment, labor efficiency, and cost expectations are met consistently.

* Develop and execute operational plans aligned with company growth and financial objectives.
* Establish clear performance expectations, operating rhythms, and accountability throughout the operations organization.

Partner with the VP of Operations

* - Manufacturing, Plant Manager, FSQA, culinary, purchasing, finance, HR, and logistics teams to align priorities and remove barriers.

**Manufacturing and Production**

* Oversee high-volume food production, meal assembly, sandwich production, packaging, and related manufacturing activities.

* Monitor production performance and implement improvements in labor efficiency, throughput, yield, downtime, and capacity utilization.

* Ensure production schedules are achieved while maintaining food safety, allergen control, product quality, labeling accuracy, and customer specifications.

* Identify and resolve operational bottlenecks and constraints.
* Lead efforts to improve Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) and manufacturing performance.

**Food Safety and Quality**

* Promote and maintain a strong food safety and quality culture throughout the organization.
* Ensure compliance with applicable food safety, regulatory, customer, and company requirements.

* Partner with FSQA leadership to maintain audit readiness and compliance with HACCP, GMP, SQF, FDA, USDA, allergen, environmental monitoring, sanitation, and documentation requirements.

* Support investigations and corrective actions related to food safety, quality, customer complaints, and production issues.
* Ensure operational teams understand and consistently follow food safety and quality procedures.

**Continuous Improvement**

* Lead continuous improvement initiatives focused on safety, quality, productivity, cost reduction, and service.
* Apply Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, TPM, and other improvement methodologies as appropriate.
* Develop and monitor key performance indicators and use data to drive decision-making.
* Reduce waste, improve yields, minimize downtime, and increase manufacturing efficiency.
* Implement standardized operating procedures and best practices across facilities.

**Maintenance and Engineering**

* Partner with maintenance and engineering teams to improve equipment reliability and reduce unplanned downtime.
* Support preventive and predictive maintenance programs.
* Participate in capital planning and prioritize investments that improve safety, capacity, quality, and operational performance.
* Lead or support equipment, automation, and facility improvement projects.

**Supply Chain and Customer Service**

* Partner with Supply Chain, Planning, Procurement, and Logistics teams to ensure efficient flow of materials and finished goods.
* Support production planning and inventory management to optimize customer service and working capital.
* Improve communication and coordination between operations and commercial teams.
* Ensure operational readiness for new products, customer requirements, and business growth.

**Financial Performance**

* Manage operational budgets and support the development of annual operating plans.
* Identify and execute cost savings and margin improvement initiatives.
* Monitor labor, materials, overhead, waste, and other key operational costs.
* Support capital investment decisions and ensure projects deliver expected business results.
* Drive operational performance that supports revenue growth and profitability.

**People Leadership**

* Lead, coach, and develop production managers, supervisors, line leads, machine operators, warehouse associates, maintenance partners, and other operational team members.
* Build a culture of accountability, teamwork, food safety discipline, urgency, employee engagement, and continuous improvement.

* Establish succession and development plans for key operations positions.
* Promote effective communication across shifts, departments, and locations.
* Ensure appropriate staffing and organizational capability to meet business objectives.

* Medical & Dental
* Doctegrity Telemedical
* 401k
* Sick Time
* Vacation Time
* Lifemart Corporate Discount program
* Bonus structure
* Free turkey for Thanksgiving

Customers choose Taher for its chef-developed recipes created from natural and sustainable local sources, and for delivering the latest in culinary trends and operational resources to provide outstanding food options for our guests. Taher maintains a consistent presence in Food Service Management's Top 25 companies.

* Bachelor's degree in Operations Management, Food Science, Engineering, Supply Chain, Business, or a related field preferred; equivalent experience will be considered.

* Experience in food manufacturing, ready-to-eat foods, bakery, commissary, packaged goods, meal assembly, or high-volume production strongly preferred.

* Demonstrated success improving productivity, quality, service, and manufacturing costs.
* Strong knowledge of food safety, quality systems, HACCP, GMP, and applicable regulatory requirements.
* Experience with Lean Manufacturing, continuous improvement, OEE, and operational performance management.
* Strong financial and business acumen.
* Proven leadership, coaching, communication, and problem-solving skills.
* Multi-site operations experience preferred.

* Manufacturing excellence

* Continuous improvement

records.description:
**About the role**

**Krosswood Doors** builds residential interior and exterior doors in Tucson, Arizona, and sells them through The Home Depot and Krosswood.com. We build doors mostly one at a time, through manual and semi-automated processes, against a daily target of 400+ doors and lead times under three days.

The **Director of Operations** is the top plant leader in Tucson and owns every function and transaction at the site, from receiving raw material to shipping quality doors on time. The job: consistently deliver safe, high-quality products, on time, at the lowest sustainable cost, while developing people and building scalable systems. At our size, that means deep involvement in daily operations while building the organization for future growth.

You will partner closely with the SVP Operations on both daily execution and priorities. The SVP owns multi-year strategy, final budget and capital approval, the ERP roadmap and the executive relationship with The Home Depot. You will be the leader on the floor and the site’s main point of contact for every stakeholder.

**How we run the plant**

* Daily success: a steady and consistent flow of great doors, built safely and efficiently, with uncompromising quality. The system you will run and improve:
* Daily accountability system: production hard-start, morning stand-up, QA meeting, hourly board walks and daily close-out, backed by Leader Standard Work for every manager.
* Total Ownership: every process, machine, tool, task and space has one named owner and a documented standard.
* SQDC-P scoreboards: safety, quality, delivery, cost and people results by station, with a first pass yield (FPY) target of 95% or better.
* 6S and visual management: 6S (5S plus safety) at every station, standard work, operator and machine cards.
* Escalation: operator to lead in under 5 minutes, to manager in under 15, to Director of Operations in under 30, and to the SVP Operations in under 60.

**What you’ll do**

* Operational leadership: own the daily production plan and schedule, capacity planning, staffing, equipment and resource allocation; manage the hour-by-hour KPIs, remove bottlenecks and lead daily issue resolution.
* Safety: own safety culture, compliance, training, reporting, audits and corrective actions; make sure the daily safety cross is completed and every issue is resolved.
* Operational excellence: run and improve the production management system (daily and weekly accountability rhythms and KPIs); drive documented standard work, visual management, Lean, 6S, kaizen and labor utilization.
* Quality: build and own the quality management system: documented quality standards, FPY, escape prevention, defect reduction and root cause and corrective action, working with the Quality & Process Specialist.
* Delivery: drive throughput, flow and on-time delivery to homedepot.com; avoid and mitigate Home Depot fines; manage releases, PPR and duration exceptions; lead ERP (NetSuite) improvements with IT.
* Cost: own labor and material cost, labor utilization and budget adherence; align staffing, temp labor and overtime with sales volume; build capital (CAPEX) proposals and a continuous cost-improvement program.
* People: build an engaged culture; run performance management (reviews, scorecards, discipline), recognition, staffing and wages; develop your managers into leaders; own training and succession planning for direct labor.
* Warehouse: own inventory and transaction accuracy, documented SOPs and adherence, PPR and order management, staffing, material shortages and cost savings.
* Analysis: make data-based decisions; build system-based tools and KPIs; dig into the details to find wins, losses, risks and opportunities.
* Cross-functional: work with sales, purchasing, IT and finance to resolve issues and improve quality, delivery, cost and the customer experience; handle HR issues and site administration.
* Process knowledge: know each process well enough to spot when an operator, machine or function falls short of the expected result, then lead root cause analysis and corrective action.

**What you’ll bring**

Required

* 10+ years of manufacturing operations leadership in a high-mix, low-volume, custom or craft setting, including leading managers across production, warehouse and maintenance.
* Proven success implementing and sustaining Lean, 5S/6S and Kaizen.
* Has built and run a production management system: daily and weekly accountability rhythms, KPIs and visual management.
* Has built or improved a quality management system, with measurable gains in first pass yield and defect reduction.
* Owned an operating budget and built capital spending proposals; manages labor, temp staffing, overtime and material cost.
* Strong data skills: builds KPIs and reports, and uses data to find root causes and make decisions.
* Hands-on HR experience: performance reviews, discipline, wage adjustments, hiring and leadership development.
* Experience writing, enforcing and training SOPs and process documentation.
* Fluent in English and Spanish, able to communicate clearly with the whole workforce.
* Able to separate a process breakdown from process noncompliance, and respond to each the right way.
* A confident, hands-on leader with the discipline to hold the line and the patience to build people up.
* Bachelor’s degree in operations management, industrial engineering, engineering or business, or equivalent experience.

Preferred

* NetSuite or other ERP experience, including leading ERP improvements (strongly preferred).
* Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt.
* Preventive maintenance or TPM knowledge.
* Safety management and OSHA compliance experience.
* Wood products, doors, millwork, cabinetry or finishing background.
* Experience meeting retailer or e-commerce delivery requirements, such as The Home Depot.

**How success is measured**

Timeframe

* First 30 days - Knows every station and function; runs the daily accountability system alongside the SVP Operations; has met each manager one-on-one; understands the budget
* First 90 days - Runs the site independently; Leader Standard Work followed at every station; top 3 throughput, quality and cost losses named with action plans; 12-month improvement plan agreed with the SVP Operations
* Ongoing - 400+ doors a day at 95%+ FPY; zero lost-time injuries; on-time delivery with no fines; labor and material cost on budget; managers leading their areas on their own; systems that scale with growth

**Work environment and benefits**

This is a 100% on-site, floor-first role in an active manufacturing plant with machinery, noise, wood dust and finishing materials. PPE is provided and required.

**Benefits**: Medical, dental, 401(k), PTO and more

**Salary:** $72,000–$85,000 per year, based on experience, plus 10% annual bonus

records.title: Director of Operations
records.description:
Advanced Mission Partners, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Science Systems and Applications, Inc (SSAI) seeks a Director of Operations to provide strategic and operational leadership across our aerospace component manufacturing, electronics manufacturing, and engineering services operations. The successful candidate will be responsible for overseeing daily operations, optimizing manufacturing performance, managing resources, and ensuring the successful delivery of high-quality products and engineering services. This position will play a critical role in driving operational excellence, improving profitability, strengthening customer relationships, and supporting the company's continued growth. 
The ideal candidate will have a strong background in aerospace and defense manufacturing, demonstrated leadership experience, and a proven ability to manage complex manufacturing operations while meeting demanding quality, cost, and delivery requirements.

**Required Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's Degree (BS) in Engineering, Manufacturing, Business Administration, Project Management, Operations Management, or a related technical discipline.
* 12+ years of progressively responsible experience in program management, project management, manufacturing operations, or engineering.
* At least 5 years of experience managing complex technical or manufacturing programs, preferably within the aerospace, defense, or electronics manufacturing industries.
* Demonstrated success leading manufacturing operations, managing budgets, and improving operational performance.
* Experience working with aerospace and defense customers, including government agencies, prime contractors, and commercial aerospace organizations.
* Working knowledge of manufacturing processes, engineering development, quality assurance, and supply chain management.
* Experience managing multidisciplinary teams and implementing operational improvement initiatives.
* Strong financial, analytical, leadership, and problem-solving skills.

**Desired Qualifications:**

* Project Management Professional (PMP) certification.
* Experience in aerospace component manufacturing, electronics manufacturing services (EMS), or precision manufacturing.
* Familiarity with printed circuit board assembly (PCBA), electronic systems integration, and aerospace manufacturing processes.
* Knowledge of AS9100, ISO 9001, IPC standards, and applicable aerospace quality requirements.
* Experience with government contracts, including FAR, DFARS, ITAR, and EAR requirements.
* Familiarity with Earned Value Management (EVM), program financial forecasting, and cost control methodologies.
* Experience using Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems and project management software, such as Microsoft Project or equivalent tools.
* Experience supporting new product introduction (NPI), production transitions, and continuous improvement initiatives.
* Familiarity with Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma methodologies.
* Demonstrated experience with manufacturing automation, process optimization, and production scalability.

**EOE, including disability/vets**

***Physical Requirements:*** *While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to stand, walk, and use hands to touch, handle or feel objects, tools or controls. records.title: Director, Quality Systems & Digital Quality
records.description:
Cambridge, MA

Development – Quality Assurance /

Full-Time /

Hybrid

 

*Scholar Rock is delivering muscle-targeted breakthroughs to transform the treatment of spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) and other rare neuromuscular diseases where muscle atrophy remains a critical unmet need.*

*As a global leader in myostatin biology, a field focused on proteins that regulate muscle mass, the biopharmaceutical company is named for the visual resemblance of a scholar rock to protein structures. Our commitment to unlock fundamentally different treatment approaches is powered by broad application of a proprietary platform, which has developed novel monoclonal antibodies to modulate protein growth factors with extraordinary selectivity. Scholar Rock works every day to create new possibilities for patients through its highly innovative anti-myostatin program, including opportunities in additional rare neuromuscular diseases. Learn more about our neuromuscular franchise at* ***ScholarRock.com*** *and follow @ScholarRock on X and on LinkedIn.*

 

**Summary of Position:**

Scholar Rock is seeking an experienced, hands-on Director, Quality Systems & Digital Quality. Reporting to the Sr Director, Global Quality Systems & Compliance, this leader is an integral part of Scholar Rock’s Quality Management System (QMS) and the GxP computerized systems and data that support it, across our commercial and early-phase pipeline. Because Scholar Rock outsources all GMP manufacturing, testing, and distribution to qualified contract organizations, this role will build and sustain a lean, risk-based, phase-appropriate QMS that meets US (FDA), EU (EMA/EU GMP), and Japan (MHLW/PMDA) requirements, ensuring that Scholar Rock’s own systems are inspection-ready and that the GxP data generated on our behalf by contract partners is reliable, complete, and traceable.

### **Position Responsibilities**

***Quality Management System***

* Partner with Quality process owners to ensure GxP digital systems effectively support QMS processes, enabling efficient, compliant, and scalable operations aligned with Scholar Rock’s evolving business needs.
* Track a focused set of key QMS performance indicators and present them in periodic quality management reviews.

 

***Digital Systems & Computer Software Assurance***

* Provide Quality oversight of Scholar Rock’s GxP computerized systems (largely cloud/SaaS, e.g., eQMS, document and training management, ERP and other GxP-relevant platforms), ensuring compliance with 21 CFR Part 11, EU GMP Annex 11, and Japan’s ER/ES guideline.
* Lead and execute GxP system enhancements and continuous improvement initiatives, partnering with business process owners to define requirements, evaluate solutions, manage implementation, and ensure effective adoption of new functionality.
* Establish and apply a risk-based computerized system validation and assurance approach consistent with applicable GxP regulatory requirements, leveraging GAMP 5 principles, relevant FDA guidance, and vendor documentation to ensure appropriate assurance while minimizing redundant testing.
* Oversee the GxP computerized system lifecycle, including risk-based validation and assurance, change control, periodic reviews, access management, audit trail controls, data retention, and system retirement. Ensure appropriate validation deliverables, testing, and documented evidence are established and maintained throughout the system lifecycle.
* Partner with IT and business owners on system selection, implementation, upgrades, and vendor releases so that new digital capabilities are adopted with right-sized assurance.
* Support qualification of computerized system suppliers (e.g., SaaS, software, and IT service providers), including risk-based vendor assessments and audits, and the Part 11/Annex 11 and data integrity provisions of their quality agreements; qualification of GMP manufacturing and testing suppliers remains with other Quality functions.
* Monitor evolving expectations, including the revision of EU GMP Annex 11 and emerging guidance on AI in GxP settings, and advise on practical, compliant adoption of digital and AI-enabled tools.
* Support the implementation of AI-enabled tools in GxP processes (e.g., document drafting and review, deviation and complaint trending, AI features within eQMS and other platforms), defining risk-based assurance, human oversight, and data integrity controls proportionate to each tool’s intended use and impact on product quality and patient safety.
* Partner with IT, Legal, and business owners to establish lightweight governance for AI use in GxP activities, including an inventory of AI applications, acceptable-use expectations, training, and ongoing performance monitoring.
* Lead the development and execution of a risk-based digital Quality roadmap, prioritizing system enhancements and improvements based on business needs, compliance requirements, and operational efficiencies.
* Partner with Quality process owners and cross-functional stakeholders to identify improvement opportunities, translate business needs into functional requirements, and implement scalable digital solutions.
* Drive the end-to-end implementation of GxP system enhancements, including requirements definition, risk assessments, configuration, testing, validation documentation, deployment, and post-implementation support.
* Establish efficient processes for managing system changes, including vendor releases, impact assessments, regression testing, and maintaining systems in a validated state.
* Provide hands-on leadership and technical guidance for Veeva eQMS, eDMS, and other GxP platforms, ensuring effective system functionality, integration, and continuous improvement.
* Establish clear system ownership, governance, and accountability across Quality, IT, and business functions, including responsibilities for system administration, validation, user access, and ongoing lifecycle management.
* Support regulatory inspections and audits involving computerized systems, electronic records, electronic signatures, and data integrity, including preparation of supporting documentation and remediation of identified gaps.
* Drive effective adoption of new digital capabilities through stakeholder engagement, training, change management, and ongoing evaluation of system effectiveness.
* Establish and maintain effective governance for GxP system enhancements and vendor releases, including change prioritization, impact assessments, testing strategies, implementation planning, and post-deployment monitoring.

 

***Data Integrity & Data Governance***

* Lead the development and ongoing governance of Scholar Rock’s GxP data integrity program, establishing risk-based expectations, controls, and oversight mechanisms in partnership with business process owners and applicable Quality functions.
* Define a lightweight data governance model with clear data ownership and stewardship for GxP data across Quality, Regulatory, Technical Operations, and Clinical.
* Extend data integrity oversight to contract organizations through quality agreement requirements, data integrity–focused audit criteria, and review of partner-generated data (e.g., batch records, CoAs, stability, deviations).
* Establish governance and controls for GxP-relevant master data, partnering with designated data owners to ensure data accuracy, consistency, integrity, and appropriate alignment across internal systems, contract partners, and regulatory information.
* Lead data integrity risk assessments and drive timely, proportionate remediation of gaps.

 

***Inspection Readiness & Regulatory Support***

* Lead inspection readiness for the QMS, computerized systems, and data integrity controls, and support health authority inspections of Scholar Rock and its contract partners.
* Contribute to regulatory submissions and responses, such as annual reports, IND/CTA updates, and marketing applications in the US, EU, and Japan.
* Maintain awareness of regulatory changes in the US, EU, and Japan and translate them into practical, minimal-necessary updates to the QMS.

 

***Leadership & Partnership***

* Act as the subject matter expert and coach for colleagues across Quality and partner functions on QMS, computerized system, and data integrity topics.
* Collaborate with the Head of Global Quality and Quality leadership, IT, Regulatory, Technical Operations, and Clinical to align quality systems with corporate goals and regulatory obligations.
* Champion a culture of quality, accountability, and data integrity, and serve as a change agent for simplification and digitization of the QMS.

### **Candidate Requirements**

* BS/MS degree in a scientific, engineering, or information systems discipline.
* 12+ years of experience in the pharmaceutical/biotech industry, with 5+ years leading Quality systems, computerized system compliance, or related programs; biologics experience preferred.
* Deep understanding of GxP and Quality System requirements (US, EU, and Japan) for biologics development and commercial products, including ICH Q9(R1) and Q10.
* Demonstrated expertise in 21 CFR Part 11, EU GMP Annex 11, risk-based CSA/GAMP 5, and global data integrity expectations, including qualification of computerized system and SaaS suppliers.
* Familiarity with AI/ML-enabled tools in regulated environments and with emerging health authority expectations for AI use in GxP activities.
* Experience in a virtual or outsourced model, including oversight of quality systems and data integrity at CDMOs and contract testing laboratories.
* Experience leading or supporting regulatory inspections and interfacing with global health authorities.
* Proven ability to design lean, simple processes and to make pragmatic, risk-based decisions on what is required versus nice to have.
* Highly proactive, decisive, and capable of independently managing key initiatives as a hands-on individual contributor.
* Collaborative leader who builds quality culture and capability across teams through influence, coaching, and knowledge sharing.
* Excellent communication skills and ability to influence across functions and with external partners.

$200,000 - $260,000 a year

*Scholar Rock is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees*.
