records.description:
**Pulse Biosciences (Nasdaq: PLSE): Join the Future of Bioelectric Medicine**

Pulse Biosciences is a novel bioelectric medicine company committed to health innovation that has the potential to improve the quality of life for patients. The Company’s proprietary CellFX® nsPFA™ (nanosecond Pulsed Field Ablation) technology delivers nanosecond pulses of electrical energy to non-thermally ablate cells while sparing adjacent noncellular tissue.

The Company is actively pursuing the development of its CellFX nsPFA technology for use in the surgical treatment of atrial fibrillation and percutaneously in a select few other markets where it could have a profound positive impact on healthcare for both patients and providers. Visit pulsebiosciences.com to learn more.

**Why Join Us?**

At Pulse Biosciences, we are driven by purpose and innovation.

* Our Mission: To build a viable Company that designs, produces, and commercializes nano-pulse technology to improve and extend the lives of patients. To solve the needs of patients, physicians, and healthcare providers with high quality and high reliability products and services, developed in accordance with rigorous scientific, engineering, and clinical standards. We exist to make a positive difference in the lives of patients, physicians, healthcare providers, shareholders and our Pulse Biosciences team members.
* Our Culture: A community of creative, forward-thinking individuals tackling challenges with ingenuity and collaboration.
* Our Commitment: Hiring the best and brightest minds to advance our world-class organization.

**What You Will Experience**

* Culture and Purpose - Purposeful and rewarding work collaborating with bright and curious minds brings us together!
* Innovative Environment - An environment that fosters innovation to take products from concept to human use quickly!
* Growth Opportunities - Learning culture focusing on professional and personal growth and development that you can only get in a startup-like environment!
* Comprehensive Benefits - A variety of health insurance plans and supplemental insurance options, and 401k retirement savings plan.
* Ownership and Rewards - Stock options awards and Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP) to share in our success.
* Work-Life Balance - Enjoy paid time off, paid holidays, flexible work schedule and wellness program, including onsite gym and mindfulness classes.
* Diversity & Inclusion - A commitment to providing a respectful work environment to our diverse workforce.

**About The Role**

The Vice President/Senior Vice President of Electrophysiology (EP) Catheter Manufacturing will lead the development, production transition, and global scale-up of a next-generation EP catheter manufacturing organization. This executive leader will be responsible for defining and executing the end-to-end manufacturing strategy, building a high-performing team, and ensuring successful commercialization through scalable, cost-effective, and reliable manufacturing operations. The ideal candidate brings deep expertise in cardiac catheter or EP device manufacturing, demonstrated success scaling production from launch to high-volume commercialization, and extensive experience managing contract manufacturers and manufacturing transfers across global regions.

**To Make An Impact, You Will**

* Develop and execute the long-term manufacturing strategy for EP catheter products from product launch through high-volume commercialization.
* Build, lead, and mentor a world-class manufacturing, operations, supply chain, and quality organization.
* Serve as the executive leader responsible for manufacturing readiness, production scale-up, operational excellence, and capacity planning.
* Partner closely with R&D, Quality, Regulatory, Clinical, and Commercial teams to support product development and market expansion.
* Define and implement a manufacturing scale-up roadmap supporting growth from approximately 50,000 units annually to 500,000+ units annually.
* Evaluate, establish, and optimize the appropriate manufacturing model, including:
* Strategic partnerships with Contract Manufacturing Organizations (CMOs)
* Hybrid manufacturing approaches
* Internal manufacturing capabilities
* Drive manufacturing process development, validation, and continuous improvement initiatives to improve efficiency, yield, and quality.
* Select, qualify, and manage global contract manufacturing partners.
* Establish robust supplier and supply chain strategies to support commercial growth and business continuity.
* Build and qualify a scalable supply network for critical components, materials, and assemblies.
* Negotiate and manage key manufacturing and supplier relationships to achieve operational, quality, and cost objectives.
* Own product cost strategy and achieve planned reductions in COGS from launch pricing to mature commercial targets.
* Drive Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, and operational excellence initiatives.
* Develop manufacturing KPIs and operating metrics to ensure predictable execution and performance.
* Lead manufacturing transfers and site expansions, including transfers between domestic and international manufacturing locations.
* Establish manufacturing capabilities that support global commercialization requirements while maintaining regulatory compliance and product quality.
* Ensure successful technology transfer, process validation, and operational readiness at receiving sites.

**To Excel, You Will Bring**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, or a related technical field; advanced degree preferred.
* 15+ years of progressive leadership experience in medical device manufacturing and operations.
* Experience at the Vice President or Senior Vice President level leading manufacturing organizations.
* Proven success scaling complex catheter-based or electrophysiology medical device manufacturing from development through high-volume commercialization.
* Demonstrated expertise in cardiac catheter, EP catheter, or related interventional medical device manufacturing.
* Direct experience with electrophysiology (EP) catheters, cardiac mapping catheters, ablation catheters, or related cardiovascular devices.
* Experience scaling manufacturing through multiple commercialization phases, including launch, growth, and mature production.
* Track record of delivering substantial COGS reductions through process optimization, automation, and supply chain strategy.
* Experience supporting commercial volumes exceeding 500,000 units annually.
* Deep knowledge of catheter manufacturing processes, assembly, automation, testing, and production scale-up.
* Significant experience managing Contract Manufacturing Organizations (CMOs) at commercial volumes.
* Proven track record developing and executing manufacturing transfer strategies, including domestic-to-international (OUS) transfers.
* Experience building global supply chains and qualifying suppliers for commercial-scale production.
* Strong understanding of medical device quality systems, process validation, and regulatory requirements.
* Strategic executive capable of building organizations and leading transformational growth.
* Strong business acumen with demonstrated success balancing cost, quality, capacity, and speed-to-market objectives.
* Exceptional cross-functional leadership and stakeholder management skills.
* Results-oriented leader with the ability to thrive in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.
* Ability to travel up to 15% of the time. Overnight and/or international travel may be required.
* Ability to lift 10-15 pounds.

**Ready to Shape the Future of Healthcare?**

Apply today to join Pulse Biosciences and help us redefine the boundaries of medicine with bioelectric innovation. To learn more about us, visit our website at www.pulsebiosciences.com.

We provide equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all persons regardless of race, age, color, gender, sexual orientation, national origin, physical or mental disability, religion, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local law. We will make reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities.

records.title: Director of Manufacturing and Quality
records.description:
Bolt Graphics is a semiconductor startup based in Sunnyvale, CA building the fastest and most efficient graphics processors. We pride ourselves on our first principles approach to solving problems. We are energized by our mission to reduce the barrier of entry for content creation and consumption. Our goal is to enable everyone to easily create, simulate and consume immersive experiences as vividly as they can imagine them.
  
  
****Our Values****

* Be Fearless: Unmute yourself. Test boundaries and get proven right.
* Remain Adaptable: Stay comfortable in a continuously changing world. If you’re wrong, concede and move on.
* Educate Your Ego: Selflessly collaborate towards our shared purpose.

**About The Role**
Reporting directly to the VP of Manufacturing Operations, the Director of Manufacturing and Quality will hold complete accountability for the global manufacturing strategy, production execution, and end-to-end quality management of Bolt’s hardware portfolio. This leadership role spans the entire product lifecycle—from early NPI (New Product Introduction) and design-for-manufacturability (DFM) reviews to high-volume mass production, factory consolidation, and field quality tracking.
  
  
The ideal candidate has a proven track record of unifying multi-site manufacturing footprints, establishing overseas extended factories (particularly in Asia), and scaling rigorous Quality Management Systems (QMS). You will lead a cross-functional team of manufacturing, test, and quality engineers to achieve world-class production yields and flawless execution.
  
  
**What You'll Do**
****Global Manufacturing Strategy & Execution****

* Production Footprint Optimization: Architect and execute the global manufacturing strategy, including the optimization of domestic facilities and the successful launch and stabilization of overseas extended factories.
* NPI to Mass Production Scaling: Drive the seamless operational handoff of complex hardware products from design engineering into high-volume manufacturing. Establish robust New Product Introduction (NPI) playbooks.
* Capacity & Efficiency Optimization: Drive line balancing, automation initiatives, and factory layout designs to optimize throughput, maximize capital expenditure efficiency, and reduce cycle times.
* Vendor & CM Operations: Manage technical execution at tier-1 Contract Manufacturers (CMs) and ODMs. Partner with Supply Chain to hold vendors accountable to strict operational SLAs.

****End-to-End Quality Engineering & Compliance****

* QMS Leadership: Own, scale, and continuous improve Bolt’s global Quality Management System (QMS) across all manufacturing sites and external partners, ensuring compliance with relevant international standards.
* Advanced Quality Planning: Embed Design for Manufacturability, Assembly, and Test (DFM/DFA/DFT) early in the product development cycle. Implement robust PFMEA (Process Failure Mode and Effects Analysis) and control plans at all factory levels.
* Yield & Reliability Maximization: Drive rigorous statistical process control (SPC) on the factory floor. Analyze complex test data to root-cause and eliminate component-level, PCBA-level, and system-level failures.
* Closed-Loop Corrective Action: Lead global failure analysis (FA) and Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) processes for manufacturing escapes and field returns, ensuring engineering feedback loops are closed instantly.

****Team Leadership & Executive Advisory****

* Organizational Scaling: Build, mentor, and lead a high-performing international team of Manufacturing, Test, and Supplier Quality Engineers.
* Executive Metrics Dashboard: Define, track, and regularly report on mission-critical operational metrics (First Pass Yield, Cost of Poor Quality, OEE, Scrap Rate, and Field Defect Rates) to the VP of Operations and the executive leadership team.

**Qualifications**

* 10+ years of progressive leadership experience in hardware manufacturing operations, NPI, and quality engineering within high-tech electronics, compute hardware, or complex electromechanical industries.

**Proven Delivery Track Record**

* Direct experience establishing and scaling overseas manufacturing facilities/extended factories (particularly in Taiwan, China, or Southeast Asia) and managing Tier-1 EMS/CM partners.

**Technical Depth**

* Deep understanding of both Electrical fabrication (SMT lines, PCBA testing, ICT/FCT fixtures, thermal management) and Mechanical processes (precision machining, die-casting, custom tooling, injection molding).

**Quality Methodologies**

* Expert knowledge of advanced quality tools (Six Sigma Black Belt preferred, Lean Manufacturing, SPC, 8D problem solving, FMEA, Gauge R&R).
* System Familiarity: Extensive experience utilizing PLM (e.g., Arena, Agile), ERP, and manufacturing execution systems (MES) to drive process discipline.

**Education**

* Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or a related technical discipline. An MS in Engineering or an MBA is highly desirable.

**Travel**

* Ability to travel globally (up to 30-40%) to domestic facilities and international manufacturing sites to lead factory bring-ups, line audits, and critical business reviews.
* Targeting cross-functional team scaling, standard setting, and unifying overseas extended factories.

**Unifying Global Quality Culture**

* "When scaling an operational footprint that includes both domestic facilities and overseas extended factories in Asia, a disconnect in quality culture often emerges. How do you instill a unified, proactive quality mindset across geographically separated teams so that local operators and remote contract manufacturers take joint ownership of quality standards rather than treating them as a checkbox exercise?"

**Developing & Mentoring Specialized Engineers**

* "Manufacturing, Test, and Supplier Quality Engineering require vastly different technical skillsets. How do you approach building out a career progression track and mentoring framework for these distinct functions? Can you give an example of how you coached a junior engineer to effectively stand their ground during an aggressive yield dispute with a tier-1 global ODM?"

**Managing Cross-Functional Friction (Engineering Vs. Operations)**

* "During a high-stakes New Product Introduction (NPI) phase, Design Engineering often pushes to relax manufacturing line requirements to hit functional deadlines, while Quality/Operations must protect factory yields and long-term reliability. Describe your personal framework for navigating this friction, managing stakeholder expectations, and ensuring team psychological safety when hard boundary lines must be drawn."

**Fostering Accountability Across Time Zones**

* "Building a high-performing international operations team means managing personnel across extreme time zone differences (US and Asia). How do you design operational handoffs, communication structures, and team habits to ensure overseas engineers feel fully integrated, empowered, and accountable—rather than feeling like a disconnected 'night shift' executing directives?"

**Driving a Zero-Defect/Continuous Improvement Mindset**

* "When a catastrophic manufacturing escape or field failure occurs, human nature leads to finger-pointing. How do you cultivate a blameless post-mortem culture focused on systematic Root Cause and Corrective Action (CAPA/8D) while still maintaining a high-performance bar for operational accountability?"

****Compensation Range:****
$200,000–$250,000 per year (California). This range represents the anticipated base pay for this role; the final offer may vary based on qualifications, experience, and location.
  
  
**Benefits**

* Medical, Dental, & Vision - 100% covered premiums
* Equity - Stock Options
* 401(k) match
* WFH Hardware Reimbursement

Maker’s Pride is seeking a proven, enterprise-minded Plant Director to lead our largest manufacturing facility in McComb, Ohio, a site of more than 1,600 Team Members that is critical to the success of our business. The Plant Director holds full accountability for the safety, quality, service, cost, and people performance of a large-scale co-manufacturing operation, and serves as the senior leader on site and the face of the plant to customers, Team Members, and the community.
  
  
This role requires a seasoned operations executive who has led large, complex plants of 1,000+ Team Members, can build and develop a strong leadership bench, and can balance day-to-day execution with long-term strategy. The Plant Director partners closely with senior leadership and corporate functions to deliver the plant’s operating plan, drive operational excellence, and position McComb for sustained growth.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**

* Operational Leadership: Lead all plant operations, including production, packaging, maintenance, engineering, quality, warehouse, and supply chain, to consistently deliver safety, quality, service, and cost targets across multiple shifts and lines.
* P&L and Financial Accountability: Own the plant’s operating plan, budget, and financial performance, including labor, overtime, yield, waste, and capital spend. Identify and execute cost-reduction and margin-improvement opportunities.
* Strategic Planning: Develop and execute a multi-year plant strategy aligned to enterprise goals, covering capacity, capital investment, automation, new business onboarding, and talent.
* Production Planning and Capacity: Partner with Supply Chain, Planning, and Customer teams to build production schedules and resource plans that optimize throughput, labor utilization, and on-time, in-full performance.

Drive staffing stability, reduce turnover, manage overtime effectively, and foster positive Team Member and labor relations, including compliance with applicable employment and labor laws and agreements.

records.description:
Please review the job details below.
  
  
Intuitive Machines - West is currently seeking a courageous, innovative, multi-skilled Director of High-Rate AIT Production to join our spacecraft production team in Palo Alto, CA.
  
  
**Life with Us**
Your Project: Intuitive Machines is a world leader in high-power spacecraft, having delivered some of the largest and highest-power spacecraft in the world. We are now looking to take this legacy of excellence to the next level, architecting a high-volume production line to build a large number of advanced spacecraft.
  
  
In this role, you will architect and implement a high-volume assembly, integration, and test (AIT) production line for these next-generation vehicles. You will be responsible for transforming our AIT operations from low-rate to high-rate production, establishing scalable processes and organizational capabilities to support our ambitious production targets. The scope includes complete spacecraft AIT from component receipt through final acceptance testing, encompassing electrical systems integration, solar array integration with the spacecraft bus, battery integration, advanced thermal solutions, and comprehensive environmental testing at production scale.
  
  
A critical aspect of this role is developing an efficient, right-sized test program—one that provides high confidence the vehicles will perform as designed while eliminating non-value-added test activities that add cost and schedule without commensurate risk reduction. You will apply rigorous engineering judgment to distinguish between essential verification activities and legacy testing practices that may not be necessary for production-rate vehicles.
  
  
We are looking for leaders to bravely challenge conventional AIT approaches and establish production-rate processes for these advanced systems. You will play an essential role in applying design-for-manufacturing/design-for-test (DFM/DFT) principles to develop AIT specifications and manufacturing plans suitable for volume production. Additionally, you will represent AIT capabilities during customer proposal efforts, providing technical credibility and instilling confidence in our ability to execute high-volume production of complex spacecraft.
  
  
Your Career: We're very serious about professional development and continuing education at Intuitive Machines - West. We offer our team members the opportunity to define their own career trajectory. You will work with your manager to set goals and design a development plan to advance your career. This unique opportunity is a high-visibility role critical to our company's leadership position in spacecraft manufacturing.
  
  
What We Offer: Time for dedicated professional development, conference attendance, industry training, peer group collaboration, as well as paid certifications and education reimbursement.
  
  
Who you will work with: You will report to the VP of Spacecraft Production and Operations and collaborate closely with Engineering, Quality, and Supply Chain teams. You will lead a team of AIT production engineers and technicians while partnering with design engineering to ensure producibility of our spacecraft systems. You will also engage directly with potential customers during proposal phases to communicate our production and test capabilities.
  
  
**Your Responsibilities**

* Design end-to-end AIT production flow optimized for high-volume throughput
* Develop capacity models, takt time analysis, and process flow requirements for production-rate AIT
* Define capital equipment strategy including test equipment, handling systems, and tooling
* Establish scalable AIT work instructions, process controls, and quality gates
* Lead development of an efficient, risk-informed test program that ensures vehicle performance confidence while eliminating non-value-added testing
* Oversee spacecraft-level integration of solar arrays, batteries, and other major subsystems with the spacecraft bus
* Implement manufacturing execution systems (MES) tailored to provide assembly process documentation and production tracking for volume spacecraft production
* Define requirements for low-cost mechanical and electrical assembly, integration and test equipment, and production tooling
* Lead Voice of Manufacturing inputs to spacecraft design to ensure producibility at scale
* Drive continuous improvement initiatives leveraging lean manufacturing principles
* Build and mentor AIT production engineering team
* Represent AIT production capabilities to potential customers during proposal efforts, providing technical credibility on execution readiness
* Support business development with AIT cost models and production capacity commitments

**How You Will Be Evaluated**
Your performance will be measured against AIT production readiness milestones, test program efficiency metrics, production ramp targets, quality metrics, and cost per unit objectives.
  
  
**What We Look For In Team Members**
As a team member at Intuitive Machines - West, we expect you to demonstrate honesty, integrity, innovation, collaboration, and a commitment to excellence.
  
  
**Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering or related technical field. Four additional years of experience may be substituted for a degree
* Minimum of 15 years related aerospace manufacturing/AIT experience
* Minimum of 7 years leadership experience in production or manufacturing engineering
* Experience working cross-functionally within a company and/or with external partners and contractors
* Proven track record scaling aerospace production operations
* Ability to travel domestically and internationally

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience with volume production of spacecraft or complex aerospace systems
* Direct experience developing and implementing a spacecraft AIT production line
* Experience with large spacecraft systems (solar array integration, battery integration, high-voltage testing)
* Demonstrated experience developing efficient, risk-based test programs that balance verification rigor with schedule/cost efficiency
* Understanding of spacecraft environmental testing at production scale (thermal vacuum, vibration, EMI/EMC)
* Prior history as an AIT engineer, process engineer, or industrial engineer for aerospace products
* Experience with sustaining engineering processes such as Change Approval, NPI, breakpointing
* Advanced degree in a technical field
* Lean/Six Sigma certification
* Experience with AS9100 quality systems
* Capital project management experience (multi-million dollar equipment investments)
* Experience taking spacecraft products into production, including progressive design iterations to reduce delivered cost
* Demonstrated experience applying system engineering practices to AIT operations
* Excellent communication and presentation skills, with experience engaging directly with customers in technical/proposal settings
* Experience working directly with customers in the commercial space industry
* Ability to work independently with a high degree of organization and attention to detail

records.description:
**Director, Manufacturing Operations (Bulking)**

**Direct Hire**

**Onsite - Windsor, CO**

**Position Summary**

The Director, Manufacturing Operations (Bulking) provides leadership and accountability for sterile and non-sterile bulking operations within a regulated pharmaceutical manufacturing environment. This role is responsible for safe, compliant, reliable, and efficient execution of manufacturing activities, including production performance, product quality, process reliability, workforce capability, operational excellence, and continuous improvement.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead day-to-day bulking operations across multiple products, processes, and shifts.
* Ensure production schedules are executed safely, compliantly, and efficiently while meeting business and customer commitments.
* Drive performance across safety, quality, delivery, cost, capacity, yield, cycle time, right-first-time, and equipment reliability metrics.
* Establish operating standards, performance management routines, and accountability systems across the organization.
* Partner with Quality, Engineering, Maintenance, MS&T, Validation, Supply Chain, and Regulatory teams to improve process performance, resolve operational challenges, and support strategic objectives.
* Provide leadership for deviations, investigations, CAPAs, change controls, audits, inspections, and regulatory compliance activities.
* Support technology transfers, process scale-up, validation, equipment qualification, automation initiatives, and implementation of new manufacturing technologies.
* Develop managers, supervisors, technical specialists, and manufacturing teams while building organizational capability and succession pipelines.
* Lead Lean, Six Sigma, standard work, and continuous improvement initiatives to improve reliability, reduce variability, and increase operational efficiency.
* Manage operating budgets, capital investments, staffing plans, and resource allocation while supporting future growth and capacity requirements.

**Knowledge, Skills & Abilities**

* Strong knowledge of pharmaceutical manufacturing operations, including aseptic processing, contamination control, and cGMP requirements.
* Ability to lead a diverse portfolio of complex manufacturing processes while establishing consistent standards across products, teams, and shifts.
* Demonstrated success leading and developing managers and frontline teams in a regulated manufacturing environment.
* Strong understanding of process control, equipment reliability, validation, technology transfer, and manufacturing scale-up.
* Ability to interpret production, quality, capacity, and financial data and translate it into clear priorities and executable plans.
* Proficiency in risk assessment, root cause analysis, deviation investigation, CAPA, and change management.
* Track record of improving safety, quality, delivery, cost, workforce capability, and operational performance through disciplined execution.
* Strong judgment and decision-making skills, including the ability to balance patient safety, compliance, supply, and business needs.
* Effective communicator with the ability to influence senior leaders, technical partners, and frontline teams and represent Manufacturing during audits and inspections.
* Proven ability to lead cross-functional work with Quality, Engineering, Maintenance, MS&T, Validation, Supply Chain, and Regulatory partners.
* Working knowledge of Lean, Six Sigma, tiered management, standard work, or comparable continuous improvement systems.
* Strategic, hands-on, and adaptable leadership style suited to a fast-paced environment with changing priorities.

**Education & Experience**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Biological Sciences, Chemistry, Pharmaceutical Sciences, or another STEM discipline required; advanced degree preferred.
* 10+ years of progressive experience in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical device, or similarly regulated manufacturing environments, including significant production operations leadership experience.
* Significant experience in sterile or aseptic manufacturing operations required; experience with formulation, compounding, bulking, filling, or related processing strongly preferred.
* 5+ years of people leadership experience, including leadership of leaders and/or multi-shift manufacturing teams.
* Demonstrated success improving operational performance, building workforce capability, and leading cross-functional change in a regulated environment.

records.title: Operations Director
records.description:
**Company Background and Summary**

Votaw Precision Technologies is a trusted leader in the manufacturing of complex precision components, assemblies, and systems for the aerospace, defense, and industrial sectors. With a strong reputation for technical excellence, quality craftsmanship, and on-time delivery, Votaw supports some of the world’s most demanding programs through its advanced manufacturing capabilities. The company specializes in precision machining, fabrication, welding, and complex assembly operations for mission-critical applications. Votaw Precision Technologies has long been a trusted partner in building mission-critical hardware for some of the most advanced aerospace and defense programs in the world. Our precision components support the International Space Station, nearly every major launch vehicle in operation, high-performance spacecraft (including classified missions), as well as next-generation fighter aircraft, bombers, submarines, radar systems, and ground vehicles.

We are seeking an experienced and highly knowledgeable Operations Director to lead the overall operations of a high-performance CNC machine shop. This individual will have full responsibility for the day-to-day management, technical excellence, production performance, staffing, scheduling, efficiency, and continuous improvement of the facility.

The ideal candidate is a seasoned machining professional with approximately 20 years of industry experience who understands metal cutting and CNC machining at a deep technical level and has progressed into a strong operational leadership role.

The Operations Director must be able to walk onto the shop floor, understand the machining challenges, evaluate processes, communicate effectively with machinists and programmers, identify inefficiencies, and make sound technical and operational decisions. The company utilizes a variety of CNC machining technologies, including 3-axis, 4-axis, and 5-axis machining, as well as vertical milling, welding and large-scale assembly tooling.

**Essential Functions**

* Responsible for ensuring that the entire organization operates safely, efficiently, profitably, and to the highest standards of quality and technical excellence.
* Have overall responsibility for the day-to-day operations of the CNC machine shop.
* Establish and maintain a culture of technical excellence, accountability, safety, quality, and continuous improvement.
* Provide leadership and direction to machining, programming, production, quality, maintenance, and other shop personnel.
* Ensure the shop has the appropriate personnel, equipment, tooling, processes, and resources to meet customer requirements.
* Establish clear expectations for supervisors, leads, machinists, programmers, and support personnel.
* Serve as the primary operational leader and decision maker for the manufacturing facility.
* Work closely with programmers, machinists, and engineers to resolve technical machining issues.
* Evaluate machining processes and identify opportunities to improve cycle time, tool life, throughput, and quality.
* Ensure manufacturing processes are technically sound, repeatable, and scalable.
* Provide technical guidance when difficult or complex machining problems arise.
* Maintain an environment where machinists, engineers, programmers continuously improve their technical capabilities.
* Responsible for weld shop, tooling assembly, and manufacturing readiness team.

**Qualifications and Skills**

* Approximately 20 years of experience in the CNC machining/manufacturing industry.
* Previous experience as a Shop Manager, Manufacturing Manager, Operations Manager, Plant Manager, Production Manager, or Director of Operations.
* Experience managing multiple shifts and 24/7 operations
* Knowledge of complex, tight-tolerance, or high-value machined components.
* Experience with 5-axis machining and advanced CNC manufacturing.
* Implementing Lean Manufacturing or continuous-improvement initiatives.
* Knowledge of ERP/MRP and production scheduling systems.
* Managing capital equipment purchases and machine capacity planning.
* Experience in aerospace, defense, medical, automotive, or other high-precision manufacturing environments is a plus.

**Personal Attributes**

* Highly self-motivated and directed.
* Keen attention to detail.
* Ability to effectively prioritize and execute tasks in a high-pressure environment.
* Ability to work both independently and in a team-oriented, collaborative environment.

**Work Conditions**

* Ability to work onsite, including hours outside of a normal working day, to meet critical deadlines.
* This position operates within a precision manufacturing environment supporting the production of mission-critical aerospace and defense components. Success requires a high sense of urgency, attention to detail, proactive problem-solving, and the ability to coordinate effectively across multiple departments to ensure uninterrupted manufacturing operations and customer delivery commitments.
* Ability to work safely in a manufacturing environment, including walking the production floor, climbing stairs or ladders, occasionally lifting up to 25 pounds, and wearing required personal protective equipment (PPE).

**Additional Requirements**

* This position requires the use of information or access to hardware subject to the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR). All applicants must be U.S. persons as defined by ITAR.

***Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge, skills, education, and experience.***

***Votaw Precision Technologies, LLC is an Equal Opportunity Employer including Disability/Vets.***

records.title: Director of Operations
records.description:
**Spartronics, LLC**

**Career Opportunity: Site Director of Operations**

**Location:**
North Logan, Utah

**Employment Type:**
Full-Time | Salaried | Exempt

**Work Arrangement:**
On-Site

**Schedule:**
Full-Time, Monday–Friday

**Reports To:**
Vice President of Operations – West / Logan Site Leader

**Who We Are**

At
**Spartronics**
, we build more than electronics. We build the technology that powers critical applications across aerospace and defense, medical devices, life sciences, and industrial markets.

As a leading provider of electronic manufacturing services (EMS), Spartronics specializes in complex, high-reliability products, including printed circuit board assemblies (PCBA), electromechanical assemblies, integrated systems, and complete product manufacturing solutions.

**Career Opportunity: Director of Operations**

Spartronics is seeking an experienced
**Director of Operations**
to lead manufacturing operations and drive operational excellence at our North Logan, Utah facility.

This senior leadership position is responsible for the overall performance, execution, and continuous improvement of the site's operational functions, including Manufacturing, Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, and Materials Planning, while providing indirect operational oversight and cross-functional partnership with Program Management.

Reporting to the Vice President of Operations – West / Logan Site Leader, the Director of Operations will establish operational priorities, develop high-performing teams, optimize manufacturing processes, and ensure the organization consistently achieves its safety, quality, delivery, cost, productivity, and profitability objectives.

The ideal candidate is a hands-on manufacturing leader with strong business acumen, experience managing multiple operational disciplines, and a proven ability to drive results in complex, highly regulated manufacturing environments.

**What You Will Do**

* Provide strategic direction and operational leadership for the facility, translating organizational objectives into actionable plans, performance expectations, and measurable results.
* Direct Manufacturing, Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, and Materials Planning functions, ensuring effective coordination, accountability, and alignment with site and corporate objectives.
* Provide indirect operational oversight and strategic partnership to Program Management, ensuring alignment between customer requirements, program execution, operational capacity and business objectives.
* Direct manufacturing operations, production planning, capacity management, and resource allocation, balancing changing customer demand, product complexity, and manufacturing constraints to achieve safety, quality, delivery, cost, and productivity objectives.
* Establish operational priorities, evaluate performance against key metrics, and implement corrective actions to address performance gaps and emerging risks.
* Provide leadership and oversight of engineering activities, including process optimization, technical problem resolution, manufacturing readiness, new product introduction, and product transfers.
* Ensure the effectiveness of quality management systems, regulatory compliance, product conformity, and corrective and preventive action processes while preserving Quality's independent authority over product acceptance and compliance decisions.
* Oversee supply chain and materials planning activities, including procurement, supplier performance, inventory management, material availability, and production support.
* Partner with Program Management and other customer-facing functions to address delivery commitments, operational concerns, customer escalations, and changing business requirements.
* Develop operational budgets, resource plans, capital expenditure priorities, and cost improvement initiatives in collaboration with Finance, supporting achievement of site financial objectives and profitability targets..
* Evaluate operational and financial performance, identifying opportunities to improve profitability, reduce waste, control costs, and optimize resource utilization.
* Lead continuous improvement initiatives utilizing Lean manufacturing, Six Sigma, root cause analysis, and other structured problem-solving methodologies.
* Ensure manufacturing processes, product traceability, configuration and change control, and supporting documentation comply with applicable customer, industry, regulatory, and company requirements.
* Promote a strong safety culture and ensure operational compliance with applicable environmental, health, and safety requirements.
* Establish and maintain structured operational performance management systems, including KPI reviews, cross-functional accountability, issue escalation, and corrective action follow-through to support timely, data-driven decision-making.
* Build, coach, and develop operational leadership teams, establishing clear performance expectations, succession plans, and workforce competency and development priorities.
* Collaborate with Human Resources on workforce planning, staffing requirements, employee performance, organizational development, and retention strategies.
* Coordinate with Facilities, Security, and other support functions to address infrastructure needs, operational continuity, physical security requirements, and business risks.
* Evaluate manufacturing capacity, technology, equipment, and infrastructure needs to support business growth, operational scalability, and capital investment decisions.
* Identify and mitigate operational risks associated with production disruptions, supplier constraints, quality concerns, regulatory requirements, and customer commitments.
* Represent site operations in corporate leadership discussions, customer interactions, audits, and strategic planning activities, communicating performance, priorities, and resource requirements.
* Perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned to support organizational objectives.

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations Management, Business Administration, or a related discipline; an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience may be considered.
* Minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible experience in manufacturing operations, including at least five years in a senior leadership capacity overseeing multiple operational functions.
* Demonstrated experience leading complex manufacturing operations with accountability for production, engineering, quality, supply chain, and cross-functional business objectives.
* Strong understanding of manufacturing operations, production planning, capacity management, materials management, and operational performance improvement.
* Demonstrated knowledge of manufacturing engineering principles, process controls, technical problem resolution, and new product introduction activities.
* Working knowledge of quality management systems, regulatory compliance, product conformity, corrective action processes, and applicable manufacturing standards.
* Proven ability to develop and execute operational strategies, establish performance objectives, and achieve measurable improvements in quality, delivery, cost, and productivity.
* Strong business and financial acumen, including experience utilizing financial metrics, cost management practices, capital planning processes, and profitability analysis to drive operational decision-making.
* Demonstrated ability to lead, develop, and hold accountable cross-functional management teams while promoting collaboration and organizational effectiveness.
* Experience applying Lean manufacturing, continuous improvement, and structured problem-solving methodologies to complex operational challenges.
* Strong analytical, organizational, and decision-making skills, with the ability to evaluate competing priorities, manage operational risks, and resolve complex business issues.
* Advanced proficiency with business and manufacturing information systems, including ERP/MRP platforms, Microsoft Office applications, and data analysis and reporting tools. Demonstrated ability to interpret operational and financial data, evaluate performance trends, and leverage technology to support strategic planning and informed decision-making.
* Excellent written and verbal communication, interpersonal, negotiation, and presentation skills, including the ability to communicate effectively with employees, senior leadership, customers, and external stakeholders.
* Ability to manage sensitive business information, exercise sound judgment, and maintain confidentiality in accordance with company and applicable security requirements.
* Ability to read, write, speak, and comprehend English sufficiently to interpret technical documentation, communicate operational requirements, and perform essential job responsibilities.
* Ability to work full-time on-site at the assigned company facility in Logan, UT.

**Security Clearance Requirement**

Candidates must possess current, verifiable eligibility for a U.S. Government Secret-level security clearance or be willing and able to complete the necessary documentation to initiate the company-sponsored clearance process within 60 days of hire. The ability to obtain and maintain the required security clearance eligibility is a continuing condition of employment. Employment may continue while an appropriately initiated clearance application is pending, subject to company authorization and applicable security restrictions. A final determination of ineligibility, denial, or loss of required clearance eligibility will result in disqualification from the position and may result in termination of employment, subject to applicable law and company policy.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Master's degree in Engineering, Operations Management, Business Administration, or a related discipline.
* Leadership experience within electronics manufacturing services (EMS), printed circuit board assembly (PCBA), or high-mix, low-volume manufacturing environments.
* Experience with surface mount technology (SMT), through-hole assembly, electromechanical assembly, manufacturing test, and related electronics manufacturing processes.
* Experience supporting aerospace, defense, medical device, or other highly regulated manufacturing industries.
* Familiarity with AS9100, ISO 9001, ISO 13485, applicable IPC standards, and customer-specific quality requirements.
* Knowledge of ITAR, controlled technical information, and security requirements applicable to defense-related manufacturing.
* Lean Six Sigma certification or other recognized continuous improvement credentials.
* APICS/ASCM certification, such as CPIM or CSCP, or equivalent supply chain management credentials.
* Experience leading operational transformations, facility expansions, production transfers, or significant manufacturing improvement initiatives.
* Experience utilizing business intelligence platforms, advanced reporting tools, and integrated manufacturing systems to monitor operational performance and support continuous improvement initiatives.
* Demonstrated success managing complex customer relationships, operational escalations, and cross-functional business challenges.

**Key Metrics and Focus Areas**

* Workplace safety performance and regulatory compliance.
* On-time delivery performance and production schedule attainment.
* Manufacturing efficiency, throughput, and capacity utilization.
* Product quality, first-pass yield, and cost of poor quality.
* Inventory accuracy, material availability, and inventory turns.
* Supplier delivery, quality, and overall performance.
* Operating cost performance, budget adherence, and profitability.
* Engineering responsiveness, manufacturing readiness, and successful new product introductions.
* Program execution support and fulfillment of customer commitments.
* Continuous improvement results, waste reduction, and operational efficiency.
* Quality management system effectiveness, audit performance, and corrective action closure.
* Workforce productivity, employee development, retention, and leadership effectiveness.
* Operational risk management, business continuity, and capacity readiness.

**Why This Role Matters**

As
**Director of Operations,**
you will play a critical role in shaping the performance, operational capabilities, and continued growth of our North Logan manufacturing facility. Your leadership will directly influence how effectively we deliver complex, high-reliability electronic products to customers operating in some of the world's most demanding industries. This is an opportunity to lead talented teams, strengthen operational performance, implement meaningful improvements, and contribute to the long-term success of a growing manufacturing organization.

**Benefits – Why Join Spartronics?**

At Spartronics, we recognize that our employees are essential to our success. We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support the health, financial well-being, and professional development of our team members.

Benefits may include:

* Medical, dental, and vision insurance.
* 401(k) retirement savings plan.
* Paid time off and company-paid holidays.
* Company-paid life insurance and disability benefits.
* Employee assistance and wellness resources.
* Professional development and career growth opportunities.
* Opportunities to contribute to innovative products supporting mission-critical industries.

*Specific benefits and eligibility are subject to applicable plan documents and company policies.*

**Physical Requirements and Work Location**

* Ability to work in both office and manufacturing environments, including regular movement throughout production, warehouse, and operational areas.
* Ability to sit, stand, and walk for extended periods, with occasional bending and reaching.
* Ability to occasionally lift, carry, or move materials weighing up to 25 pounds.
* Ability to operate computers and standard office equipment.
* Ability to wear required personal protective equipment when entering designated manufacturing areas.
* Ability to perform the essential functions of the position, with or without reasonable accommodation.

**Work Authorization & ITAR Requirements**

Due to the nature of certain products, technologies, and customer requirements, this position may involve access to export-controlled technical data or defense-related information subject to the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) and other applicable export control laws. Candidates must meet applicable U.S. export control authorization requirements and be eligible to access controlled technical information as required by the position. For this position, additional U.S. Government security clearance eligibility requirements apply, as described above.

**Equal Employment Opportunity**

*Spartronics is an Equal Opportunity Employer/Veteran/Disabled 41 CFR 60-1.4. We comply with federal Affirmative Action guidelines in all employment opportunities for qualified employees and applicants.Employment at Spartronics is considered at-will, meaning that either the employee or Spartronics may terminate the employment relationship at any time, with or without cause, and with or without prior notification.*

records.description:
**Description**
**THE COMPANY**
For over 40 years, Aero Simulation, Inc. (ASI) has provided quality flight training devices to the US Military. ASI has successfully built numerous training systems with a primary focus on aircrew and maintenance training systems. Our current programs include, but are not limited to, the B-1 Training Systems (Air Force), E-2D Training Systems (Navy), CH-53E Training Devices (USMC), IMOMS (Coast Guard), Navigation, Seamanship, Shiphandling Trainer – NSST (Navy). To learn more about ASI visit Programs- Aero Simulation, Inc.
  
  
ASI is a 100% employee-owned engineering and manufacturing company committed to supporting the nation’s warfighters. Being 100% employee-owned directly impacts our culture: it drives our decision-making, motivates our teams, increases our productivity, improves retention and contributes to the future success of our company. Our culture is one where we work hard for our clients and for each other – and we have fun collaborating, sharing experience and expertise, and learning along the way. We strive to deliver exceptional quality, elevate client relationships, and enrich the careers and lives of our employee-owners. As Employee-Owners, we are invested in the success and continued development of each other and the company.
  
  
In addition to the Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP), we offer a flexible work environment, generous paid time off, professional development opportunities, industry competitive compensation, and superior benefits to include medical, dental, 401k and more!
  
  
ASI is a great place to build a career and grow with a company that is dedicated to quality, service and to fostering a community of support for each and every member of the team. To learn more about this opportunity, keep reading!
  
  
**Position Summary**
ASI is seeking an experienced, results-driven Director of Production to provide strategic leadership and operational oversight of its production organization. This is a key senior leadership position responsible for ensuring the successful manufacturing, assembly, integration, and delivery of ASI's advanced simulation and military training device hardware.
  
  
Based in Tampa, Florida, and reporting directly to the Chief Operating Officer (COO), the Director of Production will oversee Production Control, Material Control, and Manufacturing through functional managers and department leads. The position will also provide executive oversight of Facility Management and Workplace Safety through the Facilities Manager.
  
  
The successful candidate will bring demonstrated experience leading complex manufacturing operations, developing high-performing teams, managing production capacity and resources, and delivering technical products in demanding, schedule-driven environments.
  
  
This individual will play an important role in supporting ASI's Department of Defense, U.S. military, government agency, and defense industry programs while ensuring the organization is positioned to support new business opportunities and long-term growth.
  
  
**Essential Duties And Responsibilities**
*Strategic Leadership & Operational Management*

* Provide strategic direction and operational leadership for Production Control, Material Control, and Manufacturing.
* Establish production priorities, performance expectations, resource requirements, and organizational objectives.
* Lead through functional managers, promoting accountability, operational discipline, and effective execution.
* Ensure production operations consistently meet contractual commitments, customer requirements, program milestones, and delivery schedules.
* Partner with executive leadership to develop operational strategies supporting current programs and future business growth.
* Establish and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) to measure organizational effectiveness and drive improvement.

*Production Planning & Program Execution*

* Oversee production planning, scheduling, capacity management, and resource allocation across multiple concurrent programs.
* Partner with Program Management and Engineering to translate contractual requirements and technical specifications into executable production plans.
* Ensure production readiness, including personnel, materials, equipment, facilities, documentation, and approved manufacturing processes.
* Identify and mitigate production risks that could impact cost, schedule, quality, or customer delivery.
* Support program reviews, production readiness assessments, customer meetings, and government inspections.
* Provide production estimates, labor forecasts, capacity assessments, and schedule inputs for new business proposals.

*Manufacturing & Systems Integration*

* Oversee the manufacturing and assembly of complex simulation and training device hardware.
* Ensure effective collaboration between Production and Engineering to promote manufacturability, reliability, and cost-effective designs.
* Support the integration of major simulation hardware components, including visual display systems, motion platforms, and associated subsystems.
* Ensure manufacturing activities follow approved engineering drawings, Bills of Materials (BOMs), configuration requirements, and engineering change processes.
* Drive improvements in production flow, manufacturing efficiency, product quality, and delivery performance.

*Workforce Leadership & Development*

* Lead, mentor, and develop production managers, supervisors, manufacturing engineers, technicians, assemblers, and integration personnel.
* Establish clear performance expectations and accountability standards for functional managers.
* Develop staffing and workforce plans to support current and anticipated production requirements.
* Identify workforce development needs and implement appropriate training and cross-training initiatives.
* Build organizational depth through succession planning, leadership development, and employee engagement.
* Foster a culture centered on safety, quality, teamwork, accountability, and continuous improvement.

*Materials Management & Supply Chain Coordination*

* Ensure effective coordination between Production and Procurement to maintain material availability and support production schedules.
* Monitor material shortages, supplier performance, inventory levels, and long-lead procurement requirements.
* Establish appropriate material priorities based on program schedules and contractual commitments.
* Ensure effective inventory management, material traceability, and control of customer-furnished and government-furnished property.
* Promote accurate material tracking and accountability through ASI's ERP system.

*Quality & Regulatory Compliance*

* Ensure production operations comply with ASI's ISO 9001:2015 Quality Management System and applicable contractual, customer, government, and regulatory requirements.
* Partner with Quality Assurance to address nonconformances, corrective actions, root-cause analysis, and process improvements.
* Maintain effective production documentation, inspection records, test results, and configuration records.
* Support government quality audits, customer surveillance activities, and acceptance inspections.
* Promote a culture of quality and adherence to approved manufacturing processes throughout the production organization.

*Budget, Cost Control & Performance*

* Develop and manage production budgets, labor forecasts, and operational resource plans.
* Monitor production costs, labor utilization, productivity, rework, and overhead.
* Identify opportunities to improve manufacturing efficiency, reduce waste, and increase production throughput.
* Evaluate production capacity and capital equipment requirements.
* Provide regular operational and financial performance reporting to the COO and executive leadership.
* Support long-term resource planning and investment strategies aligned with anticipated business growth.

*Facility Management & Workplace Safety*

* Provide executive oversight of Facility Management and Workplace Safety through the Facilities Manager.
* Establish strategic priorities for facility readiness, infrastructure reliability, maintenance, and workplace safety.
* Ensure facilities, equipment, and infrastructure adequately support current production requirements and future growth.
* Review facility performance, safety metrics, significant incidents, and corrective actions.
* Coordinate facility investment, capital requirements, and infrastructure planning with the Facilities Manager and COO.
* Promote a safe, organized, and efficient working environment.

*Continuous Improvement*

* Implement Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, 5S, and other operational excellence methodologies, as appropriate.
* Establish consistent production management practices, standard operating procedures, and performance measures.
* Identify opportunities to reduce cycle times, eliminate waste, improve first-pass yield, and increase productivity.
* Drive corrective and preventive actions to resolve recurring operational issues.
* Promote employee engagement, proactive problem-solving, and continuous

**LEADERSHIP EXPECTATIONS**

* Provides leadership and direct supervision of Group Leaders responsible for Manufacturing, Facility Management, Production Control, Workplace Safety, and Stockroom operations, establishing priorities, expectations, and accountability for operational performance, quality, efficiency, safety, and on-time delivery.
* The Director maintains oversight of these functional areas while ensuring alignment with program requirements and organizational objectives. Ensures teams have the resources, processes, equipment, capabilities, and organizational support necessary to maintain safe and efficient operations, support successful program execution, and meet production schedules and contractual commitments.

**Requirements**
**EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS**

* 10–15 years of progressive experience in manufacturing, production, or operations management.
* At least 5 years of leadership experience managing production teams, functional managers, and complex manufacturing operations.
* Proven experience overseeing the manufacturing, assembly, integration, and delivery of complex technical products.
* Demonstrated ability to manage production schedules, labor resources, materials, budgets, capacity, and contractual delivery commitments.
* Strong understanding of manufacturing processes, production planning, quality management systems, and operational performance metrics.
* Demonstrated ability to manage competing priorities and drive accountability across multiple functional organizations.
* Excellent leadership, communication, organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
* Working knowledge of facility operations, infrastructure, and workplace safety requirements.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience in aerospace, defense, aviation, flight simulation, military training systems, or related industries.
* Experience supporting U.S. Department of Defense programs, military customers, or defense prime contractors.
* Experience with complex electromechanical systems and hardware/software integration.
* Familiarity with ISO 9001, Lean Manufacturing, and Six Sigma principles.
* Experience with ERP/MRP systems, production planning tools, and manufacturing performance reporting.
* Familiarity with government contracting, DoD Manufacturing Planning (MIL-HDBK-896), configuration management, and Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT).
* Experience managing multiple concurrent production programs.
* Experience providing executive oversight of facility management, infrastructure planning, capital equipment, and workplace safety functions.

*Technical and Leadership Competencies*

* Defense manufacturing and production operations.
* Mechanical and electrical assembly and integration.
* Simulation hardware manufacturing and testing.
* Production planning, scheduling, and capacity management.
* Configuration management and engineering change control.
* Quality management systems and regulatory compliance.
* Government contracting and DoD acquisition environments.
* ERP/MRP systems and material requirements planning.
* Cost accounting, labor forecasting, and operational performance metrics.
* Strategic thinking and organizational leadership.
* Cross-functional collaboration and resource allocation.
* Leadership development, team building, and change management.
* Accountability for cost, schedule, quality, and delivery performance.

*Security & Compliance Requirements*

* Must be eligible to work in the United States.
* Must be eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. Government Secret-level security clearance.
* Must successfully complete applicable government security eligibility and investigation requirements.
* Must be able to work in accordance with applicable DoD security, export control, and controlled information requirements.
* Familiarity with International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), Export Administration Regulations (EAR), and Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) requirements, as applicable.

**What Success Looks Like**
The Director of Production will be successful by:
  
  

* Delivering production commitments on time and within established cost and quality objectives.
* Building a strong, accountable, and effective production leadership team.
* Maintaining production readiness and sufficient capacity to support current and future programs.
* Improving manufacturing efficiency, productivity, and operational performance.
* Ensuring effective coordination among Production, Engineering, Program Management, Quality, Procurement, and Facilities.
* Maintaining safe, reliable, and growth-ready production facilities.
* Positioning ASI's production organization to successfully execute new program awards and support long-term business growth.

**EDUCATION**
Bachelor’s degree in engineering, Manufacturing, Operations Management, or a related technic
  
  
al discipline, or equivalent relevant experience.
  
  
**Physical Requirements**

records.description:

Joyful by design, sunny by nature, and unapologetically bold. If your bestie has you saved in their phone as "Icon," you're ALANI NU® — confident, colorful, and bringing main-character energy to every moment.

SoCal in your soul, attitude in your stride. If gravity doesn't stop you and "impossible" sounds more like "dare you," you're ROCKSTAR®— a born rebel, raising the bar with mind-body energy and zero compromise.

Together, we're Celsius Holdings, Inc.— a global CPG company united by three powerhouse brands and one incredibly talented team.

At Celsius, we pride ourselves on empowering our people. Every employee has a stake in our success. We create a collaborative culture built on inclusivity, innovation, and a belief that great ideas can come from anywhere.

And we're on our way to building something bigger: a category where energy isn't just consumed, it's lived—where performance meets personality, brand becomes community, and every can crack sparks a statement.

**This is the future of modern energy. This is Celsius.**

Ready to take your career to the next level? Join our team and redefine what it means to be energized.

**Position Overview**

As the Director of Manufacturing, you will serve as the senior plant leader for a high-volume beverage canning operation responsible for batching, filling, seaming, and packaging canned CELSIUS® beverages. You will provide strategic and operational leadership across production, quality, food safety, maintenance, engineering, safety, warehousing, workforce development, and continuous improvement.

The ideal candidate is a hands-on manufacturing leader who has operated in a high-speed, automated food, beverage, packaging, or consumer products environment. This role requires strong business judgment, operational discipline, technical understanding, and the ability to build an accountable, collaborative culture focused on safety, food safety, quality, service, cost, and continuous improvement.

**On-Site:**
Based full-time in Charlotte, NC at Big Beverages manufacturing facility

**Travel Requirements:**
Up to 25% domestic travel

**People Management Responsibilities:**
Yes

**Reports To:**
VP of Manufacturing

**Role Type:**
Full-Time

**Requirements**

* **Experience:**
  7-10+ years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience, preferably in high-speed beverage filling/canning, food, or consumer packaged goods operations, including at least 3-5 years leading a plant or multi-department operation with full responsibility for production performance and hourly teams
* **Education:**
  Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Operations, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Quality, Food Science, Business, or a related field preferred; equivalent experience may be considered
* Experience leading high-volume, automated manufacturing operations and managing production, maintenance, engineering, quality, safety, and continuous improvement functions
* Working knowledge of FSSC 22000, ISO 22000 principles, HACCP, GMP, FSMA, food defense, food fraud prevention, traceability, prerequisite programs, CAPA systems, and audit readiness
* Demonstrated success improving OEE, schedule attainment, throughput, labor efficiency, yield, waste, downtime, quality, cost performance, and equipment reliability through disciplined operating systems
* Experience managing budgets, labor planning, capital projects, business cases, and plant-level financial performance
* Experience hiring, developing, coaching, and leading large hourly and salaried teams, including supervisors and frontline leaders
* Experience using ERP/MRP, MES, maintenance-management, and manufacturing-performance systems to make data-driven decisions
* Strong analytical, communication, organization, and problem-solving skills
* Ability to work onsite at the manufacturing facility and support a flexible schedule based on operational needs

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Master's degree in Engineering, Operations, Business, Food Science, or a related field
* PCQI, HACCP, FSSC 22000, Lean Six Sigma, or similar certification or training
* Hands-on experience with high-speed carbonated beverage filling and canning lines, including syrup batching/blending, water treatment, carbonation, fillers, can seamers and double-seam integrity, can warmers/pasteurizers, CIP sanitation, and end-of-line packaging and palletizing
* Experience with plant start-ups, expansions, new line installations, automation, commissioning, scale-up, or major capital investments
* Experience supporting a rapidly growing consumer brand or publicly traded company
* Experience working with labor relations or represented manufacturing environments

**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead all manufacturing operations to ensure the safe, efficient, and consistent production of high-quality canned beverages from production scheduling through finished-goods handoff
* Develop and execute the plant operating strategy in alignment with CELSIUS business objectives, demand forecasts, customer requirements, and long-term growth plans
* Own production planning, capacity, staffing, schedule attainment, changeovers, line utilization, labor efficiency, and daily operating execution
* Establish clear performance expectations and accountability across production, quality, food safety, maintenance, engineering, warehouse, and support functions
* Drive key operating metrics, including safety, OEE, throughput, yield, scrap, waste, downtime, labor productivity, cost per unit, on-time production, and schedule attainment
* Establish and sustain leader standard work, tiered accountability, visual management, root-cause problem solving, standard work, and continuous-improvement routines
* Partner with Maintenance and Engineering on preventive and predictive maintenance, equipment reliability, automation, capital priorities, commissioning, line expansions, and new technology implementation
* Coordinate with Warehousing, Logistics, Supply Chain, Procurement, and Customer Service to maintain material availability, protect product integrity, and ensure accurate and timely finished-goods handoff
* Maintain compliance with applicable safety, environmental, food-contact, quality, food-safety, and regulatory requirements, including FSSC 22000, HACCP, GMP, FSMA, and customer standards
* Ensure effective prerequisite programs, food defense, food fraud prevention, sanitation, traceability, lot control, allergen control where applicable, and environmental monitoring activities
* Oversee inspections, testing, product release, holds, deviations, nonconforming product, complaints, CAPAs, and corrective-action effectiveness in partnership with Quality
* Ensure beverage-specific quality controls are effective, including ingredient and batch accuracy, Brix and carbonation targets, fill levels and net contents, double-seam inspection, date/lot coding, and finished-product testing
* Lead audit readiness and support certification, surveillance, recertification, customer, regulatory, internal, and third-party audits
* Maintain a strong safety culture through employee engagement, training, audits, risk assessments, safety observations, incident investigations, emergency preparedness, and corrective-action plans
* Collaborate with Human Resources to recruit, develop, retain, and engage a high-performing plant workforce
* Build leadership capability through coaching, performance management, individual development plans, skills matrices, cross-training, succession planning, and consistent leader standard work
* Lead labor planning and workforce optimization in response to production volumes, seasonality, new product requirements, and business growth
* Manage the plant operating budget, labor costs, maintenance spending, capital expenditures, and other controllable expenses
* Analyze operational and financial data to identify trends, risks, opportunities, and actions needed to improve plant performance
* Communicate plant performance, operating priorities, business risks, resource needs, and improvement plans clearly to plant and executive leadership
* Contribute to network and growth planning, including capacity, new product introductions, and line additions, in partnership with corporate Operations and Supply Chain
* Build strong working relationships with corporate brand, R&D/innovation, Quality, and Supply Chain partners, as well as co-pack customers and key suppliers where applicable
* Promote a culture consistent with CELSIUS values, including ownership, agility, grit, commercial thinking, collaboration, positive influence, and a bias for action

Required PPE (such as safety glasses, hearing protection, and safety footwear) must be worn in production areas, and all plant safety, GMP, and food-safety rules must be followed.
