**Responsibilities**
****Position Summary****
The Director of Operational Excellence & Assurance owns two closely linked functions at Related Digital: driving continuous improvement across data center operations, and independently assessing and auditing operational, safety, and quality performance against the Related Digital EHS Program Manual, site standard operating procedures, and applicable regulatory and industry standards. This includes auditing facility management partner performance against contractual SLAs and KPIs, and supporting Related Digital’s SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certification programs. This role designs and executes the internal audit and assessment program, verifies that field practice matches documented procedure, drives corrective action to closure, and partners with site and regional leadership to convert audit findings into lasting process improvement. The role carries Stop Work Authority and reports significant findings directly to site and operations leadership.
  
  
****Key Responsibilities****
****Operational Excellence & Continuous Improvement****

* Lead site and portfolio level continuous improvement initiatives to improve the safety, reliability, quality, and efficiency of data center operations.
* Establish and maintain standardized operating procedures, playbooks, and best-practice sharing across sites.
* Define, track, and report key performance indicators (KPIs) for operational performance, safety, and compliance; identify trends and improvement opportunities.
* Facilitate root cause analysis and corrective/preventive action (CAPA) processes for operational, safety, and quality events, consistent with the Incident Investigation & Root Cause Analysis Program.
* Partner with Engineering, Facilities, and EHS teams to standardize processes across the portfolio and support new site commissioning and operational readiness.
* Champion a culture of continuous improvement, change management, and operational discipline among site teams.
* Monitor energy performance, including PUE, against site design targets and drive corrective action for deviations.

****Operational Assessment & Internal Audit****

* Design, own, and execute the annual internal audit and operational assessment plan across all Related Digital sites, covering all EHS programs, life-safety systems, critical facility operations, and quality/process compliance.
* Conduct on-site operational assessments and compliance audits against the Program Manuals, site SOPs, inspection/checklist templates, and applicable regulatory or industry standards (OSHA, NFPA, ANSI, Uptime Institute Tier Standards, SOC2, ISO 9001/45001/14001).
* Evaluate the completeness and currency of site-level checklists, inspection logs, JHAs/AHAs, and training records against the EHS Training Requirements Matrix.
* Document audit findings, assign risk ratings, and issue formal assessment reports to site and regional leadership.
* Track corrective action plans (CAPs) to closure, verifying effectiveness through follow-up audits.
* Maintain audit program documentation, evidence, and records consistent with the Records Management & Retention Program.
* Support external audits, customer/tenant due-diligence assessments, and regulatory inspections as the internal subject matter expert.
* Audit physical security programs, covering access control, credentialing, and key management.
* Audit commissioning and construction documentation, such as MOPs, RCAs, and general contractor turnover packages, for completeness before closeout.

****Facility Management Partner & Vendor Oversight****

* Audit facility management partner performance against contractual SLAs and KPIs, covering maintenance completion, staffing, and site inspections; validate SLA credits using EPMS, BMS, CMMS, and incident log data.
* Audit facility management partner Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery programs, and verify adherence to change management and work notification protocols.
* Support evaluation of facility management partner RFP responses and subcontractor compliance.
* Review partner markups, pricing transparency, and preferred vendor compliance.
* Support transition and exit audits when facility management partners change.

****Governance, Training & Reporting****

* Maintain and continuously improve the internal audit methodology, scoring rubrics, and assessment tools.
* Deliver periodic (e.g., quarterly) operational excellence and audit performance reporting to executive leadership, including site scorecards and trend analysis.
* Partner with the Site EHS Manager and Safety Training Program owners to close training and competency gaps identified during assessments.
* Provide coaching and calibration to site leadership on self-assessment practices, audit readiness, and continuous improvement tools.
* Participate in incident investigation reviews where root causes point to systemic operational or procedural gaps.
* Lead Related Digital’s SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 audit cycles, including evidence collection and coordination with external auditors.
* Review facility management partner SOC 2 and ISO 27001 attestation reports where relevant to Related Digital’s compliance obligations.

**Qualifications**
****Educational and Certifications****
**Minimum Education (Required):**

* Bachelor’s degree in Industrial Engineering, Occupational Safety & Health, Business Administration, Operations Management, Quality Management, or another related technical or business discipline.
* Equivalent experience in lieu of degree: an Associate’s degree plus a minimum of four (4) additional years of directly relevant operational excellence, quality assurance, or internal audit experience, or a high school diploma/GED plus eight (8) years of directly relevant experience, may be considered in place of the bachelor’s degree requirement.

**Preferred Education:**

* Master’s degree in Business Administration (MBA), Engineering Management, Occupational Safety, Quality Systems, or a related field.
* Formal coursework or certificate training in Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, or internal audit methodology.

**Required and Preferred Certifications:**

* OSHA 30-Hour General Industry or Construction certification.
* Certified Internal Auditor (CIA), Certified Quality Auditor (CQA), or CISA.
* Lean Six Sigma Green Belt.
* Certified Safety Professional (CSP), Associate Safety Professional (ASP), or Certified Industrial Hygienist (CIH).
* Data center industry certification (e.g., CDCP/CDCS/CDCE, CDCAP, or Uptime Institute Accredited Tier Specialist).

****Experience****

* Minimum 7–10 years of progressive experience in operations, quality assurance, EHS, or internal audit roles.
* At least 3 years of that experience in a data center, other critical facility, manufacturing, or industrial operating environment.
* Minimum 3 years leading or managing an internal audit, quality assurance, or operational assessment program.
* Demonstrated track record designing and executing continuous improvement initiatives with measurable, documented results.
* Experience auditing against OSHA/ANSI/NFPA standards, SOC, ISO 9001/45001/14001, IATF 16949, or Uptime Institute Tier Standards is strongly preferred given the mission-critical facility environment.
* Supervisory or project leadership experience, including leading cross-functional teams without direct authority.

****Skills & Core Competencies****

* Strong analytical and root-cause problem-solving skills; able to synthesize audit data into clear, actionable insights.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills; able to present findings to site staff, peers, and executive leadership with equal clarity.
* High attention to detail balanced with pragmatic judgment on risk prioritization.
* Proficiency with audit/GRC software, statistical and process tools (e.g., Minitab, Excel), and data visualization tools (e.g., Power BI, Tableau) is a plus.
* Comfortable exercising Stop Work Authority and holding site teams accountable with professionalism and tact.
* Working knowledge of critical facility systems (electrical, mechanical, fire/life safety) is preferred.
* Self-directed, able to plan and manage a multi-site audit calendar with minimal oversight.

****Work Environment & Physical Demands****

* Ability to walk extended distances across large facility footprints, climb stairs and ladders, and work in mechanical/electrical rooms with variable noise and temperature.
* Occasional lifting of up to 25 lbs.
* Ability to sit, stand, and use a computer for extended periods when preparing audit reports and analysis.

****Travel Requirements****

* Up to 40–50% domestic travel across the Related Digital site portfolio can be required, including occasional multi-day site visits. A valid driver’s license is required; ability to travel by air and a US passport is required.

**Overview**
**Why Related Digital?**
Formed in 1972, Related is the most prominent privately-owned real estate firm in the United States. Headquartered in New York City, the company has offices and major developments across the world. Related owns and manages a premier portfolio of assets valued at over $70 billion, including the 28-acre Hudson Yards neighborhood on Manhattan’s West Side.
  
  
Related believes in investing in its talent and cultivates a positive, team-oriented environment where every voice is valued. Employees are encouraged to boldly take on new challenges, transcend the status quo, and demonstrate strong entrepreneurial spirit. In its relentless commitment to excellence, Related fosters an innovative approach so that team members can positively impact the communities in which they conduct business.
  
  
Founded by Related Companies, Related Digital is a leading vertically integrated data center development and investment platform that partners with leading technology companies to provide best-in-class digital infrastructure and holistic energy solutions through responsible, community-centered development. Related Digital currently has $55B in active data center development and construction underway representing 6GW of capacity, with projects in Ontario, Wyoming, Michigan, Missouri, Illinois and Texas.
  
  
Its vertically integrated platform encompasses site acquisition, entitlements, supply chain procurement, steel fabrication, construction management, and utility-scale energy solutions, providing hyperscalers with differentiated, end-to-end execution. Learn more at related-digital.com .

Build Your Career as a Director, Operational Excellence & Business Enablement!
  
  
At BlueLinx, our people are at the heart of our success. We are committed to ensuring our team members can build job security, enhance their skills, and make meaningful contributions. We deliver the building blocks to better lives.
  
  
Join us and be part of a company that values its people and strives to make a positive impact on the industry!
  
  
**Why BlueLinx?**
**Comprehensive Benefits Include**

* Medical, Dental, Vision, Prescription
* 401(k) with company match
* Tuition reimbursement
* Life Insurance
* Generous Paid Time Off (PTO) and 8 Company Holidays
* Career Growth: Opportunity to develop and advance your career with a leading building products distributor.

**Job Summary**
The Director, Operational Excellence & Business Enablement leads the development and deployment of the BlueLinx operating system across the branch network. This role converts operational strategy, performance data, and technology investments into standard processes, measurable performance improvement, and sustained branch adoption. Reporting to the Sr. Director, Logistics Systems, the Director partners across Regional Operations, Branch Operations, Commercial, Inventory, Finance, Human Resources, Safety, and Information Technology to improve customer service, labor productivity, cost performance, process consistency, and the adoption of new operating capabilities.
  
  
**What You'll Do**

* Understands the company’s vision, mission, and strategy; translates business and functional objectives into clear Operational Excellence priorities and measurable outcomes.
* Leads the enterprise operations performance-management process, including metric definitions, monthly reporting, trend analysis, performance reviews, corrective-action follow-up, and continuous improvement of dashboards and reporting methods.
* Owns governance and continuous improvement for On-Time and In-Full delivery performance, including failure-reason categories, functional ownership, root-cause analysis, corrective actions, and branch adoption.
* Develops and maintains the BlueLinx branch operating system, including standard work, daily and weekly management routines, branch assessment methods, operating playbooks, and sustainment reviews.
* Leads the operational labor-management strategy, including common productivity measures, labor standards, reporting requirements, and branch improvement plans developed in partnership with Regional Operations and Human Resources.
* Serves as the business process and adoption leader for operations, logistics and warehouse technology-enabled improvement initiatives, including transportation, warehouse management, scanning, labeling, automation, data, and artificial intelligence capabilities.
* Translates operational needs into clear business requirements; leads current-state and future-state process design, operational pilots, field testing, readiness, rollout planning, training, adoption measurement, and post-launch sustainment.
* Maintains the enterprise Operational Excellence project portfolio and prioritizes work based on customer impact, business value, risk, available resources, and alignment with company strategy.
* Partners with Finance to validate expected and realized financial benefits, including direct savings, cost avoidance, productivity improvements, and working-capital opportunities.
* Provides structured problem-solving support for complex, cross-functional, or recurring branch issues while ensuring the accountable function retains ownership of execution and sustainment.
* Builds organizational capability through practical training and coaching in standard work, root-cause analysis, process improvement, visual management, and leader operating routines.
* Identifies proven branch practices and creates repeatable methods to scale those practices across regions and locations.
* Builds strong working relationships with regional, branch, and functional leadership; influences decisions through clear data, practical recommendations, and disciplined follow-through.
* Leads and develops assigned Operational Excellence, analytics, process improvement, or industrial engineering resources and actively supports talent acquisition and succession planning.
* Travel: Up to 50%, based on branch support, project deployment, leader development, and business priorities

**Qualifications**

* Certifications: Lean, Six Sigma Black Belt, or comparable process-improvement certification preferred
* Educational: Bachelor's degree in Industrial Engineering, Supply Chain, Operations, Business, or a related field required. Master's degree preferred.
* Generally 5+ years of relevant experience in distribution, manufacturing, logistics, or multi-site operations; demonstrated experience leading people and cross-functional business process improvement

**What We're Looking For**

* Deep knowledge of distribution or multi-site operations, including branch execution, warehouse processes, customer service, labor productivity, and operating cost drivers.
* Demonstrated ability to build performance-management systems that connect measures, root causes, ownership, corrective action, and sustained results.
* Practical experience developing standard work, management routines, branch assessments, and scalable operating playbooks.
* Experience leading cross-functional improvement initiatives from business requirements and process design through pilot, rollout, adoption, and sustainment.
* Strong business analytics capability with the ability to validate data, interpret performance, identify meaningful trends, and communicate findings in plain language.
* Working knowledge of warehouse and transportation technology, business intelligence tools, automation, and technology-enabled process improvement.
* Experience with labor management, industrial engineering, warehouse layout, slotting, material flow, or labor standards preferred.
* Strong facilitation, project leadership, change-management, coaching, and executive communication skills.
* Ability to move comfortably between branch-level observation and executive-level decision support.
* Ability to manage competing priorities, establish decision rights, and prevent temporary project support from becoming permanent functional ownership
* Strong follow-through, sound judgment, and a bias toward simple, repeatable solutions that can be sustained by the field.

Our Values
  
  
With every decision and action, we put people first, keep the future in mind, and work as a team toward shared progress.
  
  

* Customer Centric
* Respect
* Collaboration
* Integrity
* Grit

**About Us**
BlueLinx is one of America’s largest distributors of building products, with over 70k branded and private-label SKUs. Headquartered in Marietta, Georgia, we have over 2,000 associates and distribute our comprehensive range of structural and specialty products to approximately 15k national, regional, and local dealers, as well as specialty distributors, national home centers, industrial, and manufactured housing customers.
  
  
*The salary range provided is a good-faith estimate based on the position requirements and market data. Actual compensation will depend on factors including experience, qualifications, skills, geographic location, and other job-related considerations. BlueLinx also offers a comprehensive benefits package including health care, dental, vision, life and disability insurance starting the first day of the month, 15 days of paid time off that start accruing your first day, and 8 paid holidays per year.*
To report any issues with this job posting, please contact talent@bluelinxco.com

* Provide leadership, coaching, mentoring, and performance management for assigned staff.

records.title: VP, Quality
records.description:
***Archer**
is collaborating with
**Stord**
to connect them with exceptional professionals for this role.*
Stord is The Consumer Experience Company, powering seamless checkout through delivery for today's leading brands. Stord is rapidly growing and is on track to double our revenue in the next 18 months. To meet and exceed this target, Stord is strategically scaling teams across the entire company, and seeking energetic experts to help us achieve our mission.
 
 
By combining comprehensive commerce-enablement technology with high-volume fulfillment services, Stord provides brands a platform to compete with retail giants. Stord manages over $10 billion of commerce annually through its fulfillment, warehousing, transportation, and operator-built software suite including OMS, Pre- and Post-Purchase, and WMS platforms. Stord is leveling the playing field for all brands to deliver the best consumer experience at scale.
 
 
With Stord, brands can increase cart conversion, improve unit economics, and drive sustained customer loyalty. Stord’s end-to-end commerce solutions combine best-in-class omnichannel fulfillment and shipping with leading technology to ensure fast shipping, reliable delivery promises, easy access to more channels, and improved margins on every order.
 
 
Hundreds of leading DTC and B2B companies like AG1, True Classic, Native, Seed Health, quip, goodr, Sundays for Dogs, and more trust Stord to deliver industry-leading consumer experiences on every order. Stord is headquartered in Atlanta with facilities across the United States, Canada, and Europe. Stord is backed by top-tier investors including Kleiner Perkins, Franklin Templeton, Founders Fund, Strike Capital, Baillie Gifford, and Salesforce Ventures.
 
 
**About The Role**
Stord is looking for a Vice President of Quality to build and lead the quality function across our fulfillment network.
 
 
This leader will own the systems, standards, and operating mechanisms that ensure inventory is accurate, processes are followed, and every order moves through our network the way it was designed to. The mandate spans the full lifecycle of inventory inside our buildings from inbound receipt and putaway through picking, packing, sorting, and outbound shipment.
 
 
This is an independent quality function. While our Operations teams are responsible for delivering volume efficiently, the VP of Quality is responsible for ensuring we never achieve speed, growth, or cost improvements by compromising inventory integrity or execution quality.
 
 
This leader should be an inventory and fulfillment quality expert at heart — someone who understands how inventory moves through a complex fulfillment operation, knows where process breakdowns create downstream failures, and is relentless about identifying and eliminating root causes.
 
 
**What You'll Own**
**Inventory Health & Accuracy**

* Own inventory health and accuracy across Stord's fulfillment network.
* Establish the standards, controls, and operating mechanisms required to maintain book-to-floor and floor-to-book inventory integrity.
* Own cycle counting, inventory reconciliation, adjustment governance, and inventory variance reduction.
* Build mechanisms to identify inventory defects early and systematically eliminate their root causes.
* Establish network-level metrics and reporting that make inventory health visible and actionable.

**Fulfillment Process Quality**

* Own process adherence across inbound, receiving, putaway, picking, packing, sorting, and outbound operations.
* Define the critical quality controls for each process path and ensure sites consistently execute against them.
* Build audit mechanisms that identify process drift before it becomes a customer or inventory issue.
* Partner with Operations, Product, Engineering, and Data to eliminate systemic sources of defects.
* Develop a clear view of transaction volume, exception rates, and defect rates by process path to identify where quality is breaking down.

**Lot Control & Regulatory Compliance**

* Own lot, expiration-date, and inventory-attribute accuracy across applicable customers and facilities.
* Establish controls for FIFO, FEFO, lot traceability, recalls, quarantine, and other regulated inventory requirements.
* Ensure Stord's operating processes meet applicable customer, regulatory, and contractual quality requirements.
* Build a quality organization capable of supporting increasingly complex and regulated categories as Stord grows.

**Continuous Improvement**

* Build a rigorous root-cause and corrective-action discipline across the fulfillment network.
* Turn recurring defects into permanent process, system, or training improvements rather than repeatedly solving individual incidents.
* Identify network-wide trends and deploy standardized improvements across sites.
* Partner with Product and Engineering to ensure recurring operational defects inform the technology roadmap.
* Create a culture where defects are surfaced quickly, investigated objectively, and permanently resolved.

**Quality Organization**

* Build and lead Stord's network Quality and Inventory Control organization.
* Establish clear ownership and accountability between Quality and Operations.
* Develop site and regional quality leaders capable of independently auditing operational performance.
* Serve as the executive escalation point when inventory integrity, regulatory compliance, or fulfillment quality is at risk.
* Maintain an independent point of view and be willing to stop, challenge, or redesign processes when quality standards are not being met.

**What We're Looking For**
We are looking for someone who has spent their career inside
**large, complex fulfillment or distribution operations**
and understands inventory at a level most operators do not.
 
 
**The Ideal Candidate**

* Has 12+ years of experience across fulfillment quality, inventory control, operational excellence, distribution, or supply chain operations, including significant leadership experience.
* Has led quality or inventory control across a multi-site fulfillment or distribution network.
* Comes from a scaled 3PL, retailer, e-commerce fulfillment network, food distribution company, or similarly complex physical operation.
* Is deeply fluent in inventory control, WMS-driven processes, cycle counting, reconciliation, lot control, and inventory accuracy.
* Understands the mechanics of inbound, putaway, pick, pack, sort, and outbound processes — and how defects in one process create downstream failures elsewhere.
* Has built quality systems based on data, audits, root-cause analysis, corrective actions, and measurable defect reduction.
* Is comfortable challenging Operations leadership when execution does not meet the required standard.
* Has operated in environments where quality and compliance cannot be traded for throughput or cost.
* Ideally brings experience from food, grocery, pharmaceutical, healthcare, or another environment with rigorous lot, expiration, traceability, or regulatory requirements.
* Can operate strategically at the executive level while still being willing to go onto the warehouse floor, trace an inventory discrepancy through a WMS, and understand exactly where a process failed.

: Columbia, MD
 
 
**About Us**
Tate Americas is a key business within Kingspan Data Solutions and is at the forefront of delivering integrated solutions to the rapidly expanding data centre market. We combine engineering expertise, advanced manufacturing and operational excellence to deliver complex, mission-critical projects for some of the world’s largest technology companies.
 
 
With significant investment and ambitious growth plans, Tate is evolving beyond traditional manufacturing to become a fully integrated solutions provider, offering customers a seamless delivery model from design and manufacturing through installation, commissioning and final handover.
 
 
**About The Role**
The US Head of Quality provides strategic leadership of the quality management function across all US manufacturing sites, ensuring products manufactured for data-centre applications consistently meet customer specifications, regulatory standards and internal quality benchmarks. This role is accountable for the deployment and governance of the Quality Management System (ISO 9001) across US operations, the development of Site Quality Managers, the integrity of supplier quality, and the effective close-out of quality non-conformances. Working closely with the US Head of Compliance, Site General Managers, Engineering and Supply Chain, the role holder will drive a culture of Zero Defects, First-Time-Right, and continuous improvement through Lean and Six Sigma methodologies. The role is a key member of the Global Quality, Compliance & Health & Safety leadership team and supports the delivery of the Quality & Compliance Pyramid across all US sites.
 
 
**What You’ll Do**
**Quality Management System Leadership**

* Own and continually improve the US Quality Management System aligned to ISO 9001 and customer-specific requirements.
* Ensure consistent deployment of quality procedures, work instructions, Inspection & Test Plans and control plans across all US sites.
* Provide quarterly reporting on QMS maturity, system performance and external audit readiness.
* Act as the principal quality signatory for US operations at Management Review.
* Ensure calibration programs, nonconforming material controls and change-control processes operate effectively across all sites.

**Site Quality Leadership & People Development**

* Lead, coach and develop Site Quality Managers, Quality Engineers and Quality Supervisors across US sites.
* Establish clear objectives, capability frameworks and development plans for the US quality community.
* Drive a culture of accountability, cross-site collaboration and high performance within the quality function.
* Own succession planning and technical competence development including AWS CWI, AWS CWS, AMPP, Six Sigma and internal auditor certifications.
* Champion a Zero Defects mindset and psychological safety for raising quality concerns.

**Supplier Quality & Incoming Material Control**

* Govern the supplier quality program across US operations, including supplier qualification, PPAP / First Article Inspection, supplier audits and Supplier Corrective Action Requests.
* Ensure robust incoming goods inspection, control of externally provided processes, and supplier performance reporting.
* Drive measurable reduction in supplier-driven non-conformances, line stops and rework cost.
* Partner with Supply Chain leadership to align supplier strategy, approved vendor lists and commercial terms with quality expectations.

**Welding, Fabrication & Coating Process Quality**

* Own the welding qualification program (WPS, PQR, WPQ) to AWS D1.1 / D1.3 and applicable customer standards for structural steel and hot aisle containment products.
* Own the coating qualification program to AMPP (NACE/SSPC) requirements, including surface preparation, DFT, adhesion and cure.
* Establish in-process inspection regimes (VT, DFT, dimensional) and statistical process control across fabrication, welding and paint processes.
* Ensure capable, calibrated inspection equipment, traceable measurement systems and robust Measurement System Analysis.

**Non-Conformance, CAPA & Continuous Improvement**

* Govern the US non-conformance and CAPA program, ensuring root cause rigor, effectiveness verification and closure discipline.
* Drive Lean, 5S and Six Sigma improvement activities focused on defect prevention and reduction of Cost of Poor Quality.
* Establish and track regional quality KPIs and performance dashboards: DPPM, first-pass yield, customer complaints, scrap and rework cost, audit score.
* Lead quality improvement initiatives linked to the Quality & Compliance Pyramid Action Plan.

**Customer Quality & External Audit Face-off**

* Serve as senior quality representative for hyperscale customer audits, Factory Acceptance Tests and customer site visits.
* Manage customer quality escalations, 8D responses and corrective-action delivery with rigor and pace.
* Ensure customer-specific requirements are captured in quality plans, control plans and inspection regimes at site level.
* Partner with Sales, Commercial and Estimating teams on quality-related tender qualification and customer onboarding.

**Governance & Reporting**

* Provide monthly quality performance reports to the Global Head of Quality, Compliance & Health & Safety.
* Support Management Reviews, internal audits and external ISO 9001 surveillance and recertification audits.
* Ensure quality risks are identified, quantified and escalated appropriately within the US operation.
* Maintain regional ownership of Management of Change impacting product quality, process qualification or inspection regimes.

*Additional Expectations*

* Remain compliant with the Code of Conduct and Policies which includes the Kingspan Group Compliance Policy.
* Ensure that all duties related to product compliance are adhered to in accordance with the Product Compliance Policy, Laws, Regulations, and market demands.
* Responsible for all tasks to achieve compliance goals and demands of the Compliance Management System.
* Must raise concerns related to the Compliance Management System to their supervisor, manager, or any member of the Leadership Team, or through the confidential whistle blower service.

**What You’ll Bring**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Quality Management or related technical discipline; advanced degree preferred.
* Minimum 10 years of progressive quality experience in a manufacturing environment, including at least 5 years leading multi-site operations.
* Proven leadership of Quality Managers or equivalent senior roles across multiple sites.
* Lead auditor qualification in ISO 9001 required; additional qualification in ISO 37301 or ISO 14001 desirable.
* Deep experience of welded and fabricated product quality; AWS QC1 Certified Welding Inspector certification preferred.
* Practical experience with coating qualification to AMPP (NACE/SSPC) standards desirable.
* Certified Six Sigma Black Belt or equivalent continuous improvement qualification.
* Strong working knowledge of PPAP, APQP, control plans, PFMEA, SPC and Measurement System Analysis.
* Experience managing quality for hyperscale data-center customers, OEMs or comparable demanding clients.
* Exceptional leadership, communication, stakeholder management and decision-making skills.
* Willingness and ability to travel regularly to US manufacturing sites.

**What You’ll Get**

* This role is eligible for a discretionary bonus.
* Career Scope and Advancement: As we grow, new positions and career opportunities arise, offering accelerated paths for the right candidates, locally and globally.
* World of Wellness Philosophy: We empower you to take charge of your health and well-being. You’ll have access to a wide range of medical, dental, and vision benefits, along with personalized guidance from a “Health Advocate.” We also offer other supplemental options, including 401k, legal, disability, and theft insurance, to ensure your financial wellness.
* Corporate Social Responsibility: Through Planet Passionate we are determined to reduce our manufacturing carbon (CO2e) emissions to as close to zero as technically possible, together with halving carbon intensity in our primary supply chain. We are very involved in our community, and you will have ample opportunities to support us in creating a better world.
* Skills Development: Given the dynamic pace of our business and a strong collaborative environment, your new role will be diverse and multifaceted – allowing you to be more versatile and develop a broader skill set.
* Mentorship and development: At Tate, we don’t believe in hierarchy; we work together as one team for one common goal. You will have access and exposure to our senior leaders and experts for learning in your role, and additional mentorship for the future.
* Culture: We have a great team of culture, highly collaborative, supportive, and social skills. Together we innovate, collaborate, take ownership, and strive for excellence.

Stay connected with us on LinkedIn for insights into life at Tate. Join us in our mission to make a difference through exceptional solutions.
 
 
Tate Inc. is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to legally protected characteristics. We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities. Employment is contingent upon the successful completion of post-offer requirements, including a background check and drug screening, in accordance with company policy and applicable laws.

records.description:
**Vice President Quality**

**Global Product Distribution Quality**

**The Opportunity**

Our client is a leading global medical technology company looking to appoint a hands-on VP Global Product Distribution Quality. Reporting directly to the SVP of Corporate Quality, you will be responsible for developing and implementing business strategies to effectively manage all global product distribution quality. In this role, you will lead the global product distribution quality organization and processes, holding quality management accountability for all captive and outsourced distribution centres across every entity worldwide.

This is a genuine turnaround and organizational design mandate, rather than a caretaker or step-up role. You will step in to stabilize day-to-day operations, manage significant FDA and global regulatory scrutiny, and reshape the commercial quality infrastructure into a world-class function. For a seasoned executive who enjoys building progressive systems at scale, there is a clear path to expanded enterprise responsibility within 6 to 20 months.

**Key Responsibilities**

* **Global Distribution Governance:**
 Own quality management systems/compliance performance across captive/3PL distribution centres globally - alongside full P&L, budget, and headcount accountability for the function.
* **Turnaround & Future-State Design:**
 Audit current teams, workflows, and systems to close compliance gaps, restructuring the global commercial quality organization into a streamlined, best-in-class model.
* **FDA & Global Regulatory Execution:**
 Act as the single accountable global executive for all distribution-related regulatory inspections, audit responses, and direct agency communications, including intensive FDA engagement.
* **Quality Systems & Digital Traceability:**
 Direct the IT partnership to optimize warehouse management systems (WMS), end-to-end product traceability, inventory controls, and nonconforming product containment.
* **Enterprise Leadership:**
 Serve as the global subject matter expert for distribution quality and contribute to enterprise-wide quality strategy as a senior member of the Global Corporate Quality leadership team.

**Candidate Profile**

* **Sitting or Recent Med-Tech VP:**
 Minimum 10 years of global organizational leadership at the Vice President level within medical devices, capital equipment, or adjacent life sciences—ready to deliver impact from day one.
* **Post-Manufacturing & 3PL Mastery:**
 Deep operational expertise in commercial, supply chain, and global distribution quality across multi-site networks (upstream supplier quality into manufacturing is out of scope).
* **Proven Remediation Track Record:**
 Demonstrated success leading quality turnarounds, organizational redesigns, and systemic remediation under active FDA scrutiny.
* **Global Trade & Customs Compliance:**
 Hands-on command of international medical device regulations, import/export laws, embargoes, import bans, and regional market-entry barriers.
* **Academic Foundation:**
 Bachelor of Science in a medical or applied science discipline

**What Sets You Apart**

You lead from the front with high energy and a clear appetite for complex turnarounds. You combine sharp analytical rigor with executive presence, enabling you to influence across commercial, supply chain, and regulatory stakeholders while building high-performing global teams.

records.title: VP, Regional Manufacturing
records.description:
**Overview**

Primo Brands is a leading branded beverage company in North America with a focus on healthy hydration. We are proud to offer an extensive and iconic portfolio of highly recognizable, sustainably sourced, and conveniently packaged branded beverages distributed across more than 150,000 retail outlets.

**Compensation:**
$185,048 - $248,596. This position is eligible for an annual bonus.

**Location:**
Dallas, TX

**Health Benefits**

Benefits of working for Primo Brands:

Medical, prescription, dental, vision, flexible spending account (FSA), dependent care flexible spending account (FSA), health savings account (HSA)

**Retirement/Investing**

401K with a 5% match, Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP)

**Insurance**

Employee Life Insurance, short and long-term disability, critical illness, hospital indemnity, accident insurance, spouse/domestic partner/child life insurance, accidental death and dismemberment

**Other Great Benefits**

Employee discounts, save on auto, home, and pet insurance, tuition reimbursement, paid vacation and sick time, 9 paid holidays and 3 paid floating holidays, paid leave for when you have a baby, adopt a child, or become a foster parent, legal services, identity theft protection, employee assistance program (EAP), adoption reimbursement benefit, FEDlogic, commuter benefits.

**Responsibilities**

The Regional Vice President (RVP), Manufacturing is responsible for leading the end-to-end manufacturing operations across a multi-site regional network within Primo Brands. This executive leader drives safety, quality, production, cost, service, people, and continuous improvement performance across factories while ensuring alignment with enterprise Supply Chain strategies and business objectives.

The RVP, Manufacturing partners closely with Supply Chain, Operations, Engineering, Quality, Maintenance, Procurement, Planning, HR, and Finance leaders to deliver operational excellence, optimize manufacturing capacity, develop organizational capability, and support long-term business growth. The role is accountable for creating a high-performance culture that prioritizes safety, quality, associate engagement, customer service, and productivity improvements.

The Regional Vice President, Manufacturing reports to the Senior Vice President, Manufacturing Operations.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Safety & Compliance Leadership**

* Lead a culture where safety is the first priority and operational decisions reflect a zero-harm mindset.
* Ensure compliance with all federal, state, provincial, environmental, food safety, and regulatory requirements.
* Drive accountability for safety performance, incident reduction, risk mitigation, and compliance excellence.
* Serve as a visible champion for workplace safety and associate well-being.

**Manufacturing Operations**

* Lead manufacturing performance across multiple factories, ensuring consistent execution against operational objectives.
* Deliver production plans that support customer demand, service expectations, and inventory requirements.
* Drive schedule attainment, throughput, asset utilization, and manufacturing reliability.
* Optimize regional manufacturing capacity and network performance.
* Ensure disciplined execution of daily management systems and operational governance routines.

**Food Safety & Quality**

* Champion food safety and quality excellence across all facilities.
* Ensure manufacturing sites maintain compliance with applicable regulatory, customer, and company standards.
* Provide leadership oversight of quality management systems, audits, inspections, recalls, and corrective action processes.
* Promote a culture of first-time-right execution and continuous quality improvement.

**Financial & Productivity Performance**

* Own regional manufacturing budgets, labor productivity, conversion costs, and operating performance.
* Deliver annual productivity, cost savings, and efficiency targets.
* Identify opportunities to reduce waste, improve OEE, optimize labor deployment, and improve asset performance.
* Partner with Finance to ensure operational results support annual business plans and long-range objectives.

**Talent & Organizational Leadership**

* Build and lead high-performing teams through effective leadership, coaching, succession planning, and talent development.
* Develop strong Plant Directors, Factory Managers, Technical Managers, Operations Managers, and functional leaders.
* Drive leadership capability, workforce planning, succession readiness, and organizational effectiveness.
* Foster a culture of accountability, inclusion, collaboration, and associate engagement.

**Continuous Improvement**

* Lead implementation of manufacturing excellence initiatives across the region.
* Drive improvements in OEE, asset reliability, labor productivity, quality, and service performance.
* Leverage Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, TPM, and continuous improvement methodologies to drive sustainable results.
* Establish performance metrics and governance processes that accelerate operational excellence.

**Strategic Leadership**

* Contribute to the development and execution of Supply Chain and Manufacturing strategies.
* Partner with cross-functional stakeholders to evaluate network optimization opportunities, capacity investments, automation initiatives, and capital projects.
* Lead manufacturing integration, transformation, and change management initiatives.
* Support enterprise growth through scalable operational solutions and disciplined execution.

**Scope of Responsibility**

* Multiple manufacturing facilities within assigned region.
* Direct leadership of Plant Directors, Factory Managers, Regional Engineering, Manufacturing Excellence, and operational support functions.
* Accountability for regional safety, quality, production, service, cost, talent, and financial performance.
* Significant influence on capital planning, organizational design, and operational strategy.

**Qualifications**

**Education**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, Operations Management, Supply Chain, Business, or related field required.
* Master's Degree (MBA or related discipline) preferred.

**Experience**

* 15+ years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience.
* 10+ years leading multi-site manufacturing operations.
* Experience managing large-scale manufacturing networks in food, beverage, consumer packaged goods, or related industries.
* Proven success leading large teams through operational transformation and continuous improvement initiatives.
* Experience managing significant P&L, productivity, and capital investment responsibilities.

**Skills & Competencies**

* Executive leadership and influence.
* Manufacturing operations expertise.
* Safety and quality systems leadership.
* Financial and operational acumen.
* Strategic thinking and execution.
* Change leadership and organizational transformation.
* Talent development and succession management.
* Data-driven decision making.
* Cross-functional collaboration.
* Strong communication and stakeholder management skills.

**Success Measures**

* Safety Performance
* Quality Compliance & Customer Metrics
* OEE and Asset Reliability
* Production Attainment
* Cost per Case Equivalent
* Labor Productivity
* Service Levels / OTIF
* Associate Engagement
* Leadership Bench Strength
* Productivity Savings Delivery
* Capital Project Execution
* Manufacturing Excellence Maturity

**If you're ready to embark on an exciting journey with Primo Brands, apply now!**

**Salary Range Disclaimer**

The salary range provided for this position is an approximation based on market research, internal compensation data and the candidate’s qualifications and experience. Final salary offers are determined through a comprehensive evaluation of candidate qualifications and may vary depending on factors such as skills, experience, and geographic location of the position. Other components of the compensation package, including benefits and bonuses, will also be considered. We are committed to fair and equitable compensation practices, and we encourage open dialogue about compensation during the interview process.

Primo Brands’ established portfolio includes billion-dollar brands Poland Spring® and Pure Life®, premium brands like Saratoga® and Mountain Valley®, regional leaders such as Arrowhead®, Deer Park®, Ice Mountain® Ozarka®, and Zephyrhills®, purified brands, Primo Water® and Sparkletts®, and flavored and enhanced brands like Splash® and AC+ION®. Our extensive direct-to-consumer offerings and industry-leading line-up of innovative water dispensers create consumer connectivity through recurring water purchases across Water Direct, Water Exchange, and Water Refill. At Primo Brands, our more than 11,000 associates are at the heart of what we do and deliver on our mission to provide healthy hydration to consumers wherever, however and whenever they want it. We believe in fostering a respectful culture, which values our associates who are deeply invested in quality hydration, our communities, and the sustainability of our packaging and water sources for generations to come.

Primo Brands is proud to be an Equal Opportunity and Affirmative Action employer, seeking to create a welcoming and diverse environment. We do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, gender expression, transgender status, sexual stereotypes, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics. We also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with applicable federal, state, and local law.

Candidates must possess strong English language skills to effectively communicate with customers and provide exceptional service. Proficiency in English is essential for understanding customer needs, resolving inquiries, and collaborating with team members.

records.title: Director, Operations
records.description:
**Company Overview**
**Nikkiso Clean Energy & Industrial Gases**
is a leading provider of cryogenic pumps, heat exchangers, process systems, services, and solutions for the LNG and industrial gases industry. We are a subsidiary of Nikkiso Company Ltd, a leading industrial manufacturer headquartered in Tokyo, Japan, with over $1.5 B in annual revenue, 8000 + employees worldwide, and publicly traded on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
 
 
**Nikkiso ACD**
is an engineering and manufacturing company specializing in machinery designed to operate at cryogenic temperatures as low as – 420 degrees Fahrenheit, the boiling point of Liquid hydrogen. For over 50 years, Nikkiso ACD has specialized in centrifugal and reciprocating pumps as well as turbines for air separation. Nikkiso ACD has the most diversified product line in the industry covering nearly every application requiring pumps or turboexpanders.
 
 
**Job Overview**
The Director, Operations is responsible for overseeing all aspects of the manufacturing process. This role will develop and implement strategies that optimize the efficiency and effectiveness of the manufacturing operations to ensure the delivery of high-quality products on time and within budget.
 
 
**Responsibilities**

* Develop and implement operational strategies that improve the efficiency, productivity, and profitability of the manufacturing operations for cryogenic pumps
* Ensure that manufacturing operations comply with all relevant safety and environmental regulations
* Develop and manage the annual manufacturing budget and monitor and control expenses to ensure that they remain within budgetary constraints
* Identify and implement process improvements that increase efficiency, reduce costs, and enhance product quality while reducing product cost and increase margins
* Manage and develop a large team of manufacturing professionals, providing coaching and mentoring to enable them to reach their full potential
* Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including engineering, design, and sales, to ensure that products meet customer requirements
* Maintain positive relationships with key stakeholders, including suppliers, customers, and outsourced manufacturing partners
* Develop and implement consistent processes and best practice strategies, policies, procedures, and goals
* Work cross-functionally with product manager, product development, engineering and project management teams to ensure company goals are met and the necessary support to deliver on time is provided
* Lead the effort in identification, recruiting, interviewing, onboarding, training, and ongoing engagement of high-performance team members
* Monitor and analyze key performance indicators for manufacturing such as safety, quality, delivery, cost, cash and, people
* Address escalated customer issues with speed and urgency, orchestrating resources across the company as appropriate
* Identify and remove obstacles to delivering products consistently on time with the right quality

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor's or Master’s degree in Engineering, Supply Chain, or Operations Management, or related field or equivalent work experience
* Minimum of 10 years of experience in a manufacturing leadership role, preferably in the rotating equipment industry
* Extensive knowledge in manufacturing that are consistent with pump products, and how they are manufactured for the cryogenic industry preferred
* Proven track record of developing and implementing operational strategies that improve efficiency, productivity, and profitability
* Experience managing budgets and controlling expenses for operations
* Strong understanding of regulatory requirements and environmental and safety regulations

**Director of Manufacturing Operations (low-volume, high-mix or complex assembly req.)**

**Location: East Dallas, near Mesquite, TX**

**Salary: $200,000 - $250,000+ (DOE) + Performance-based Bonus + Benefits**

**Benefits: Medical, Dental, Vision, Holidays, PTO, Equity Shares**

**Job Type: Full-Time | On-site**

**Typical Hours: Monday-Friday; 40-45 hours/week**

**Start Date: ASAP**

**Sponsorship is not available**

**Relocation assistance available**

**Director of Manufacturing Operations Description**

Our client in the manufacturing industry is looking for a Director of Manufacturing Operations to join their team in East Dallas, near Mesquite, TX. This newly created role will lead approximately 40 employees across production, supply chain, inventory, quality, and continuous improvement, through three direct report managers. You will build the operating systems needed to support continued growth, with an emphasis on improving production flow, standardizing work, strengthening material availability, and reducing order-to-ship lead times. The operation is low-volume, high-mix, and highly customized, making experience applying lean principles in complex manufacturing environments critical. Our client is looking for a manufacturing leader who has led multiple functions and personally delivered measurable improvements from batch production toward flow. This is an opportunity to build and improve an operating system while leading a growing manufacturing organization in a high-demand market.

**Director of Manufacturing Operations Responsibilities**

• Lead production, supply chain, inventory, quality, and facilities

• Develop production flow, capacity, scheduling, and standard work systems

• Reduce order-to-ship lead times and improve on-time delivery

• Build material replenishment, point-of-use, and inventory systems

• Improve supplier performance, sourcing, material availability, and lead times

• Move quality controls upstream to reduce defects reaching final testing

• Establish daily management and structured problem-solving systems

• Lead lean improvements across low-volume, high-mix production

• Develop operations leaders and an approximately 40-person team

• Build capacity to support growth without proportional labor or space increases

**Director of Manufacturing Operations Qualifications**

• 10+ years of manufacturing operations experience required

• 5+ years leading multiple manufacturing departments, including production, required

• Low-volume, high-mix or complex assembly experience required

• Experience leading production flow improvements or measurable lead-time reduction required

• Experience implementing and sustaining lean management practices in manufacturing required

• Experience scaling production capacity or output required

• Manufacturing ERP proficiency required

records.description:
**Sierra Space Careers:**
At Sierra Space, we build the missions and systems that keep our world secure in the domain above Earth.
 
 
Sierra Space team members share a spirit of innovation and collaboration and a belief that we can deliver on the boldest missions in space today. Together with our customers, we aim to safeguard our nation, sustain human presence in space, and secure the freedom of operations in low Earth orbit and beyond.
 
 
Our success is measured by the trust of those who rely on what we build and deliver, and our technologies keep the United States and its allies mission-ready throughout space.
 
 
We are mission-driven, and together, we are an extraordinary team.
 
 
**About The Role**
Sierra Space is scaling from development programs into high-rate, repeatable production across a diversified portfolio of military and commercial systems, including satellites and spacecraft, propulsion systems, solar power systems, and the Dream Chaser spaceplane. As Director, Production Operations based in Madison, Wisconsin, you will play a critical role in executing the production strategy for propulsion development and manufacturing, building the operational systems required to deliver hardware at pace, at quality, and at cost.
 
 
This is an execution-focused leadership role for a proven operations professional with expertise in propulsion systems. Reporting to the Vice President, Production, you will lead manufacturing and assembly operations for propulsion product lines and additional enterprise products within Sierra Space's Madison facility. You will drive standardization of production processes, implement data-driven manufacturing systems, and build high-performing teams capable of scaling propulsion output while maintaining quality and efficiency. You will partner closely with Engineering, Supply Chain, Quality, and Program Management to ensure production readiness and on-time delivery of critical propulsion systems for space and defense applications.
 
 
**About You**
Our mission is driven by an unyielding commitment to advancing space-based technology in service of our customers and safeguarding national security. We seek individuals who are passionate about innovating beyond boundaries and relentlessly pursuing solutions that protect, preserve and empower – to join us in this critical mission.
 
 
We’re looking for team members who align with our values, mission and goals – while also meeting the minimum qualifications below. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.
 
 
**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead manufacturing and assembly operations for propulsion product lines, including day-to-day oversight of production floor activities, scheduling, and workflow management at the Madison, WI facility.
* Execute production strategy to scale propulsion manufacturing from development programs into repeatable, high-rate production with a focus on throughput, yield, and cost efficiency.
* Standardize propulsion production processes and workflows to create consistent, repeatable, high-quality build operations aligned with enterprise-wide best practices.
* Support capacity planning and facility buildout efforts for propulsion manufacturing, including layout optimization, equipment installation, and production line commissioning.
* Drive vertical integration initiatives by standing up and maturing internal propulsion manufacturing capabilities, including additive manufacturing, machining, assembly, and test operations for propulsion components and systems.
* Implement and mature manufacturing execution systems (MES) and production data infrastructure to enable traceability, repeatability, and real-time visibility into propulsion manufacturing performance.
* Establish and maintain production operating rhythm through KPIs, dashboards, and review cadences focused on cycle time, yield, throughput, labor efficiency, on-time delivery, and cost for propulsion production.
* Apply lean manufacturing and continuous improvement methodologies (Lean, Six Sigma) to identify and eliminate production inefficiencies, reduce waste, and improve quality in propulsion operations.
* Collaborate with Propulsion Engineering and Product Assurance to drive design-for-manufacturing (DFM) and design-for-test (DFT) into propulsion product development and support new product introduction (NPI) activities.
* Partner across Supply Chain, Engineering, Quality, Facilities, Security, and Program Management to ensure aligned production readiness, material availability, and execution against propulsion program schedules.
* Manage production budgets for propulsion operations and analyze manufacturing costs to implement cost-saving measures that maintain quality standards and support financial goals.
* Lead and develop production management teams at the Madison facility, including supervisors, engineers, and technicians, fostering collaboration and accountability while upholding company values and a culture of operational excellence.
* Ensure compliance with industry-specific production standards, safety regulations, and quality management systems (ISO, AS9100, GMP, etc.) applicable to aerospace and propulsion manufacturing operations.
* Represent propulsion production operations in cross-functional forums and communicate status, risks, and mitigation plans to executive leadership and external stakeholders, including customers and regulatory bodies.

**Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in engineering, manufacturing, operations, or a related technical field (or equivalent work experience in lieu of degree).
* 10+ years of experience in manufacturing, production, or operations roles in complex technical industries, with a significant portion in leadership positions.
* The ability to obtain and maintain a Top Secret U.S. Security Clearance is required
* Proven track record of successfully managing large teams and complex production projects in high-rate manufacturing environments.
* Strong background in manufacturing processes, assembly & integration, and operational execution for complex electromechanical or aerospace systems, with emphasis on propulsion systems preferred.
* Demonstrated experience implementing and scaling production operations, including process standardization, workflow optimization, and capacity planning.
* Experience with data-driven manufacturing systems, MES, and production management processes, including OKR development and performance tracking.
* Knowledge of design-for-manufacturing (DFM) principles and ability to collaborate with engineering teams to optimize product designs for production.
* Proven ability to lead multidisciplinary teams and drive operational excellence in fast-paced, highly technical environments.
* Expertise in continuous improvement methodologies (Lean, Six Sigma) with proven ability to identify and eliminate production inefficiencies.
* Strong financial acumen with demonstrated ability to manage production budgets, analyze manufacturing costs, and implement cost-saving measures.
* In-depth knowledge of industry-specific production standards, safety regulations, and quality management systems (ISO, AS9100, GMP, etc.).
* Excellent cross-functional collaboration and communication skills, with the ability to represent production interests effectively to executive leadership and external stakeholders.
* Ability to uphold and model company values while holding others accountable and fostering a culture of operational excellence.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience in propulsion manufacturing and test operations, including liquid or hybrid rocket engines, thrusters, or propulsion subsystems.
* Familiarity with additive manufacturing (3D printing) for propulsion components, including metal printing processes and post-processing.
* Experience in aerospace, defense, satellite, launch, or high-rate hardware manufacturing across both military and commercial product lines.
* Experience with vertically integrated manufacturing capabilities such as propulsion, fluid systems, PCBAs, structures, or integrated vehicle production.
* Experience with spacecraft or satellite integration and production.
* Familiarity with classified manufacturing and secure production operations.
* Experience implementing lean or continuous-improvement frameworks at scale in production environments.
* Experience with automated manufacturing, MES implementation, or production data systems.
* Experience leading organizational change initiatives specific to production environments, including technology implementation, process redesign, and workforce development.
* Experience building and scaling production teams during periods of rapid company growth.
* Master's degree in engineering, operations, business, or a related field.

Compensation:
 
 
Pay Range:
 
 
$164,513.00 - $226,205.00
 
 
Your actual base compensation will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on job-related knowledge and skills, education, experience, internal equity and market competitiveness.
 
 
**IMPORTANT NOTICE:**
This position requires the ability to obtain and maintain a Top Secret U.S. Security Clearance. U.S. Citizenship status is required as this position needs an active U.S. Security Clearance for employment. Non-U.S. Citizens may not be eligible to obtain a security clearance.  The Department of Defense Consolidated Adjudications Facility (DoD CAF), a federal government agency, handles the adjudicative aspects of the security clearance eligibility process for industry applicants. Adjudicative factors which affect the outcome of the eligibility determination include, but are not limited to, allegiance to the U.S., foreign influence, foreign preference, criminal conduct, security violations and illegal drug use.

records.title: Director of Manufacturing
records.description:
***Custom Fabrication & Assembly Manufacturing | Southeast Alabama***
**Location:**
Dothan, AL (Onsite).
*Relocation assistance is available.*
**Compensation:**
$165,000 to $180,000 base, plus 10% annual bonus
 
 
**Reports to:**
President, Signage Division
 
 
**Team:**
Top leader on site for a custom manufacturing facility with approximately 125 employees across welding, metal fabrication, CNC, forming, electrical, and assembly
 
 
**Required**

* 7+ years of hands-on manufacturing leadership experience with direct responsibility for plant-level performance, whether as a Director of Manufacturing, Plant Manager, Operations Manager, or similar role
* Experience leading a labor-intensive, high-mix, low-volume operation such as a job shop, fabrication, or build-to-order environment. Broad manufacturing judgment matters more than deep expertise in any single process
* A track record of improving throughput, labor efficiency, quality, and on-time delivery through steady, practical improvements while keeping production running
* Working knowledge of manufacturing cost, including labor standards, earned hours or standard costing, and how floor performance shows up in a plant P&L
* Strong floor presence and the ability to earn trust with a long-tenured workforce, build real buy-in, and hold people accountable when the reasons for falling short do not add up
* Experience building repeatable systems and a leadership structure that keep a plant running dependably without relying on any one person
* Resourcefulness and comfort delivering results in a lean environment without large corporate engineering or support teams behind you
* Clear, professional communication with executive and finance leadership, including regular reporting on plant performance
* Bachelor's degree in engineering, operations, business, or a related field preferred; equivalent hands-on manufacturing experience will be considered
* Genuine comfort relocating to and leading in a small Southern community

**Nice to Have**

* Background in custom fabricated products such as signage, store fixtures, displays, architectural metals, or electrical closures
* Industrial engineering training or a similarly technical, process-focused background
* Experience in a private equity-backed or recently acquired manufacturing business
* Lean, Six Sigma, or similar continuous improvement experience applied in a practical, hands-on way
* Experience scaling production capacity, including adding shifts or growing output in a constrained labor market

**The Opportunity**
Our client is a private equity-backed national company that designs, builds, and installs branded products for well-known multi-site businesses across North America. This role leads their primary manufacturing facility in Southeast Alabama, a custom, build-to-order operation where a skilled team works hands-on with aluminum, steel, and electrical components, producing a wide variety of products in small lots.
 
 
The plant has made steady progress in recent years, with lower costs, better quality, and more reliable delivery. The next step is a strong, hands-on leader who can keep that momentum going and take the operation further. This is not a turnaround and not a maintenance role. It is a long-term opportunity to increase output, keep improving cost and efficiency, and build an operation that runs dependably every day.
 
 
**What You'll Do**

* Own plant performance: Lead every aspect of the facility, including safety, quality, throughput, delivery, and cost, with accountability for the plant P&L.
* Lead from the floor: Spend a good part of every day in production, getting to know the people, understanding what drives them, and building the trust that makes change stick.
* Find early wins: In the first 90 days, learn how the factory runs, stabilize performance, and identify practical process changes that make work easier for the people on the floor.
* Drive throughput and cost: Partner with the division President and finance leadership on a multi-year plan to increase output and reduce manufacturing cost, then deliver against it.
* Build repeatable systems: Put processes, metrics, and a leadership structure in place that let the plant run reliably without intensive oversight or dependence on any single person.
* Develop the team: Coach and grow the existing leadership group, including long-tenured leaders who know the product inside and out, and shape the structure the plant needs going forward.
* Hold the line on accountability: Understand the work well enough to see past excuses, set clear expectations, and follow through consistently.

**Why This Role Is Different**
This is the top leadership seat on site. The division President is based in another state, so this person will have real ownership and autonomy over how the plant runs, along with a leadership team that is invested in their success and has done this job before.
 
 
You will not be starting from scratch. The plant has a solid foundation, a clear direction, and the backing of a growing national platform and patient, long-term ownership. The opportunity is to take what has been built and make it better, with room to put your own mark on the operation.
 
 
**The Culture**
The plant has a loyal, tenured workforce that wants to do good work and takes pride in what it builds. The right person brings both process discipline and genuine people skills, someone who can hold the team to a high standard while building the relationships that earn real buy-in. Leadership is not looking for someone to shut things down and start over. They want a steady, visible leader who can find improvements while the work keeps moving, and who will feel at home in a close-knit, small-town Southern community.

records.title: Plant Manager I
records.description:
This position leads all plant operations for a70+ employee, 2 shift, manufacturing site. This leader ensures day-to-day operations are delivered with the aligned objectives of safety-first mindset, customer satisfaction along with growing and developing the leaders within the facility. This position also plays a critical role in developing and executing capital project plans for the facility to enable continuous improvement and growth in market share.

This full-time position reports directly to region General Manager and is located at Liberty Packaging’s manufacturing plant in Houston, Texas

**Duties And Responsibilities**

* Directly lead and supervise a team of direct reports to deliver major site functions across manufacturing, shipping, maintenance, and scheduling.
* Own end-to-end performance for the facility to meet KPIs in the areas of Safety, Quality, Cost, and Delivery. Establish, measure, and monitor performance across facility and root cause performance issues. Develop and deploy plans to drive improvements in manufacturing processes to ensure superior product quality, reduced cycle times, lead times, and minimize overall manufacturing costs.
* Provide day-to-day leadership for manufacturing team decision-making in the areas of production, labor, material costs, design, and production scheduling.
* In partnership with Continuous Improvement function, guide leaders and front-line staff through the identification and deployment of continuous improvement initiatives with an impact on key performance indicators.
* Ensure the right talent and capabilities are in place to meet strategic objectives; accountable for establishing goals, managing performance, and developing teams to ensure short- and long-range objectives are achieved
* Establish a two-way communication & engagement culture to ensure all plant employees are clear on plant performance and connection to business performance, including KPIs.
* Lead key change initiatives across the plant in partnership with regional and functional support systems (e.g., continuous improvement, engineering, human resources, sales, etc.)
* Lead the successful identification, business case design, and execution of capital projects in partnership with functional teams and executive leadership. Ensure multi-year capital plans support market growth and customer delivery
* Ensure employee relations stay connected with open and continuous dialogue
* Develop and grow community engagement presence by representing plant locally in key activities and through execution of frequent employee and community engagement activities
* Own direct P&L responsibility for plant site
* Provide leadership by connecting and being visible to all three shifts daily
* Other duties, as assigned

**Required Education, Experience And Skills**

* Bachelors’ degree and 7+ years manufacturing experience OR 10+ years manufacturing industry experience in lieu of education
* 5+ years people leadership experience
* Experience analyzing downtime, production, and financial variance trends, and identifying actions to deliver expected performance
* Previous experience developing and managing a budget, forecasting, and monitoring results
* Experience with identifying and executing capital projects to drive improvement against KPIs
* Demonstrated experience with organizational effectiveness, operations management, and a proven track record of achieving results
* Experience developing and presenting information to multiple levels of the organization from front-line to executive leadership
* Superior time management, attention to detail, verbal and written communication skills, decision-making, and organization skills
* Excellent computer skills required, including Microsoft Word and Excel skills.
* Demonstrated entrepreneurial spirit

**Preferred Education, Experience And Skills**

* Previous experience with Amtech / CTI or Kiwi
* Previous experience with ERP systems
* Previous experience in corrugated or paper manufacturing
* Lean and / or Continuous Improvement certifications
* Bilingual English / Spanish

**Compensation & Benefits**

The starting base salary range for this position is $110,078 - $137,598 per year plus eligibility in annual bonus program. The compensation posted is the anticipated pay for the position at the time of the posting. We may pay above or below posted amount based on several factors, including, but not limited to education and/or certifications, skills, experience, or work location. Some positions may qualify for additional compensation in the form of bonuses or deferred compensation options.

At LDI, we are pleased to provide employees with a comprehensive benefits package including health/dental/vision insurance options; paid time off; 10 paid holidays; 401(k) plus company matching and annual discretionary profit sharing; flexible spending and health savings account options; life and disability insurance; tuition assistance; wellness and mental health resources, and financial advising services. Eligibility in benefit programs is based on hours worked per week.

**Physical Requirements**

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

* Regular sitting, standing, and walking throughout the day to accomplish tasks
* Manual and finger dexterity used regularly with some repetitive finger motions
* Ability to work in front of a computer screen for long periods of time
* Specific vision abilities include close and distance vision; able to identify colors, small letters, and numbers; hand/eye coordination, depth perception and able to adjust focus
* Hearing and speaking
* Other conditions may include frequent reaching, stretching, pushing, pulling, pinching, grasping, and gripping.

**About Our Company**

Comprised of multiple companies with headquarters in New Hope, Minnesota, Liberty Diversified International (LDI) is a privately held company employing more than 1,900 individuals across our manufacturing facilities, production facilities and core business operations in Minnesota, Iowa, Nebraska, Illinois, Mississippi, Texas, Arizona, Virginia, California, and Mexico. With deep roots in the corrugated box manufacturing industry, we operate in the core markets of paper, packaging, workplace products, corrugated plastics and building products.

Since 1918, our values – Caring, Innovation, Trust and Excellence – have guided our day-to-day activities. We believe that when our employees are aligned with these values, we create superior service and solutions for our customers. The LDI family of companies includes Liberty Packaging, Liberty Paper, Liberty Plastics (Custom Solutions and Quarrix Building Products) and Safco.

Liberty Diversified International is an equal opportunity employer and makes all employment decisions without regard to race, color, sex, religion, age, creed, sexual orientation, national origin, marital status, disability, or any other protected class.

We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us.
